Upon submission of a summary report of the identified gaps in finance and business support

Expected to take place by 3rd week of engagement

- A written summary of key findings and analysis from stakeholder consultations, data analysis, and service mapping, identifying relevant themes and insights to inform the financing strategy.
- Submitted strategy for connecting entrepreneurs with potential funders

Expected to take place by 5th week of engagement

Upon DRC approval of the final report and actionable roadmap on new financial processes

To be submitted by the 8th Week of engagement.

**Eligibility Criteria**

For this assignment, the Consultant should have extensive experience and knowledge in strengthening systems for BDS/FSP in Kenya that supports refugees and vulnerable host communities’ initiatives.

Among the desirable qualifications for a lead consultant are:

- Master’s degree, or a bachelor's degree with over five years of substantial experience in Finance, Business, Development Economics, or related field
- The consultant should have a Minimum of 5 years of demonstrated experience working in enterprise development, MSME financing, or inclusive financial systems.
- Proven understanding of the innovation ecosystem in particular innovative alternative financing, challenge funds and accelerators.
- Completion Certificates for similar works from recognized and reputable institutions are an added advantage and/or provide at least 3 references of similar assignments s/he has successfully undertaken in the last 3 years.
- Demonstrated experience in small business development and management, experience with small business financing, market analysis, and market research.
- Strong networking capabilities, with the ability to build and maintain strategic partnerships.
- Proven ability to demonstrate innovative thinking and previous experience working in innovative alternative financing for SMEs and start-ups.
- Experience in designing or working with challenge funds.
- Substantive knowledge of community micro-entrepreneurs and alternative financing modalities to support refugee entrepreneurs.
- Cultural awareness and sensitivity and contextual knowledge of Entrepreneurship Development as a thematic area.
- Proven experience in professional report writing, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and insightful documentation.

**Conditions**

The engagement calls for adherence to the context security guidelines. On the same breadth, DRC does not guarantee security in relation to this engagement, and it will therefore not be liable for any eventuality. Nevertheless, any relevant security updates will be shared when necessary.

- The tasks must be completed within the stipulated time frame.
- This engagement is set to begin in October 2026 with assignment spreading within a period of 2 months. The operations must be within the agreed terms of engagement.
- The engagement calls for adherence to and signing of DRC’s Code of Conduct
- The offer for this engagement should be inclusive of all associated and agreed costs.
- For general information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit [www.drc.dk](https://www.drc.dk/).

**Reporting lines**

Reporting will be to the Project Manager with provision of regular updates to Economic Recovery Team Leader on the progress of the project as per the agreed-upon schedule.

For the duration of the engagement, progress update is expected on a weekly and monthly basis to the Project Manager.

**Travel**

The engagement necessitates the consultant to be based or travel to Turkana County during the exercise in understanding the context, markets and establishing possible linkages. As such, the consultant is responsible for making their own arrangements for transportation, accommodation, insurance, and meals, and should include these provisions in the Financial Proposal.

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
**1. Position Summary**

The Finance Manager has overall responsibility for managing and overseeing the day-to-day financial operations of Feed the Children in the Philippines. The position provides financial leadership, technical guidance and oversight of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, treasury and cash management, payroll reconciliations, procurement-related financial controls, audit and risk management, and statutory compliance. The role ensures that financial transactions are accurate, appropriately authorised, adequately supported by documentation and recorded in a timely manner. It also ensures that bank accounts, balance sheet accounts, payroll, budgets and expenditure are regularly reconciled and monitored, with discrepancies investigated and resolved promptly. The Finance Manager oversees the preparation and submission of monthly financial reports, budget-versus-actual (BVA) reports, accrual schedules, balance sheet reconciliations, cash forecasts and other required financial information. The position works closely with the Country Director, programme teams, Administration, Human Resources, Procurement and the International Office to ensure resources are appropriately managed, financial risks are mitigated, and management decisions are supported by reliable financial information. The role provides functional leadership to the Finance team and ensures that financial procedures, internal controls and reporting requirements are consistently applied across the Country Office.

**2. Essential Accountabilities**

**Financial Management and Accounting:**

- Oversee day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accurate, complete and timely recording of all financial transactions.
- Ensure compliance with Feed the Children financial policies, accounting procedures, donor requirements, applicable Philippine laws and regulations, and relevant accounting standards.
- Review monthly financial reports, general ledger transactions and expenditure records to identify errors, mispostings, unusual transactions, coding inaccuracies and potential compliance concerns.
- Monitor shared cost allocations, advances, receivables, payables and other balances
- Investigate abnormal or unexplained transactions and ensure corrective action.

**Audit and Risk Management:**

- Maintain and update the financial risk tracker, tracking risks, mitigation actions and progress against agreed actions.
- Identify financial, operational, compliance and control risks and recommend preventive and corrective measures.
- Ensure effective internal financial controls, segregation of duties and policy compliance.
- Coordinate audits, donor reviews and compliance assessments.
- Monitor implementation of audit recommendations and escalate irregularities, fraud risks or policy violations.

**Reconciliations and Financial Control:**

- Oversee payroll, bank, and balance sheet reconciliations, ensuring accuracy, documentation, and timely resolution of reconciling items.
- Monitor suspense accounts, advances, and inter-account balances, investigating abnormal transactions and ensuring compliance with reporting schedules and delegated authority.

**Procurement Oversight and Payment Pack Compliance:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Cash and Treasury Management:**

- Review procurement transactions and payment packs for compliance with policies, approval thresholds, budget availability, and delegated authority.
- Verify supporting documentation, contract compliance, coding accuracy, receipt of goods/services, and budget availability before payment processing.
- Monitor procurement commitments and supplier payments, maintain audit trails in SharePoint, and escalate procurement irregularities while providing financial compliance guidance.

**Financial Reporting & Month-End Close:**

- Ensure timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and month-end close processes.
- Maintain accrual schedules, reconcile financial records, review balance sheet accounts, and ensure proper accounting for depreciation, prepayments, and deposits.
- Prepare financial dashboards, shared-cost reports, and budget-versus-actual (BVA) analyses, presenting key variances and recommendations to management.
- Ensure all supporting documentation is uploaded to SharePoint and reports are submitted according to established timelines.

**Payroll & Statutory Compliance:**

- Oversee payroll reconciliations, payroll cost allocations, statutory deductions, and payroll-related liabilities.
- Coordinate with HR to ensure payroll accuracy, compliance, timely payments, and secure maintenance of payroll records.

**Taxation & Regulatory Compliance:**

- Ensure accurate recording, reconciliation, filing, and payment of taxes and statutory obligations.
- Oversee BIR Form 2307 compliance, maintain supporting tax documentation, monitor deadlines, and liaise with tax authorities and advisers as required.
- Escalate compliance risks, penalties, or regulatory changes impacting operations.

**Budgeting & Financial Planning:**

- Review and consolidate departmental and project budgets, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and funding requirements.
- Monitor budget utilization, analyze variances, support forecasts, revisions, and realignments, and identify funding gaps, restrictions, overspending, or underutilization.
- Provide financial analysis to support decision-making and cash-flow planning.

**Financial Systems & Records Management:**

- Ensure accurate transaction recording and reconciliation within QuickBooks Online and other approved systems.
- Maintain complete, accurate, and accessible financial records, payment packs, reconciliations, and supporting documentation in SharePoint.
- Safeguard confidential financial information and support continuous improvement of systems, reporting processes, and internal controls.

**Team Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement:**

- Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and technical guidance to Finance staff, ensuring accountability and high-quality outputs.
- Foster understanding of financial procedures, controls, and compliance requirements across the team.
- Collaborate with HR, Procurement, Administration, Programme teams, and International Office stakeholders to support reporting, audits, cash management, compliance, and organizational objectives.
- Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and sound financial stewardship.

**3. Key Performance Expectations:**

**The following deliverables will be monitored through agreed performance indicators and the organisational reporting calendar.**

- **Risk Tracker and Internal Controls**
- **Frequency:** Updated and reviewed daily, with material risks escalated promptly.
- **Internal and External Audit Support**
- **Frequency:** As required, with audit recommendations tracked through to closure.
- **Bank Reconciliations (Eight Accounts)**
- **Frequency:** Daily monitoring, with formal reconciliation and approval in accordance with the financial close calendar.
- **Balance Sheet Reconciliations**
- **Frequency:** As per the reconciliation schedule, with prompt follow-up on abnormal or outstanding items.
- **Bank Statements Against QuickBooks Online (QBO)**
- **Frequency:** Daily.
- **Accruals, Journal Entries, Depreciation, Deposits and Prepayments**
- **Frequency:** As transactions arise and during the month-end close process.
- **Payroll Reconciliations and Payroll Tax Checks**
- **Frequency:** Monthly and in accordance with statutory deadlines.
- **Procurement Transactions and Payment Packs**
- **Frequency:** Reviewed as submitted, with daily monitoring of outstanding payments.
- **Monthly Wire/Fund Transfer Requests**
- **Deadline:** By the International Office's prescribed deadline.
- **Cash and Bank Balances**
- **Frequency:** Monitored daily, with funding requirements identified promptly.
- **Budget Versus Actual (BVA) Reporting and Budget Utilisation**
- **Frequency:** Monthly, with BVA reports presented to the Country Office team.
- **Budget Requests and Forecasts**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with the established budgeting calendar.
- **Month-End Reports and Checklist**
- **Deadline:** By the 10th day of each month.
- **Financial Documentation and SharePoint Uploads**
- **Frequency:** As financial transactions are processed.
- **BIR Form 2307**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with applicable statutory requirements.
- **International Office Financial Reporting**
- **Deadline:** In accordance with prescribed International Office reporting deadlines.

**4. Qualifications and Experience:**

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Competencies**

- Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial management, financial reporting and internal controls.
- Experience in budgeting, cash-flow management, bank reconciliations, balance sheet reconciliations and financial analysis.
- Knowledge of procurement-related financial controls, payment verification and supporting documentation requirements.
- Understanding of payroll accounting, statutory deductions, taxation and applicable Philippine financial compliance requirements.
- Experience in audit coordination, financial risk management and implementation of audit recommendations. • Proficiency in accounting systems, preferably QuickBooks Online, and advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
- Ability to analyse financial data, investigate discrepancies and prepare accurate financial reports and management information.
- Strong planning, organisation, communication, problem-solving and deadline-management skills.
- Ability to communicate financial information to non-finance colleagues and collaborate across departments.
- Integrity, confidentiality, attention to detail, leadership and commitment to strengthening financial controls.

**5. Leadership Competencies:**

- **Accountability:** Takes responsibility for decisions, manages resources efficiently and holds self and others accountable.
- **Integrity and Ethical Judgement:** Demonstrates honesty, transparency, confidentiality and sound ethical decision-making.
- **Analytical Judgement:** Investigates discrepancies, assesses financial risks and uses evidence to recommend corrective action.
- **Collaboration:** Builds effective relationships across Finance, HR, Procurement, Administration, Programme teams and the International Office.
- **Team Leadership:** Develops staff capability, sets clear expectations and promotes quality and timely delivery.
- **Continuous Improvement:** Identifies opportunities to improve processes, documentation, reporting and internal controls.

**6. Other Role Requirements:**

- Primary location: Philippines Country Office in Cebu.
- Travel: As required for country operations.
- Other responsibilities: The employee may be assigned other job-related duties that are reasonable and consistent with the position's level, purpose and experience requirements.

**7. Standard Organisational Policy Statements:**

**Safeguarding and Child Protection**

Feed the Children is committed to preventing exploitation, abuse, harassment, child abuse and neglect and to responding promptly and appropriately to concerns. Employees must maintain high ethical standards, protect organisational integrity and comply with Feed the Children’s safeguarding, child protection and related policies and protocols. Violations may result in corrective action, up to and including termination of employment.

**Standards of Conduct:**

Employees are expected to act honestly, fairly and respectfully and in alignment with Feed the Children’s values and Standards of Conduct. These standards guide acceptable workplace behaviour and may form the basis for corrective or disciplinary action when violated.

**Commitment to Gender, Diversity and Inclusion:**

Feed the Children is committed to a diverse, inclusive, respectful and safe work environment in which all individuals are treated fairly and with dignity. Feed the Children prohibits discrimination, harassment, retaliation and workplace bullying and promotes equitable participation and opportunity across its workforce and operations.

**8. Review and Approval:**

This job description identifies the position’s principal purpose, accountabilities, authority and requirements. It is not all-inclusive and may be updated as organisational needs evolve. Annual objectives and performance measures are established separately through the performance planning process.

jobs.title: Request for Proposal AASHA Program County Consultants Kwale, Narok and Migori Counties
jobs.description:
## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media that girls want, trust and need. From chatbots to chat shows and TV dramas to tech, our content helps adolescent girls in Africa and Asia make life choices and changes.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, and relationships, empowering girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible “for a girl”.

Our reach is 50 million and counting. And we’re using technology to reach girls at scale so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and her livelihood.

Because when a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country.

That’s the Girl Effect.

## **Background**

AASHA, the Age-Appropriate Sexual Health Approach, is implemented by Girl Effect in partnership with Kenya’s Ministry of Health. It seeks to improve access to age-appropriate sexual and reproductive health information and support for adolescents and young people aged 10–24 and contribute to reducing teenage pregnancy.

The programme works with national, county and community stakeholders. County delivery includes government and partner coordination, community and youth engagement, training and mobilisation, human-centred design activities, safeguarding and consent processes, data collection and programme learning.

Girl Effect seeks county-based individual consultants to coordinate and support these activities in Kwale, Narok and Migori counties.

## **Objective of the consultancy**

The consultant will serve as Girl Effect’s principal community-engagement and county-implementation focal point for AASHA in the assigned county.

The consultant will translate approved plans into safe, timely and well-documented delivery; strengthen government, partner and community coordination; support community champions and youth mobilisers; and provide reliable implementation information and learning to Girl Effect.

## **What You’ll Do**

The selected consultant will be responsible for the following tasks:

### **1. Project Implementation and Coordination**

- Serve as the main local liaison for Girl Effect in the County, and collaborate with local implementing partners and County Government teams to implement AASHA activities.
- Collaborate with the County Health Management Team to organize and facilitate community activities through community-owned resource persons, e.g. champions, child protection volunteers, community health promoters, etc and programme ecosystems, e.g. schools, health facilities, administrative units.
- Support planning and execution of training, community sessions, events, monitoring visits, and surveys/assessments.
- Support County in supervision and adaptation of tools and job aids, gather session feedback and share insights with the relevant project team(s) to inform continuous learning.
- Coordinate and co-facilitate training workshops building facilitation, mobilization, safeguarding, digital tool use and health messaging skills.

### **4. Government and Partner Engagement**

- Serve as the link between Girl Effect and county/sub-county offices (Child Protection, GBV, Health, Local Administration) as applicable
- Support and participate in TWGs (SRH, ACSM, M&E and Resource Mobilization) and Stakeholder meetings.
- Support rollout of SRH campaigns in the county, aligning with official reporting, referral and health service delivery structures.
- Facilitate collaboration between government ministries to implement AASHA activities to strengthen protection, reporting and priority behaviour uptake.

### **5. Monitoring, Learning, and Reporting**

- Document attendance, feedback, key discussion points, health service referrals and champions'/mobilisers' performance, by programme.
- Organize AASHA performance review meetings.
- Submit timely reports, work plans, and recommendations to the relevant programme team.
- Support Girl Effect’s Evidence & Insights team with data collection, ensuring community buy-in and data quality, including consent processes where research activities are involved.
- Capture stories of change and lessons learned for donor and partner reporting.

### **6. Flexible Surge Support**

- Be available for additional tasks such as extra training, launch events, urgent dialogues, troubleshooting or media rollouts to ensure responsiveness to evolving community needs.

## **Deliverables**

- **County Work Plan:** Detailed implementation plan, outlining how CHPs/facilitators, schools, parents and adolescents will be engaged in the counties.
- **Training/Meeting Reports:** Attendance sheets, training materials and post-training summaries for all champion and stakeholder training sessions.
- **Discussion Session Reports:** Session attendance, discussion summaries, feedback forms, and photo documentation (where appropriate).
- **Government Engagement Log:** Record of meetings, agreements and joint activities with the county's relevant government offices.
- **Monthly Report:** Comprehensive report summarizing activities, insights, challenges, outcomes and recommendations for scale-up.
- **Ad-hoc Deliverables:** Any additional reports or updates required to respond to emerging needs or opportunities during implementation.

## **Duration, Location and Level of Effort**

The consultancy is expected to run from November 2026 to September 2027, subject to contracting and programme requirements.

The consultant must be based in, or able to maintain a regular field presence in, the selected county.

This is a high-level-of-effort consultancy requiring consistent availability during agreed implementation periods. The consultant will manage their time against approved work plans, deliverables and an agreed monthly level of effort. The consultancy does not create an employment relationship or fixed working hours.

Travel within the assigned county will be required. Travel outside the county, exceptional activities or additional support must be requested in writing and delivered within the agreed level of effort or separately approved before the work begins.

## **Management and Working Arrangements**

The consultant will report to the designated Programme Manager and work closely with the Programme Lead and relevant Girl Effect teams, including:

- Programmes;
- Evidence and Insights;
- Safeguarding;
- Finance and Operations; and
- Communications and Digital Delivery.

Materials and reports will be prepared in English unless otherwise agreed. Girl Effect will provide programme guidance, approved tools and consolidated feedback through the designated focal point.

## **Who You Are**

## **Qualifications**

- Proven experience in communications, public relations, or a related field.
- Proven experience coordinating community-based projects focused on SRH, MNH, GBV, FGM, child marriage prevention, or similar social issues
- Strong background in community mobilization, facilitation, and stakeholder relationship management.
- Demonstrated experience working with county government structures and departments.
- Knowledge of participatory training methods and experience delivering capacity-building workshops.
- Skilled in documentation, basic reporting, and feedback collection.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse community groups and adolescents.
- Commitment to safeguarding, gender equality, and child protection principles.
- Strong cultural awareness and sensitivity about the cultures within the counties.
- Excellent written and spoken English and Swahili.
- Commitment to realizing girls' potential and to the Girl Effect's vision and values.
- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences and related fields.
- 3+ years of experience.

## **Proposal Submission**

Applicants should submit a concise technical proposal of no more than five pages together with a separate financial proposal.

The application should include:

- A cover letter stating the county applied for, current location, availability and suitability for the assignment.
- A technical approach covering county coordination, community and youth engagement, government and partner engagement, champion support, safeguarding, monitoring and reporting.
- A proposed plan for the first 30 days and an approach to managing delivery risks.
- A current CV highlighting relevant assignments and county-level experience.
- Three professional references, including name, organisation, position, email address and telephone number.
- A separate financial proposal in Kenya shillings **(KES)** showing:
- The proposed all-inclusive monthly professional fee;
- The underlying daily rate or estimated level of effort;
- Applicable taxes shown separately.

## **Evaluation Criteria**

Proposals will be evaluated in the following order:

- Pre-screening;
- Technical evaluation; and
- Financial evaluation.

Girl Effect may establish a minimum technical score that applicants must achieve before their financial proposals are considered.

- Relevant qualifications and community engagement experience: 15%
- Experience in adolescent and youth health, SRH or related community programmes: 15%
- County knowledge, government engagement and multi-stakeholder coordination experience: 15%
- Quality and practicality of the proposed technical approach: 15%
- Safeguarding, monitoring, reporting and risk-management capability: 10%
- Value for money and clarity of the financial proposal: 30%

Girl Effect may request interviews, written clarifications, reference checks or a best-and-final financial proposal. The lowest-priced application will not necessarily be selected.

## **Procurement Timelines**

- Terms of reference published: 15th October, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: **26th October 2026**

## **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful consultant will sign Girl Effect’s standard consultancy agreement. Payment will be linked to the satisfactory delivery and approval of agreed outputs and supporting documentation.
- **Pricing, Taxes and Expenses:** Fees must be quoted in Kenya shillings, with applicable taxes shown separately. Girl Effect will deduct taxes where required by law. Only reasonable expenses approved in writing in advance will be reimbursable in accordance with the final agreement.
- **Confidentiality, Data and Intellectual Property:** The consultant must protect all confidential, personal and sensitive information. Deliverables and materials produced under the consultancy will be governed by Girl Effect’s intellectual property, confidentiality, and data protection provisions.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct**: Appointment is subject to satisfactory due diligence, reference and safeguarding checks. The consultant must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical, anti-fraud, information-security and code-of-conduct requirements.
- **Conflicts of Interest**: Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest.
- **Equal Opportunity:** Girl Effect welcomes applications from qualified individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourages candidates based in or with strong working knowledge of Nairobi County.
- **Right to Award**: Girl Effect may seek clarification, interview or negotiate with applicants, amend or cancel the process, reject any or all proposals, or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for costs incurred in preparing an application.
- **Proposal Validity**: Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Request for Proposal (RFP) On-Call IT Support Services October, 2026 India
jobs.description:
## **Request for Proposal (RFP) On-Call IT Support Services**

## **October, 2026**

**India**

## **Procurement Summary**

**Item Details**

RFP Title On-Call IT Support Services – India

Eligible Applicants India-based individual consultants and registered IT support agencies/firms

Location Remote support across India, with in-person coordination where required

Contract Period 12 months, with possible renewal subject to satisfactory performance and organisational need

Reporting To Senior IT & System Manager and India People and Operations Manager

RFP Issue Date 16th October 2026

Proposal Deadline 30th October 2026

Submission Email suppliers@girleffect.org

## **Who We Are**

Girl Effect is an international non-profit that builds media and technology that girls want, trust and need. We use evidence-based social and behaviour change approaches to help adolescent girls make informed choices about their health, education and economic future.

In India, Girl Effect’s digital-first youth programme, Chhaa Jaa, reaches girls through social media, digital content, community spaces and interactive products, including Bol Behen. Reliable IT support is essential to the teams delivering this work.

## **Background**

Girl Effect India has approximately 28 staff working across locations including New Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Pune, Nagpur, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Noida, Gurugram and Jaipur.

Girl Effect requires dependable on-call IT support to resolve hardware and software issues, coordinate repairs and warranties, and assist with approved IT sourcing.

## **Objective**

The objective of this engagement is to maintain reliable day-to-day IT operations by providing responsive remote support, timely issue resolution, and effective coordination of repairs, warranties, and approved equipment purchases across India.

### **What You will do**

The selected service provider will be responsible for:

- Providing remote, on-call IT support to approximately 28 users across India between 10:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m., Monday to Friday.
- Diagnose and resolve laptop, peripheral, operating-system, application, and connectivity issues within agreed service levels.
- Support IT setup and onboarding for new employees, including device configuration and troubleshooting access.
- Coordinating OEM warranty claims, repairs, and replacements, including clear communication on status, cost, and expected completion time.
- Supporting the sourcing of approved IT requirements, such as laptops and accessories, by providing specifications, availability, and quotations where requested.
- Providing access to capable support personnel and service coverage in major Indian cities, either directly or through an established support network.
- Protecting Girl Effect data, credentials and systems and complying with applicable security, confidentiality and data-protection requirements.

### **Service levels and Deliverables**

**Requirement Standard Evidence Frequency**

Support availability 10:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., Monday–Friday Ticket or support log Ongoing

Initial diagnosis for a received deviceWithin 24 hours of receiving the device Diagnosis or update provided to the

user Per incident

Issue resolution Within three working days unless parts or

OEM action are unavailable Closure note or agreed action plan Per incident

Warranty and

repair coordination Prompt escalation and regular

status updates OEM or repair record As required

Monthly service report Incidents logged, resolved and pending; response

and resolution performance; recurring issues Approved monthly report Monthly

Where a delay is outside the service provider’s control, the provider must explain the cause, expected resolution date and any practical workaround.

Any additional costs for parts, travel, call-outs or extended services must receive Girl Effect’s prior written approval.

### **Girl Effect Responsibilities**

- Girl Effect will:
- Maintain the required device licences and antivirus protection.
- Provide reasonable access to staff, devices and relevant information needed to diagnose issues.
- Approve additional costs for parts, travel or services before they are incurred.
- Nominate the contract supervisors and provide timely feedback on service quality.

#### **Reporting**

The agency will work closely with the Senior IT & Systems Manager and the People and Ops Manager in India

#### **Expected Commitment**

- The assignment is expected to take approximately 1 year. Effective Period: November 2026 - November 2027. This is subject to renewal upon satisfactory delivery of the work.
- The consultant will be expected to present to the team if needed.

## **Applicant Requirements**

Applications are welcome from both qualified individual consultants and registered IT support agencies or firms. Applicants must be based in India and demonstrate:

- Relevant experience providing remote and on-call IT support to distributed teams or organisations of comparable size.
- Strong knowledge of laptop hardware, operating systems, productivity applications, endpoint security, connectivity and user support.
- Capacity to meet the stated support window and service levels and coordinate support in major Indian cities.
- Experience working with OEM warranty, repair, and replacement processes.
- Clear communication, accurate documentation, and appropriate confidentiality and data-security practices.
- At least two contactable references for similar assignments.

Individual applicants should submit a current CV.

Agencies or firms should submit a brief company profile and CVs or profiles of the personnel who would deliver the services.

### **Proposal Submission Requirements**

Applicants should submit a concise proposal of no more than five pages, covering the following:

- **Understanding and Approach**
Explain how you will provide support, manage incidents, communicate with users, and meet the required service levels.
- **Experience and Capacity**
Provide details of relevant assignments, geographic coverage, and the proposed individual or team responsible for delivering the services.
- **References**
Provide contact details for at least two clients for whom you have undertaken similar work.
- **Financial Proposal**
Provide fees in **INR,** with applicable taxes quoted separately. The financial proposal should clearly state:
- Proposed monthly retainer or fixed fee.
- Hourly or daily rates, where applicable.
- Call-out or on-site support charges.
- Travel or logistics charges.
- Any other costs that may apply.
- Items, replacement parts, and third-party costs that are excluded from the proposed fee.

### **Evaluation Process and Criteria**

Proposals will be reviewed in the following sequence:

1. Prescreening against the mandatory requirements.
2. Technical evaluation.
3. Financial and value-for-money evaluation.

Only substantially responsive proposals that meet the required technical standard will proceed to financial evaluation.

**Evaluation Criterion Weight**

Understanding of the requirement and proposed support approach 15%

Relevant IT support experience 25%

Geographic coverage, availability and ability to meet the SLA 20%

Qualifications, team capacity and references 10%

**Technical Total 70%**

Financial proposal and value for money 30%

**Total 100%**

Girl Effect may invite shortlisted applicants to an interview or clarification meeting and may conduct reference checks and due diligence before making an award.

### **Performance Measures**

Performance will be assessed against:

- Response and resolution times under the agreed service levels.
- Quality and accuracy of incident records and monthly reports.
- User satisfaction and effectiveness of communication.
- Timely coordination of repairs, warranties and approved sourcing requests.
- Compliance with Girl Effect’s data-security, confidentiality and safeguarding requirements.

### **Project Timelines**

- Terms of reference published:16th October, 2026
- Deadline for proposal submission: 30th October 2026

**On-Call IT Support Services – India**

Only submissions received through the stated application process and email address will be considered.

### **General and Commercial Terms**

- **Contracting and Payment:** The successful applicant will enter into Girl Effect’s applicable agreement. Payment will be linked to satisfactory delivery of the agreed services and receipt of a correct, approved invoice.
- **Pricing and Taxes:** Fees must be firm for the stated proposal validity period and clearly show the currency, applicable taxes and any separately chargeable costs. Girl Effect will deduct or account for taxes where required by law.
- **Additional Costs:** Replacement parts, travel, third-party services and other additional costs will only be reimbursable where agreed and approved in writing by Girl Effect before the costs are incurred.
- **Confidentiality and Data Protection:** The selected provider must protect Girl Effect information, systems, credentials and any personal, confidential or sensitive information accessed during the engagement.
- **Safeguarding and Conduct:** The selected provider must comply with Girl Effect’s safeguarding, ethical and supplier-conduct requirements and may be subject to appropriate due-diligence checks.
- **Conflicts of Interest:** Applicants must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest that could affect the procurement process or delivery of the services.
- **Right to Award:** Girl Effect may seek clarification, negotiate, amend or cancel the procurement process, reject any or all submissions, or make no award. Girl Effect is not liable for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a proposal.
- **Proposal Validity:** Proposals must remain valid for 90 days from the submission deadline.

jobs.title: Recruitment Agency Services
jobs.description:
**Terms of Reference: Recruitment Agency Services**

**1. Background**

Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) is establishing a regional Investigation & Compliance Support Team based in Nairobi, Kenya. To support the recruitment of qualified professionals for this function, NCA seeks to engage an experienced recruitment agency registered in Kenya to manage the recruitment process.

**2. Key responsibilities**

- Review NCA's job descriptions and agree on the recruitment process, workplan, and timetable.
- Advertise the vacancies and conduct targeted search in Kenya.
- Screen applications, verify eligibility and qualifications, conduct first-round interviews, administer agreed assessments and conduct second-round interviews together with NCA.
- Provide a ranked shortlist with brief candidate assessments.
- Coordinate candidate communication and interview logistics with NCA, and conduct reference and qualification checks.
- Submit final recruitment recommendations and support communication with selected candidates, as requested.

**3.General information**

**Name**:*External recruitment company-To be completed.*

**Title**: Recruitment Agency Services for the Investigation & Compliance Support Team

**Reporting to**:NCA’s designated HR and Finance representatives

**Office location**: Nairobi, Kenya

**Time frame:** The recruitment timetable will be agreed with the selected agency upon contract signature.

**4.Scope of services and deliverables:**

**Objective**

Identify, assess, and support the recruitment of qualified candidates for NCA’s Nairobi-based Investigation & Compliance Support Team.

**Positions to be recruited**

One Senior Investigator and one Investigator / Compliance Officer.

**Required candidate profile**

Candidates must meet the qualifications, experience, competencies, language requirements, and travel expectations specified in the approved job description for each position. Relevant experience may include investigations, compliance, audit, risk, governance, legal, or finance functions, preferably within NGOs, humanitarian organizations, or international organizations.

Detailed job descriptions will be provided to the selected agency upon contract signature.

**Deliverables**

- Agreed recruitment strategy and timeline
- Vacancy advertisements
- Ranked shortlist with candidate assessment summaries
- Reference and qualification check reports
- Final recruitment recommendation report

**5.Requirements for the recruitment agency:**

**Agency requirements**

The provider must be legally registered to operate in Kenya and demonstrate relevant recruitment experience. The provider must understand the Kenyan and East African labor markets and have a proven track record of recruiting professionals in investigations, compliance, audit, finance, legal, governance, or related fields, preferably for NGOs or international organizations.

**6**.**Proposal requirements**

The proposal should include a company profile, relevant experience, proposed methodology, workplan and timetable, proposed team, financial proposal, references from comparable assignments, and details of any guarantee or candidate replacement arrangements offered by the agency.

**Proposals should be evaluated based on**

**Relevant experience** of the firm conducting comparable recruitment assignments, particularly for investigations, compliance, audit, legal, finance, governance, NGO, or international organization positions.(40%)

**Understanding of the assignment** and quality of the proposed recruitment approach.(30%)

**Capacity and qualifications** of the proposed recruitment team.(20%)

**References** from comparable assignments, demonstrating successful delivery of recruitment services(10%)

**Total Technical Score:100**

Proposals will be evaluated using a combined technical and financial scoring method. The technical proposal will account for 80% of the total score, while the financial proposal will account for 20% of the total score.

**7.Success factors/risks and restraints**

**Success factors:** A timely and transparent recruitment process, a strong candidate pool, effective candidate communication, and qualified final candidates.

**Risks and restraints:** Limited availability of qualified candidates, candidate withdrawal, delays in the recruitment process. The agency must maintain confidentiality and disclose any conflicts of interest.

**8.Reporting**

The recruitment agency will report to the designated NCA representatives listed above, provide regular progress updates, and ensure that all information and deliverables are managed securely and confidentially.

jobs.title: East Africa Programme Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** East Africa Programme Officer
**Reports To:** Africa Regional Manager
**Status:** Full-Time
**Direct Reports:** Interns/volunteers, where relevant. (At present, this role doesn’t have direct reports)
**Contract duration:** Two years (with the possibility of extension depending on funding)
**Compensation:** ETB 2,093,000–2,898,000 annually
**Location:** This post is based in Addis Abba, Ethiopia. Please note that IDC is unable to support relocation and the postholder needs to have the ability to work in Ethiopia.

**Background**

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network, of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, that coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention.

**Role Purpose**

We are seeking a highly organized and motivated individual with a solid background in advocacy on migration and human rights. The ideal candidate will coordinate projects, initiatives and events efficiently, contribute to strategic advocacy efforts and support the development of the capacity of IDC members. Strong communications, organizational, planning, and stakeholder engagement skills are essential.

**Role Summary**

The Africa Programme Officer will play a key role in supporting IDC’s mission in the region by combining strong organizational and coordination skills with a solid understanding of advocacy on migration and human rights. Working closely with the Africa Regional Manager and other team members, the Programme Officer will contribute to the design and implementation of regional programs, events, initiatives and advocacy strategies. The role involves providing operational, administrative, research, and communications support, as well as helping to strengthen networks with members, partners, decision makers and other key stakeholders across the Africa region and specifically in Eastern Africa. The Programme Officer should be available to travel within the region as needed.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Project implementation, admin support and support to IDC members and partners**

- Contribute to the implementation of national and regional projects and events by providing technical, administrative, and logistical support to the Africa Regional Programme and in collaboration with relevant IDC staff and members
- Support the overall implementation of IDC’s mission and strategic priorities in the Africa region (with a priority focus on Easter Africa) through a balance of operational efficiency and advocacy engagement.
- Support IDC’s members in the region and support in network building.
- Maintain a high level of organization in managing project timelines, deliverables, and follow-ups in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members.
- Support administrative processes related with finances in the Africa Programme.

**Advocacy and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Support the development and implementation of advocacy strategies related to immigration detention, alternatives to detention, and broader migrant and refugee rights.
- Engage effectively and in coordination with the Africa Regional Manager and other relevant team members with a wide range of stakeholders, including government representatives, civil society actors, UN agencies, and regional networks, to build partnerships and advance shared objectives.
- Contribute to drafting and disseminating advocacy materials, briefing notes, and strategic communications tailored to diverse audiences across the Africa region.
- Maintain regular contact with IDC members and partners to identify policy gaps, advocacy opportunities, and spaces for support, partnership and coordinated action.
- Assist in the planning and facilitation of stakeholder consultations, trainings, and regional events that promote rights-based alternatives, pathways and regional dialogue.

**Communication**

- Assist with developing print and digital communication materials for the region, including social media material for different platforms.
- Disseminate and share resources among members and other stakeholders through different platforms.
- Contribute to monitoring media platforms and keep track of reports and updates on relevant developments in the region.

**Internal Systems, Monitoring, Fundraising, and Institutional Support**

- Actively contribute to IDC’s fundraising efforts by providing background research, identifying potential funders, coordinating inputs, and play an active role in the drafting of proposals aligned with regional priorities
- Ensure accurate and timely monitoring and reporting of programmatic activities, supporting internal evaluation processes and donor accountability in line with IDC’s MEL systems.
- Maintain organized records of project outcomes, stakeholder engagement, and communications to support institutional memory and knowledge sharing.
- Assist in the preparation of high-quality reports, updates, and documentation for internal use, funders, and external dissemination.
- Support budget tracking, planning, and financial monitoring processes in collaboration with the Regional Manager, Executive Director, and relevant IDC staff.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of collaboration, teamwork, and support within the IDC team.
- Demonstrate a passion for and alignment with the IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, representation and being solutions-focused
- Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies including IDC Children and Vulnerable Adults Safeguarding policy to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
- Actively engage with organisational systems, processes, and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time

**Key Selection Criteria**

**Essential Criteria**

- Demonstrated understanding of the Africa contexts, particularly related to migration, human rights, and advocacy.
- A university degree in a relevant field such as international relations, law, migration studies, political science, or social sciences.
- A minimum of five years of professional experience, including project coordination, stakeholder engagement, and advocacy in the migration and/or human rights sectors.
- Proven experience in reporting and follow-up, including contributions to monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes and reporting experience.
- Strong communication, writing, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and work independently in a remote setting.
- Experience engaging effectively with diverse stakeholders, including civil society, government actors, and international organizations, to advance advocacy and collaboration.
- Demonstrated ability to plan, organize, and facilitate events such as meetings, workshops, and advocacy activities.
- Excellent organizational and coordination including good attention to detail. The ability to take initiative and to work remotely and autonomously, to manage competing deadlines, prioritise workload appropriately and work in a flexible manner. Proficiency in using digital communication tools and platforms, including social media.
- Ability to undertake travel in the region for the role
- Residing in Ethiopia with the legal right to work.
- Fluency in both English and Amharic (written and spoken) is mandatory. Fluency in Somali and/or Arabic is an added advantage.
- Strong commitment to IDC’s mission and values, including its safeguarding and child protection principles.

jobs.title: 22867 Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) (P)
jobs.description:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) – the United Nations (UN) migration agency – in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) implements a broad, integrated programme supporting crisis‑affected populations and national institutions in a context of protracted conflict, large‑scale displacement, and limited access to essential services. The programme combines humanitarian assistance, stabilization, durable solutions, peacebuilding, migration governance, and border management interventions across multiple provinces, targeting Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, host communities, ex‑combatants, vulnerable households, and government counterparts. Core activities include community‑based planning, rehabilitation of key infrastructure, livelihood and reintegration support, social cohesion initiatives, displacement tracking, protection services, and capacity building for national and local authorities. Through these efforts, IOM aims to strengthen resilience, restore basic services, enhance local governance, and advance sustainable solutions for displacement‑affected communities.

Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director of the Regional Office (RO) for East Horn and Southern Africa (EHSA) and direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and in close coordination with the Regional Thematic Specialist (RTS) and relevant Divisions/Departments/Units at Headquarters, the Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will provide strategic leadership and oversight across the Country Office’s (CO) programme portfolio. This includes guiding programme development and implementation, leading strategic planning processes, strengthening donor and government engagement, ensuring coherence with One UN frameworks, overseeing programme support functions, and maintaining high‑level coordination with national authorities, UN agencies, partners, and stakeholders. The Senior Programme Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery) will also ensure integrated planning, quality assurance, knowledge management, and effective representation of IOM in inter‑agency fora, while supporting the COM in advancing the CO’s priorities and institutional objectives.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee the overall development, implementation, and monitoring of programme activities under areas of responsibility, including oversight of IOM’s cluster participation and ONE UN obligations. Identify potential and existing obstacles to programme delivery through continuous monitoring of new programme areas that reflect changes in host country and donor priorities.
2. Develop the CO’s programme overview, including all (or thematically relevant) programmes implemented by the CO, and schedule the major activities for the COM.
3. Lead the development of country strategic plans, which are in line with IOM’s global & regional strategies, the Country National Peace & Development Strategy, and the One UN Programme.
4. Lead the development of the CO’s donor and partner outreach strategies, taking into account priorities in DRC, Humanitarian Response and Recovery, and IOM’s regional and global strategic priorities and objectives; implement the strategies in close coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units.
5. Develop and maintain Government working relationships with the ministries and international agencies involved in migration-related issues in DRC, and maintain regular liaison with key government officials and interlocutors. Serve as overall Focal Point for Humanitarian Response and Recovery.
6. In coordination with the COM and CO’s relevant units, establish liaison and maintain continuous dialogue with relevant stakeholders (i.e., national governmental authorities, donors, UN Agencies, national and international Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), national and international institutions, Private sector) aiming at coordinating and facilitating the implementation of ongoing activities and promoting new activities and fundraising for new projects; identify synergies with IOM’s programmes and make recommendations on donor/partner engagement.
7. Lead the Programme Support Unit and supervise the Unit’s staff providing project development, public information, reporting, donor relations, government liaison and information management functions for the CO.
8. Ensure an integrated approach to CO’s programming, with required support functions such as project development, reporting, donor relations, public information and information management are provided to programme units in a timely manner.
9. Provide overall guidance to Programme Managers on project development, public information, donor relations, government liaison and information management; ensure consistency and coherence of project/ programme activities in accordance with the CO’s strategies and in coordination with the RO and relevant departments/units at HQ.
10. Provide guidance and support to the Heads of Sub-Offices on the CO’s priorities, policies and strategies.
11. Identify programme strategic priorities in relevant service areas and areas of interest in line with IOM mandate and expertise, aiming to further expand the CO’s partnership basis and the scope of activities.
12. Act as Focal Point for government liaison and oversee the CO’s correspondence and reporting to the government authorities; ensure that the CO’s interests are accurately communicated and promote IOM’s visibility.
13. Represent the CO in inter-agency fora, including but not limited to the Programme Management Team (PMT) and One UN, and One Programme.
14. Lead knowledge management and capacity building activities in the CO.
15. Prepare policy guidance notes, documentation and briefs for COM and senior management.
16. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Political Science, Business or Public Administration, International Studies or a related field from an accredited academic institution with seven years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with nine years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Extensive experience in programme formulation, implementation and evaluation;
- Demonstrated supervisory experience in staff management;
- Proven record of establishing and maintaining good working relationships with governmental and diplomatic authorities, national, regional and international institutions, as well as civil society actors;
- Previous work experience in a rapid transition or post-conflict area;
- Demonstrated experience in liaising with governmental authorities, international agencies (i.e., UN), and civil society organizations;
- Experience in project development, implementation, and reporting, including financial and budgetary aspects; and,
- Familiarity with inter-agency programme regulations of the UN and other donors.

**Skills**

- In-depth knowledge of the broad range of migration-related subject areas dealt with by the Organization;
- Sound judgment, ability to analyze information and make decisions rapidly to resolve operational problems;
- Efficiency, flexibility, high level of professionalism and ability to adhere to strict deadlines;
- Strong leadership, management, and coordination ability;
- Sound communication and interpersonal skills;
- Ability to work effectively and harmoniously with colleagues from varied cultures and backgrounds;
- Familiarity with IOM’s Migrant Management Operational Systems Application (MiMOSA) and Project Information and Management Application (PRIMA) systems;
- Knowledge of the IOM project management cycle; and,
- Knowledge of IOM’s administrative and financial management.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Business Development & Resource Acquisition Manager
jobs.description:
**The Organisation**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking an ambitious, strategic and relationship-driven Business Development Manager to lead the growth and diversification of Plan International Liberia's funding portfolio and strengthen our position as a trusted partner for donors, National Organisations, foundations, UN agencies, NGOs and corporate stakeholders.

As a member of the Extended Country Leadership Team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering the country's resource mobilisation strategy, identifying and securing new funding opportunities that support sustainable, high-impact programmes for children and young people, particularly girls. You will lead strategic donor engagement, build high-value partnerships, provide market and donor intelligence, and position Plan International Liberia to compete successfully for institutional and private funding.

This is a unique opportunity to influence the future growth of the organisation, leading the full business development lifecycle from opportunity identification, donor mapping and consortium building through to proposal development, grant acquisition and donor stewardship. Working closely with programme, finance and technical teams, you will ensure the development of compelling, donor-compliant funding proposals that align with both donor priorities and Plan International's country strategy.

Key responsibilities:

jobs.title: Recruiter

- Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines simultaneously.

- Provide technical guidance and training to program staff and roster personnel on MEL tools, reporting requirements, and evidence-based learning practices.

- Practical experience monitoring outbreak response, surveillance or contact-tracing activities.

jobs.title: Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Location** DRC based /home based for DRC Nationals
**Position Type:** Consultant (40 hours per week)
**Length of Contract:** 3 months with possibility of extension

**Compensation:** Rates competitive for DRC

**Start Date**: ASAP

**Background**

Global Outbreak Response Support (GORS) delivered by Global Emergency Group, Inc. (GEG), under a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy (GHSD), provides rapid activation, surge response, and transition support enabling countries to detect, contain, and recover from infectious disease outbreaks. GEG leads GORS as the prime recipient, building on its ongoing role as Field Programs Support lead for Team Credence on the Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC). Founded in 2007, GEG delivers GORS through a global network of regional response hubs, a pre-vetted surge roster, and embedded in-country teams that mobilize within hours of an authorized outbreak response.

**Reporting/Communication Lines**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator reports to the GORS Senior Operations Lead for work planning, delivery and performance and receives functional technical oversight from the GEG Finance Lead. The Finance Compliance and Grants Coordinator works closely with the Program Director, Senior Technical Director, designated subaward managers, Senior Operations Lead, A2A Technical Lead and Senior MEL Officer.

**Scope of Work**

**Position Description**

The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator is responsible for accurate, compliant and decision-useful financial management for readiness, activations, partners, technology and expenditure-to-results reporting.

*The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will:*

- Maintain the program budget, forecasts, burn rate, activation scenarios and cost allocation across fixed and activation-dependent activities.
- Ensure every material cost links to an approved activity, output, result and responsible function.
- Jointly develop, test and maintain rapid-activation finance procedures with Finance leadership and the GORS team, covering emergency budgets, advances, payment processing and reconciliation, including delegated and backup approvals.
- Review potential new subawards to ensure due diligence, past performance, and eligibility requirements are followed in accordance with award requirements and flow-down provisions.
- Financial onboarding for new personnel.
- Manage payroll and expense processing for personnel including performing monthly reconciliations for any credit card company charges.
- Administer approved personnel-related financial processes in coordination with HR and qualified country-specific advisers. Contribute financial inputs to personnel and travel policies; refer policy approval and employment-status decisions to authorized GEG management
- Coordinate partner financial monitoring with designated subaward managers and technical leads; verify required technical acceptance and supporting documentation before payment processing under applicable terms and delegated authority.
- Produce financial reports and decision briefs for the Program Director, Senior Technical Director, Senior Operations Lead and GEG Finance Manager, highlighting commitments, forecasts, variances and implications for delivery.
- Prepare funding requests and financial reports in the formats and at the intervals required by the applicable award, for authorized review and submission. Maintain a calendar of applicable financial compliance obligations.
- Produce monthly accounting of all expenses for submission to GHSD.
- Support expenditure-to-results reviews and flag where spending, delivery and performance diverge.
- Maintain separation of requisition, technical acceptance, authorization, payment and reconciliation, with alternative controls where staffing is limited
- Support Analysis-to-Action (A2A) Hub in lifecycle-cost modelling.
- Ensure compliance with all USG financial requirements.

**Required Position Qualifications**

- Relevant degree/professional qualification in finance, accounting, grants management or a related field.
- At minimum 5 years of donor-funded program and finance experience, preferably including USG and emergency operations.
- Demonstrated experience adhering to USG award requirements and ability to translate award provisions into actionable award management procedures.
- Experience managing subrecipients and subcontracts.
- Strong experience in budgeting, forecasting, subaward monitoring, audit readiness and rapid-response finance.
- Ability to translate financial data into clear management decisions under time pressure
- Excellent attention to detail in maintaining organized and accurate financial and programmatic records across multiple projects and countries.
- Fluent professional English and French; additional languages and international experience are assets.
- DRC nationality or African regional nationality a prerequisite

**Competencies/Performance Criteria**

- Adherence to and promotion of the GEG Way.

**Travel Frequency**

The Finance Compliance and Grants Coordinator may conduct occasional planned travel to support program meetings, workshops, simulations, or response activities as required.

**Working Conditions**

The Finance Compliance and Grants Coordinator will work from their home base in the DRC if a DRC national, or will be based in the DRC if a national from a country within the region. Working hours will be scheduled within the contracted 40-hour weekly allocation, with hours aligned to DRC operations and agreed overlap across relevant time zones. Emergency support will follow agreed activation and backup arrangements. The Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator adheres to GEG security management directives and policies.

**Benefits**

As personnel dedicated to GORS delivery, the Finance, Compliance and Grants Coordinator will have access to those Global Emergency Group benefits available in DRC.

**About Global Emergency Group**

Founded in 2007, GEG is a benefit corporation that supports vulnerable people affected by crisis in more than 52 countries by providing a broad range of humanitarian support services to a wide range of organizations, including the United Nations, the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, donor governments, companies, major international and national NGO’s and local communities. Every day, these organizations and communities rely on GEG’s emergency response expertise, and on the combined capabilities and dedication of its people to implement strategies, find solutions and seize opportunities to assist the world’s most vulnerable people.

Global Emergency Group is committed to being an equal opportunity employer and recruiting people of diverse backgrounds and experiences. GEG does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion or belief, color, gender, sex, sexual orientation, marital status, family structure, age, medical condition, disability, ancestry, national origin or ethnic group. All recruitment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications, merit and business need.

jobs.title: Consultoría para la Evaluación Final del proyecto “Resilientes, Empoderadas, Sanas y Decididas (RESPOND)” – Venezuela
jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
Consulta los TDR completos aquí: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20261006_TdR_Evaluacion_Final_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/20261006_TdR_Evaluacion_Final_RESPOND.pdf)

Anexo Marco lógico: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_1_Marco_Logico_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_1_Marco_Logico_RESPOND.pdf)

Anexo proyecto Respond: [https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_2_MMR_RESPOND.pdf](https://entintavioleta.com.ve/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Anexo_2_MMR_RESPOND.pdf)

**Antecedentes**
El proyecto Resilientes, Empoderadas, Sanas y Decididas (RESPOND) se implementa en Venezuela con el
propósito de mejorar el ejercicio de la salud y los derechos sexuales y reproductivos (SDSR) de las mujeres
adolescentes y jóvenes (MAJ) y de las mujeres en edad reproductiva (MER) en los estados Anzoátegui y
Miranda.

El proyecto se desarrolla en nueve municipios: Simón Bolívar, Sotillo, Bruzual, Píritu y Guanta en Anzoátegui; y
Sucre, Cristóbal Rojas, Urdaneta y Tomás Lander en Miranda. RESPOND articula acciones orientadas a
fortalecer la demanda, reducir barreras en la oferta de servicios de SDSR y fortalecer la rendición de cuentas y
la incidencia de organizaciones de mujeres y organizaciones lideradas por jóvenes.
En el marco del proyecto se realizó una línea de base con enfoque antes-después para establecer valores
iniciales de indicadores del Marco de Medición del Rendimiento (MMR). La línea de base incluyó encuestas a
adolescentes y jóvenes, encuestas a mujeres en edad reproductiva, revisión de datos secundarios, encuestas a
líderes y lideresas comunitarias y evaluación de impacto organizacional a organizaciones de mujeres y de
jóvenes.

La línea de base se desarrolló entre diciembre de 2024 y abril de 2025 y alcanzó una muestra efectiva de 2.239
personas/entidades: 788 mujeres adolescentes y jóvenes, 838 hombres adolescentes y jóvenes, 422 mujeres
en edad reproductiva, 126 líderes y lideresas comunitarias y 65 representantes de organizaciones.
Adicionalmente, mediante la Evaluación de Necesidades de los Centros de Salud (ENCS), se establecieron los
valores iniciales de los indicadores 1200b y 1220a en los seis establecimientos de salud focalizados por el
proyecto (tres en Anzoátegui y tres en Miranda). Esta medición, realizada mediante entrevista estructurada y
observación con representantes responsables de infraestructura y de servicios e insumos, fue complementaria
y separada del estudio de línea de base. Dado que el instrumento original de la ENCS abarcó elementos
adicionales a los requeridos por los marcos de medición de estos indicadores, El equipo técnico del proyecto
revisará y acotará el instrumento para la medición final. La evaluación aplicará únicamente las variables
necesarias para calcular los indicadores 1200b y 1220a, manteniendo sus definiciones, reglas de cálculo y
comparabilidad con los valores iniciales. Además, profundizará cualitativamente en los cambios, barreras, uso
de recursos, protocolos, referenciación y sostenibilidad.
De cara al cierre del proyecto, se requiere una evaluación final mixta que combine: (i) la medición cuantitativa
de indicadores seleccionados del MMR; y (ii) un componente cualitativo que analice el desempeño y los
resultados del proyecto con base en criterios del Comité de Ayuda al Desarrollo (DAC por sus siglas en inglés)
de la Organización para la Cooperación y el Desarrollo Económicos (OCDE), complementando y explicando los
hallazgos cuantitativos.

**Objetivo general de la consultoría**
Realizar la evaluación final del proyecto RESPOND en Venezuela mediante la medición cuantitativa de
indicadores priorizados del MMR, y la evaluación cualitativa del desempeño, resultados, aportes y
sostenibilidad del proyecto con base en criterios CAD/OCDE (DAC), a fin de generar evidencia útil para la
rendición de cuentas, el aprendizaje y el diseño de futuras intervenciones.

**Objetivos específicos**
• Medir al cierre los indicadores cuantitativos priorizados del proyecto que fueron establecidos en la línea de
base, utilizando como referencia los instrumentos aplicados en esa medición, con ajustes menores
debidamente justificados.
• Obtener los valores finales de los indicadores 1200b y 1220a en los seis establecimientos de salud
focalizados, mediante la aplicación de un instrumento revisado y acotado por el equipo técnico del proyecto
que incluya únicamente las variables necesarias para su cálculo, preservando la comparabilidad con los
valores iniciales establecidos mediante la ENCS. Comparar los resultados finales con los valores de línea
de base y/o de mediciones previas disponibles y con las metas establecidas, identificando cambios,
avances, rezagos y hallazgos relevantes.
• Diseñar e implementar un componente cualitativo que permita evaluar el proyecto con base en criterios de
pertinencia, coherencia, eficacia, eficiencia, impacto y sostenibilidad, e integrar el análisis transversal de
género, derechos, protección e inclusión.
• Analizar factores facilitadores y limitantes del proyecto, incluyendo factores institucionales, operativos,
comunitarios, socioculturales, de género y contextuales que hayan influido positiva o negativamente en la
implementación y los resultados alcanzados, así como percepciones de participantes y actores clave sobre
la relevancia, calidad, resultados y sostenibilidad de las acciones del proyecto. Documentar conclusiones,
lecciones aprendidas, buenas prácticas y recomendaciones para futuras intervenciones en SDSR, igualdad
de género, prevención y respuesta a la violencia y fortalecimiento comunitario/organizacional.

jobs.title: GBV Case Worker
jobs.description:
**Who we are?**

***IDA is an international independent non-governmental organization providing medical and humanitarian assistance to people affected by conflicts, natural disasters and epidemics regardless of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.***
***IDA was founded in 2012 by Syrian doctors from Aleppo in response to the healthcare and humanitarian crisis in Syria.***

***IDA Syria is the main healthcare provider in the Northern Aleppo/Syria area, working closely with 500,000 IDPs and 700,000 host community through 20 healthcare facility and other health and nutrition projects***

**During last year, IDA has provided 1.2 million services in Heath, Nutrition, WaSH and Camp Management**

***Location: Syria - Aleppo : Qabtan Eljabal PHC + Kafr Hamra PHC+ : Medanki PHC+ Basuta PHC***

Main Duties and Responsibilities:

Participation and support in identifying individuals at risk of gender-based violence
Provide individual case management to clients in accordance with the survivor-centred approach and all relevant case management steps, tools and procedures: conduct needs and risk assessments, care planning, safety plans, case conferences, referrals, and provide emotional support to survivors as required.
Ensure proper documentation and compilation of case management forms according to the GBV Case Management System.
Ensure that all high-risk cases are promptly addressed in coordination with the direct line manager
In collaboration with the supervisor, work closely with the other organization in order to ensure smooth referrals
Actively participate in the weekly case management team meeting
Communicate regularly with the Program Officer for updates on achievements and challenges
Doing weekly clinical supervision and consultation
Any other GBV related activities as requested by the line manager
Provide input for weekly and employee activity reports
Collaborate closely with PSS teams, CP & other sectors when needed.
Communicate directly with social workers and other service providers as part of individual case management
Regularly attend case management meetings at the field level
Contribute to the development of proposed activities in relation to case management

-Strictly adhere to humanitarian and protection principles and standards, as well as organizational policies including the Code of Conduct, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and Child Protection

**Required Qualifications:**

Technical Diploma or Degree in Social Work, Counseling, Human Rights or related degree
At least one year of experience implementing GBV programmes, preferred social work or case management, in humanitarian or development settings
Committed to rights-based and community-based approaches.
Demonstrate understanding of working with vulnerable women
Personal qualities: Good listener, team player, flexible, network builder, able to handle pressure well and work in a multicultural environment.
Native speaker of the Arabic language

***Independent Doctors Association does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, and committed to acting professionally and ethically.***
***Independent Doctors Association is zero tolerable with any SEA case, IDA is creating the best environment to make sure that all staff have understood SEA and how to report in case there is any suspected case***
