The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

The successful implementation of CDR’s digital transformation requires the establishment of a clear governance and implementation foundation before major technology investments and platform deployments can proceed. This includes defining ownership and decision-making arrangements, validating the target structure and functions of the Information Technology Department, establishing an enterprise architecture and data governance framework, and ensuring that core business processes are appropriately re-baselined to reflect the future operating model. It also requires a clear understanding of CDR’s existing technology, systems, data, infrastructure, and security environment, together with a structured approach to prioritizing investments and addressing critical gaps.

Therefore, a set of foundational measures have been identified to be undertaken during Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Roadmap. These measures are intended to establish the rules, governance arrangements, technical and organizational architecture, inventories, and implementation baseline required to guide subsequent phases of digital transformation. They include the establishment of programme governance arrangements, validation of the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, definition of data governance principles, risk-based re-baselining of core processes, and preparation of the inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budgets required to move from planning to implementation. Immediate actions have also been identified to strengthen CDR’s existing backup, recovery, and cybersecurity arrangements using available tools and resources, alongside urgent remediation measures that need to be initiated.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert to support CDR in delivering Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Program. The Expert will establish the programme governance arrangements and implementation baseline, validate the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, define the foundations for data governance, and validate the priority use cases of the document management system and the shared workflow system. The Expert will also prepare the key inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budget requirements needed to enable subsequent digital investments and implementation.

Through this assignment, the Expert will support CDR in moving from the recommendations of the Functional and Business Process Review to a structured and implementable digital transformation programme, ensuring that the institutional, governance, process, technical, procurement, and financial foundations are in place before major digital platforms and systems proceed to implementation.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Program Governance and Mobilization**

- Within two weeks of mobilization, agree with CDR the process scope, the technical changes, the available working days and the resources required for this assignment, and prepare a work plan that schedules the remaining work with its owners, dependencies and costs.
- Support CDR in establishing the governance bodies of the Digital Transformation Program, comprising the ICT Steering Committee, the Data Governance Committee and the Technical Review Committee, and prepare their terms of reference, their decision rights and the responsibility matrix that assigns each decision to a named body. The terms of reference of the ICT Steering Committee cover its decisions, escalation arrangements, meeting frequency and progress reporting. Support CDR management in formally designating the interim ICT Transformation Lead and the business and technical owners of critical systems and services.
- Support the establishment of the Digital Transformation Program Office function, comprising the integrated roadmap, the dependency register, the risk register, the benefits plan, the procurement plan, the architecture decision log and the reporting calendar, and hand the instruments over in working order.
- Assist in validation of the target structure and staffing of the Information Technology Department against the functions the program requires, the existing staff and their workload, and coordinate the resulting job descriptions with the human resources workstream so that a single set of descriptions is produced. Prepare the responsibility matrix of the Department, identify staffing and skills gaps, and recommend interim assignments, training and specialist support. Formal appointments and organizational decisions remain with CDR.

**Workstream 2. Architecture and Data Governance**

- Develop and validate the enterprise architecture and the digital building blocks against the baseline covering the business, data, application, integration, technology and governance domains. Produce an updated high-level application and integration diagram, confirm the roles of JDE, the document management system, ArcGIS and the planned systems, and record the compatibility issues, dependencies and decisions required before procurement.
- Support in establishing the standing coordination arrangement with the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and, where relevant, with the national digital acceleration program, with a designated focal point, a defined agenda covering hosting, interoperability, digital identity and electronic signature, and a reporting line to the ICT Steering Committee.
- Prepare the initial data governance principles, covering named business data owners, authoritative systems, shared project and contract identifiers, minimum metadata, access and classification, data quality, retention and controlled sharing. Submit the principles, with the validated enterprise architecture, to the ICT Steering Committee for endorsement.

**Workstream 3. Process Re-baselining and Technical Readiness**

- With the business service owners, review the process maps to identify the common requirements for the document management system and the shared workflow system. Validate representative use cases, bottlenecks, document types and control needs to the level required for the terms of reference. Validate the approval thresholds and segregation of duties for these use cases, and record unresolved decisions and required authorizations. Produce a prioritized catalogue of business flows for later implementation. Full process redesign and configuration follow in later stages.
- Prepare the system, application, asset and workload inventories, including hardware, software licenses, contracts and support arrangements, and record the baseline performance indicators, or the method for collecting them where data are not yet available, against which the benefits of the program are later measured. The inventories record quantities, condition, capacity, hosted workloads, owners, dependencies, support status and renewal dates. They also assess workstation upgrade readiness and the priority server, storage, backup, scanner and power-protection needs. The workload inventory of the hosts designated for retirement, prepared by the firm contracted for the server refresh, is incorporated rather than repeated.

**Workstream 4. Procurement and Funding Readiness**

- Prepare the phased procurement strategy. The strategy specifies the document management system and the shared workflow system during this assignment, establishes and accepts the platform in a later stage, and configures the priority business flows in successive releases. Identify the packages, dependencies, lead times and owners, and define separate deliverables and acceptance gates for the platform foundation and for each business-flow release.
- Prepare the technical specifications, quantities and supplier pricing schedule for the justified priority hardware, infrastructure and services. Compare reuse, support renewal, repair and replacement, and include capacity, compatibility, migration, warranty, support response, acceptance testing and staff handover requirements.
- Reconcile the installed software and its use with entitlements and contracts. Verify the current vendor lifecycle and upgrade terms for operating systems, productivity tools, server and database licenses, electronic mail, endpoint protection, backup, firewalls and core applications. Identify renewals, unused entitlements and license gaps, and prepare a costed renewal and upgrade schedule.
- Prepare the terms of reference for the document management system and the shared workflow system, assessing the modernization of the existing SharePoint environment against its replacement. Define document capture, metadata, search, versioning, retention, permissions and audit trails; reusable forms, routing, approvals, notifications and monitoring; configurable roles, approval rules and audit controls; integration with JDE and identity services; and migration, hosting, licensing, training and support. Specify the platform acceptance tests and the later releases of priority business flows. The requirements preserve CDR data ownership, editable documentation, interoperability, portability and exit rights, with brand-neutral specifications where feasible.
- Prepare the indicative multi-year budget for the three-year horizon of the roadmap, separating implementation costs from recurring costs, and covering operations, maintenance, staffing, training, security reviews, licensing, hosting, support, hardware refresh, integration maintenance and contingency, and confirm the institutional and budget owner of each system before procurement.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 16 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

Any continuation of the services beyond this period, including the second phase of support described in the Background, is subject to a separate contract or a formal amendment of this contract. Continuation depends on satisfactory performance under this contract, the continued requirement for the services and the availability of funds.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Digital Transformation, Information Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field. Specialized focus on enterprise architecture, information systems, digital transformation, data governance, cybersecurity, or ICT management is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) designing, managing, or implementing digital transformation and information management programmes, including ICT governance, enterprise architecture, systems integration, data governance, and business-process digitization; and (ii) providing strategic and technical advice on ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity, information systems, technology procurement, and digital transformation planning, preferably in public-sector or institutional environments.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

To this end, there is a need to strengthen the human resource function itself, including its organization, processes, policies, systems, and service delivery arrangements. A strengthened HR function is essential to support workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, career progression, and other core personnel processes, while also providing the institutional capacity required to support the wider CDR reform programme. In this context, the HR function needs to move beyond the administration of personnel matters toward a more structured and integrated approach to workforce management aligned with CDR's functions, organizational structure, and operational priorities.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Human Resources Expert to support CDR in implementing the human resource measures under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will review and update the existing and proposed job descriptions against the applicable legislative framework and operational requirements, reassess the HR function identified, and translate the findings into an HR Strategy, HR Policies and Procedures Manual, and target operating model for the Human Resources Department. The assignment will also ensure that the HR Strategy incorporates the human resource requirements arising from other reform areas, including change management and the development and implementation of a Human Resource Information System.

Through this assignment, the Expert will contribute to establishing a clearer, more functional, and sustainable human resource framework for CDR, with defined roles and responsibilities, updated job descriptions, appropriate HR policies and procedures, and an operating model capable of supporting both CDR's immediate staffing needs and the longer-term institutional reforms identified in the roadmap.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Human Resources Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Assessment of the Human Resource Function and HR Strategy**

- Review human resource arrangements, relevant institutional findings and proposed reform priorities to establish the baseline for the assessment.
- Review the legal and regulatory framework that governs CDR staff, including Decree No. 10941 of 2003, Decree No. 10942 of 2003, Section 54 of the 2004 Budget Law, the Council of Ministers freeze on hiring and promotion, the allowance decrees issued between 2021 and 2025, the Council of Ministers decision of 19 June 2025 and the internal regulations of CDR, and record for each human resource process the rule that governs it and the authority that approves it.
- Validate the workforce baseline with the Administrative Affairs Division, covering filled and vacant mandated posts, individual contractors, project implementation unit personnel, projected retirements, resignations and multi-role assignments, and identify any figures that are not substantiated by the available records.
- Assess the mandate, organization, staffing and capacity of the Human Resources Department within the Administrative Affairs Division.
- Map the human resource processes as they operate today, covering workforce planning, recruitment and onboarding, personnel records, attendance and leave, performance evaluation and promotion, training, discipline, and separation and end-of-service, and record where a process is informal, paper-based or undocumented.
- Identify the gaps between current practice, the legal framework and the needs of the reformed structure, and distinguish the gaps that CDR can close within the current legal framework from those that depend on the amendment of Decree No. 10941 and Decree No. 10942.
- Establish the baseline and the method of measurement for human resource indicators including the employee-satisfaction baseline survey, coordinated with the staff survey used for the change indicators so that staff are surveyed once.
- Prepare the HR Strategy for CDR, setting out its objectives, priority measures, responsibilities and sequence, aligned with the Target Roadmap and the Interim Arrangements, and addressing the vacancy, multi-role and key-person dependency risks identified.
- Set out in the Strategy the recruitment route for the transitional period and the longer-term recruitment model, consistent with the position on the Civil Service Board mandate.
- Define the target operating model of the Human Resources Department, comprising its functions, roles, reporting lines and staffing, and its role as business owner of the Human Resource Information System.
- Set out in the Strategy the human resource input to the Change Management Committee on the resistance factors linked to restructuring, redeployment and remuneration, and coordinate the staff messages on these matters with the Change Management and Communications Expert.
- Set out in the Strategy the business requirements of the Human Resources Department for the Human Resource Information System identified, validating the human resource process definitions, the business rules for attendance, leave and missions, and the employee data structure, and confirming the legal basis of the end-of-service calculation before any procurement.
- Prepare the action plan that implements the Strategy, with responsibilities assigned by post and timing reconciled with the master roadmap.

**Workstream 2. Review and Update of Job Descriptions**

- Compile the inventory of the job descriptions already prepared, comprising those prepared by the Administrative Affairs Division including identified positions, Terms of Reference, job description summaries and IT Department job descriptions, and identify the existing and new posts for which no description exists.
- Review each JD against the applicable legislation, including the ranks, sub-grades and qualification requirements under Decree No. 10942, the divisional and departmental mandates under Decree No. 10941 and the reformed structure, and, for procurement posts, the requirements of Law No. 244 of 2021 on the competencies and career paths of procurement staff.
- Review each description against the operational needs of CDR, testing with the Heads of Division whether the scope of work, reporting lines, decision rights and qualifications correspond to the work the role performs under the redesigned business processes.
- Harmonize the descriptions into a single template that records, for each post, the interim placement within the current structure and the position under the reformed structure, so that the same document serves recruitment now and redeployment later.
- Update the descriptions on the basis of the review, remove overlaps between posts, reflect the segregation of duties required in the financial management, procurement and ICT processes, and complete the descriptions for the posts not yet covered.
- Reconcile the rank assigned to each post with the indicative costing identified, and record each discrepancy for the remuneration and financing proposal.
- Confirm the updated descriptions with the Heads of Division and prepare the submission through which the Board approves them.
- Prepare the procedure through which the Administrative Affairs Division maintains the descriptions as the structure changes, and brief the Division on its application.

**Workstream 3. HR Policies, Performance Management and Capacity Development**

- Prepare the HR Policies and Procedures Manual, documenting each human resource process with its steps, responsibilities, approvals, time standards and forms, and removing steps whose risk does not justify them before the process is digitized.
- Review the performance-evaluation system for promotion reactivated in 2025, and propose how it draws on the updated job descriptions within the promotion rules of Decree No. 10942.
- Prepare the human resource provisions on employee protection, covering discrimination and workplace misconduct, conflict-of-interest declarations for staff holding more than one role, and disciplinary consequences for retaliation, in coordination with the Audit Committee, which owns the whistleblower policy set out, and with the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert.
- Prepare the competency-based capacity development strategy, consolidating the role-based learning pathways with the identified function-specific training and defining the training-needs assessment method, the format of the annual training plan and the pre- and post-training assessment of competency.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 11 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Human Resources Management, Public Administration, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Management, Public Policy, Law, or a related field.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) assessing and strengthening human resource functions and organizational structures, including workforce planning, HR processes, job descriptions, performance management, recruitment, staff development and HR policies; and (ii) designing and implementing HR strategies, operating models, policies and procedures, including HR information systems and competency-based capacity development frameworks.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1I4CjphA3f10d4Xemt4XjIPPy2AeOVK9z/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1I4CjphA3f10d4Xemt4XjIPPy2AeOVK9z/view?usp=drive_link)

The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

Workplace integrity and employee protection arrangements are particularly relevant to the implementation of CDR's broader institutional reform programme. As organizational structures, responsibilities, processes, and management arrangements evolve, CDR requires clear institutional policies and mechanisms governing workplace conduct, employee protection, reporting of concerns, and equal treatment. Such arrangements need to be embedded within CDR's regular management and human resource practices rather than treated solely as requirements associated with individual donor-funded projects. They should also be supported by practical reporting, awareness, monitoring, and accountability mechanisms that can operate within CDR's existing institutional framework.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert to support CDR in developing the institutional instruments and operational arrangements required under Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will prepare the policies and mechanisms governing whistleblowing and protection from retaliation, workplace conduct, discrimination, harassment, and gender equality in a form that can be adopted by the Board of Directors within the existing legal framework. The assignment will also establish a practical gender-mainstreaming framework, with defined entry points across workforce management, recruitment and promotion, staff development, workplace policies, reporting, and monitoring.

The assignment will further support the establishment of a confidential reporting channel and the awareness and communication arrangements required to ensure that staff understand their rights, responsibilities, reporting options, and available protections. Through these measures, the assignment will contribute to strengthening workplace integrity and employee protection at CDR and to embedding gender mainstreaming within the institution's management and human resource practices as an integral component of the broader reform programme.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Workplace Integrity and Gender Mainstreaming Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1: Whistleblower Protection and Workplace Integrity**

- Identify the provisions of Lebanese law applicable to whistleblower protection, equality and non-discrimination, sexual harassment and other relevant workplace protections that bind CDR, citing the instrument, article and date for each, and determine what those provisions already require of the institution and what they leave to internal policy.
- Review the safeguarding and reporting arrangements that already operate within donor-funded project frameworks at CDR and determine which staff categories they cover and which they leave unprotected, including staff on all employment categories, contractors embedded within CDR and project implementation unit personnel. Identify relevant gender-related provisions, including measures addressing gender-based violence, sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment.
- Draft the Whistleblower Policy, covering a designated confidential reporting channel separate from line management and accessible to all staff and embedded personnel; a non-retaliation commitment enforceable by the Board that prohibits adverse employment action against a person making a good-faith report and defines the disciplinary consequences of retaliation; an investigation protocol owned by the Audit Committee that specifies handling, confidentiality and escalation, including referral to the internal audit function and, where appropriate, to the competent legal or regulatory authority; and a requirement that all staff are reminded annually of the policy, the channel and the protections in place.
- Draft the Workplace Conduct Policy covering discrimination, harassment and sexual harassment, setting out the prohibited conduct, the reporting routes, the investigation and decision procedure, the sanctions available, and the protection of complainants and witnesses.
- Draft the employee protection provisions that accompany both policies, including confidentiality of records, protection against secondary retaliation and the treatment of reports made in bad faith, in coordination with the human resource provisions on employee protection prepared by the Human Resources Expert.
- Specify the confidential reporting channel in operational terms, covering intake, case registration and numbering, confidentiality safeguards, conflict-of-interest handling, response timelines and record retention, and prepare the case-handling forms and the case register.
- Prepare the submission pack for the Board decision adopting the instruments, and brief the Audit Committee on its responsibilities as policy owner and oversight body.
- Deliver an awareness session for staff, and prepare the annual communication calendar and the awareness materials through which the policies are recalled to staff and embedded personnel.

**Workstream 2: Gender Mainstreaming**

- Assess the existing CDR institutional and human-resource arrangements from a gender-mainstreaming perspective, including women’s representation and participation across grades and decision-making levels taking into account the current workforce profile, recruitment and promotion arrangements, career development, performance management and staff development, and identify key gaps and opportunities for strengthening gender equality within CDR.
- Identify priority gender-mainstreaming entry points across CDR's human-resource and institutional management processes, including workforce planning, recruitment and selection, promotion and career development, performance management, staff development, workplace conduct, internal communication and staff engagement, as well as, where relevant, institutional planning, programmes/projects and decision-making processes.
- Review the existing workplace and employee-protection arrangements from a gender perspective and identify measures required to strengthen prevention of gender-based discrimination, harassment and sexual harassment, as well as gender-sensitive reporting and protection arrangements.
- Define the institutional framework for gender mainstreaming, including the roles, responsibilities and accountability of relevant CDR functions, priority areas for action, and appropriate arrangements for monitoring and periodic review of progress, including the use of sex-disaggregated data across relevant HR and institutional indicators where relevant and feasible.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 9 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 9 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/197**
- **Position Title**: Change Management and Communications Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 5 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hW6l0y4j6wBZ5kkyu0wVnQfOhYf1Oxt4/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hW6l0y4j6wBZ5kkyu0wVnQfOhYf1Oxt4/view)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

The successful implementation of the reform roadmap requires more than the introduction of revised structures, processes, roles, and governance arrangements. The sustainability of the reforms will depend on the extent to which they are understood, accepted, adopted, and integrated into the day-to-day functioning of CDR. This requires a structured approach to managing organizational change, engaging internal and external stakeholders, communicating the rationale and expected benefits of the reforms, anticipating and addressing sources of resistance, and ensuring that emerging challenges are identified and managed in a timely manner. Effective communication will also be important in maintaining transparency and confidence throughout the reform process, particularly where reforms affect institutional roles, responsibilities, reporting arrangements, and working practices.

Furthermore, inclusive change arrangements, transparent and reform-focused communication, and active management of resistance are key conditions for the successful institutionalization of the reform. These instruments form part of the reform governance arrangements identified, including the role of the Change Management Committee in monitoring reform adoption and reporting progress and challenges to the Board of Directors.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Change Management and Communications Expert to support the implementation of Stage 1 of the reform roadmap. The Expert will develop a comprehensive Change Management Plan for the CDR reform programme, incorporating a reform-focused Communications Strategy, a Crisis Communication Plan, and practical measures for identifying, anticipating, and managing resistance to change. The assignment will also support the establishment of appropriate arrangements, tools, and mechanisms through which the Change Management Committee can monitor the adoption of reforms, identify implementation and change-management challenges, and report to the Board of Directors. Through this support, the assignment will contribute to ensuring that the reforms identified through the Functional and Business Process Review are effectively communicated, progressively adopted, and embedded within CDR’s institutional practices and governance arrangements.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Change Management and Communications Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Change Management Plan**

- Review existing reform governance, change management and risk management arrangements, implementation priorities and interim measures to establish the baseline for the Plan.
- Validate, through structured consultations with Heads of Division, with staff at non-managerial level and with the Change Management Committee, the internal and external resistance factors identified, including restructuring and redeployment, shifts in authority and oversight, procurement formalization, digital transformation and remuneration constraints.
- Identify the stakeholder groups affected by each reform measure, the concerns specific to each group, and the points in the roadmap at which those concerns are expected to arise.
- Prepare the Change Management Plan, setting out the intended change process stage by stage in line with the consolidated roadmap, the responsibilities of the Board, the Change Management Committee and the Heads of Division, and the decision points at which the Plan is reviewed.
- Link the Plan explicitly to the Risk Register maintained by the Risk Management Committee, so that each identified resistance factor carries a recorded response approved by the Board.
- Define the measures to manage resistance, including the schedule of outreach used to gauge sentiment across the organization, the early-warning signals that trigger remedial action, and the approach to involving potential opponents of the reform in its implementation.
- Define a set of change indicators covering institutional uptake and adoption, distinct from the activity-completion indicators already carried identified in indicator tables, together with the method and frequency of measurement and the reporting format to the Board.
- Prepare the operating arrangements of the Change Management Committee, comprising its composition of eight to twelve members drawn from across the reform areas, its terms of reference, its meeting calendar, its liaison with the Risk Management Committee and the form of its formal updates to the Board.

**Workstream 2. Communications Strategy and Crisis Communication Plan**

- Conduct baseline assessment of the internal and external communications of the CDR, identifying key challenges starting from the practical issues, including institutional and organizational arrangements, tools and channels used for the communications.
- Design the internal communication arrangements, including regular all-staff meetings led by senior management and a channel through which employees can raise questions and receive answers, and specify how the feedback received is reported to the Committee and to the Board.
- Prepare the Communications Strategy for CDR, defining for each internal and external audience the messages, the channels, the frequency and the responsible speaker, and covering staff, line ministries, oversight bodies, financing partners, contractors and consultants, and the public.
- Prepare the Crisis Communication Plan, identifying the categories of crisis to which CDR is exposed, designating prepared spokespeople and pre-positioning approved messaging, with specific attention to public perception of corruption and to the demonstration of CDR commitment to oversight and audit compliance.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 5 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 5 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Organizational Development, Change Management, Communications, Public Administration, Public Policy, Business Administration, Management or a related field. Specialized focus on organizational change, institutional development, strategic communications, or public sector reform is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) designing and implementing change management approaches for organizational or institutional reforms, including stakeholder engagement, resistance management, change adoption, and organizational communication; and (ii) developing and implementing strategic communications strategies, internal communications arrangements, stakeholder engagement plans, and/or crisis communication frameworks.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

jobs.description:
To lead and represent **Takaful Al Sham Association** in Germany by translating the Association's international strategy into operational plans, local programs, and initiatives that serve the targeted communities and address their needs. The role ensures full compliance with German legal and financial regulations while building strategic partnerships and mobilizing resources to support the Association's projects and international objectives under the direct supervision of the **Director of Missions and International Offices.**

Main tasks and responsibilities:

- Develop and implement outreach, networking, and stakeholder engagement plans with German institutions, NGOs, community centers, academic institutions, and professional associations to expand the Association's partnership network and establish strategic cooperation agreements.
- Plan, manage, and oversee fundraising campaigns, local initiatives, and resource mobilization activities in full compliance with German and European fundraising regulations.
- Build, manage, and strengthen relationships with local donors and supporters in Germany in accordance with the Association's approved fundraising policies and guidelines.
- Translate the Association's strategic objectives into operational plans, projects, and local initiatives tailored to the needs and context of the target communities in Germany.
- Lead the implementation, supervision, and quality assurance of approved educational, capacity-building, vocational, and empowerment programs and activities.
- Lead and coordinate knowledge transfer initiatives by engaging highly qualified professionals residing in Germany and developing programs that strengthen the capacities of personnel inside Syria in accordance with the Association's approved mechanisms.
- Develop context-appropriate project proposals and present them to local partners and potential donors.
- Manage the Association's registered legal entity in Germany and ensure full compliance with applicable labor laws, municipal regulations, tax requirements, and other legal obligations.
- Issue day-to-day operational and administrative decisions within the delegated authority framework approved by the Association.
- Coordinate with external legal and financial auditors, including certified public accountants, and manage the execution of local service contracts in compliance with German regulations.
- Prepare the annual administrative and operational budgets for the Germany Mission and submit them for approval. Ensure that no expenditures or financial commitments are made without prior authorization from the Association's management.
- Manage daily financial operations and accounting records in accordance with the Association's financial policies and procedures.
- Manage the Association's official bank accounts and approved electronic payment channels, perform reconciliations, and submit regular cash flow reports.
- Prepare and submit periodic monitoring, evaluation, quality assurance, and performance reports to the Association's management for review and technical guidance.
- Prepare and submit all required compliance reports to German municipalities, tax authorities, and other relevant regulatory bodies, while regularly sharing complete copies with the Association's management.
- Ensure that all emergency, exceptional, or strategic programmatic reports are submitted to the Association's management for review and approval before being shared with any external entity or international donor, ensuring consistency in the Association's institutional messaging.
- Immediately report and escalate to the Association's management any significant developments, disputes, or operational decisions that may pose legal, reputational, or public-benefit risks.

- Experience: Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in managing non-profit organizations, training institutions, civil society organizations, or academic associations.
- Languages: Full professional proficiency in both Arabic and German (spoken, written, and reading). Excellent command of English is considered a strong asset.

- Initiative and Accountability: Strong sense of ownership, proactive approach, and demonstrated ability to build teams and foster institutional collaboration with diverse stakeholders.

- Organizational and Financial Management Skills: Excellent planning, organizational, budgeting, financial analysis, and official reporting skills.

jobs.title: MICRO-INFLUENCER CAMPAIGN TO PROMOTE THE CHOREOGRAPHY OF THE DISASTER RISK AWARENESS SONG
NVPPA Supervisor (Service Staff Supervisor)
jobs.description:
**IRC background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job overview**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year:”*

The National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement (NVPPA) is a nationwide, fully virtual program through which IRC will serve newly arrived refugees under a cooperative agreement with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR). Participants receive career navigation, training, job placement support, and direct financial assistance to advance an individualized career goal.

The NVPPA Supervisor manages the day-to-day work of the program's direct service team across a fully virtual, national caseload. This role is responsible for caseload management, case file review, escalation and resolution of participant issues, and consistent quality across Professional Advancement Plans (PAPs) and uses of direct financial assistance.

**Major responsibilities**

**Supervision and caseload management**

- Manage day-to-day caseloads for direct service staff, including assigning and balancing participants across Career Navigators and routing participants on credentialing and recertification pathways to specialized navigators.
- Conduct regular case file review to confirm that participant records, including eligibility documentation, PAPs, and case notes, are complete, accurate, and timely.
- Resolve escalated participant issues in partnership with the Customer Service Representative, and determine when an issue requires the Deputy Director's involvement.
- Support onboarding and ongoing training of direct service staff.
- Translate program requirements into standard operating procedures and desk guides for the direct service team.

**Program quality and compliance**

- Review PAPs for soundness and confirm that career goals and proposed uses of funds meet ORR eligibility requirements before assistance is requested.
- Ensure required safeguards are applied to higher-risk uses of financial assistance, such as vehicle purchases.
- Work with the data team to ensure required data is recorded in Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) and electronic case files are complete for ORR reporting.
- Monitor progress against program targets, identify barriers in the service model such as digital access, language access, or credential evaluation delays, and work with the Deputy Director on practical adjustments.

**Coordination**

- Coordinate handoffs among navigation, training, financial assistance, and job placement so that participants move smoothly through the program.
- Work with administrative and finance staff to ensure financial assistance requests are complete, documented, and aligned with each participant's PAP.
- Coordinate with other resettlement and employment programs, IRC offices, sister agencies, and local partners serving the same participants to support appropriate co-enrollment and avoid duplication of services.

**Job requirements**

- Undergraduate degree required, ideally in Social Work, Human Services, or a related field; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 2 years of management or supervision experience required, including onboarding, coaching, and managing staff performance; experience with remote or distributed teams strongly preferred.
- Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience in human services, preferably in resettlement, workforce development, or employment services.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing high-volume caseloads in a compliance-heavy environment, including case file review and quality assurance.
- Demonstrated skills tracking and reporting information in a database; experience with ETO preferred.
- Familiarity with federally funded program compliance and eligibility documentation; experience with ORR-funded programming preferred.
- Experience developing standard operating procedures or workflow documentation, and familiarity with credential evaluation, professional licensing, or recertification pathways, preferred.
- Demonstrated commitment to client confidentiality and data protection, including oversight of how a remote team handles sensitive personal and immigration documents, required.
- Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and time management skills, and demonstrated success working in a multicultural environment.
- Commitment to anti-racism, ongoing learning, and equitable service to all eligible clients regardless of national origin, language, location, or resettlement agency, required.
- Lived experience as a refugee or immigrant preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and remote collaboration tools required.
- Fluency in spoken and written English required; fluency in an additional language relevant to current refugee populations desired.

**Working environment**

- Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet and a private work space suitable for confidential client conversations.
- Scheduling flexibility is required to serve participants across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($58,000 - $70,000 / Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: AI Lead - Consultancy
jobs.description:
**Strengthening Media Capacity and Civil Oversight for Accountability in Lebanon**

## **Project Background**

Lebanon's governance environment is heavily impacted by systemic crises and erosion of the national integrity system. This project aims to strengthen the organizational capacity of six Lebanese media and civil society organizations (CSOs) to evaluate public data sources, apply advanced analytical workflows, and execute evidence-based accountability work.

The project integrates cutting-edge technology, AI-assisted research routines, and automated data monitoring workflows to enhance the analytical capacity of independent media and CSOs scrutinizing public procurement, registries, and financial data in Lebanon.

This project is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in partnership with Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT). It is funded by Germany through the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

- **Duration:** 12 months
- **Level of Effort:** 10 days per month (Total: 120 working days)

## **Role Objective**

The AI Lead establishes and oversees the AI methodology, technical architecture, and workflow standards across all technical activities, ensuring practical, safe, and sustainable integration of AI tools for newsrooms and civic watchdogs.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Data Access & Workflow Feasibility Assessment:** Evaluate automated extraction, web scraping, API routes, LLM prompt engineering, and parsing possibilities for Lebanese public platforms (PPA, CDR, Central Bank, parliamentary records).
