jobs.title: Financial Management and Internal Audit Expert - CDR
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/196**
- **Position Title**: Financial Management and Internal Audit Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/11G9U98moBJUQJ0FYTdCyo-lvs9S6ZEUh/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11G9U98moBJUQJ0FYTdCyo-lvs9S6ZEUh/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

Strengthening of financial control and assurance is an important component of CDR’s institutional reform. This requires reinforcing the independent internal audit function, clarifying the relationship between financial management and the applicable Internal Financial Regulation, strengthening the operating framework of the Financial Management System (FMS), and reassessing the mandate and positioning of the Funding Evaluation Department. These measures are intended to strengthen the control environment, clarify responsibilities and reporting lines, improve the consistency and effectiveness of financial procedures, and enhance CDR’s capacity to assess and monitor funding-related matters.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Financial Management and Internal Audit Expert to support CDR in implementing the relevant Stage 1 reforms through three connected workstreams. The first will support the establishment of an internal audit function on an interim or outsourced basis, with appropriate independence and direct reporting to the Board of Directors through the Audit Committee and aligned with the Global Internal Audit Standards of the Institute of Internal Auditors. The second will support the alignment of the structure, reporting lines, and procedures of the Financial Management System with the Internal Financial Regulation, including through the preparation of an updated Financial Management System Manual. The third will undertake a detailed assessment of the Funding Evaluation Department and support the measures required for its reactivation.

Through this assignment, the Financial Management and Internal Audit Expert will contribute to strengthening CDR’s financial governance, internal control, and assurance arrangements, while supporting the implementation of the broader institutional reform roadmap. The assignment will help establish clearer financial management and oversight responsibilities, strengthen independent assurance, and support the effective functioning of the mechanisms through which CDR manages, evaluates, and oversees its financial resources and funding-related activities.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Financial Management and Internal Audit Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Establishment of the Internal Audit function**

- Assess the current control and assurance environment at CDR against the requirements of Circular No. 5/2025, the audit requirements of Law No. 244/2021 and the Global Internal Audit Standards, and record what the institution must put in place to close the gap.
- Draft the Internal Audit Charter for adoption by the Board, covering the mandate and scope of the function, its authority, the protected functional reporting line to the Audit Committee, the administrative relationship to the Office of the President, unrestricted access to records, staff and information across all divisions without prior clearance from management, and the protection of the budget and of the appointment terms of the person responsible for the function.
- Prepare the mandate, scope, charter and rules of procedure of the Audit Committee, covering its composition, its meeting frequency and quorum, its decision rights, its coordination between CDR, the external auditor and the internal audit function, its ownership of the whistleblower policy and its role as escalation point for integrity-related grievances.
- Define the boundary between the internal audit function, which performs ex-post and risk-based assessment, and the ex-ante legality control exercised by the Government Commissioner, so that the two do not duplicate one another.

**Workstream 2. Alignment of the Financial Management System (FMS) with the Internal Financial Regulation**

- Review the Internal Financial Regulation, the financial procedures currently applied, the organizational chart and the reporting lines of the divisions and departments concerned and record each point at which the prescribed process and the assigned role do not correspond.
- Facilitate the workshops with the Finance Division and the other units concerned through which the procedures, responsibilities and reporting lines are updated, and record the decisions taken.
- Prepare the updated Financial Management System Manual, comprising the policies, the procedures, the process flows, the control points, the segregation of duties and the job descriptions for all positions within the divisions and departments concerned, with the job descriptions prepared in the transition-ready form used across the reform.

**Workstream 3. Assessment and Reactivation of Funding Evaluation Department**

- Reassess the mandate and positioning of the Funding Evaluation Department against current institutional priorities, available capacities and governance needs, and set out the options available to CDR, comprising the recruitment of the minimum staffing required to activate the department as mandated, and the redefinition of its mandate with the integration of its functions within existing units.
- Define the analytical outputs that support decisions of the President and the Board on funding sources and financial engineering, and that can be produced within current resources, specifying for each output its content, its data sources, its preparation route and its frequency.
- Prepare the mandate, scope, charter and rules of procedure of the Strategy Committee, covering its composition, its meeting frequency and quorum, its role in coordinating investment and financing planning and its interface with management.
- Define the coordination mechanism between the two committees (Strategy and Audit) and CDR management, including the calendar of submissions to the Board and the form of the committee reports.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 11 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 11 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within three months from the contract signature date.

Any continuation of the services beyond this period, including the second phase of support described in the Background, is subject to a separate contract or a formal amendment of this contract. Continuation depends on satisfactory performance under this contract, the continued requirement for the services and the availability of funds.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular field visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Accounting, Finance, Financial Management, Auditing, Public Financial Management, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field. Specialized focus on internal audit, public financial management, financial controls, risk management, or institutional financial reform is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) financial management, accounting, internal and/or external audit, financial control and risk management; and (ii) assessing and strengthening financial management systems, internal control frameworks, financial procedures, and governance arrangements, preferably within public-sector institutions and/or donor-funded programmes.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Deputy Director, NVPPA
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**SCOPE:**

*“This position has an end date of Month, Day, Year.”*

The Deputy Director, NVPPA provides leadership to the National Virtual Program for Professional Advancement, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) funded program implemented in FY27. The Deputy Director leads the NVPPA team and ensures sound program implementation, compliance with ORR regulations, client success, and strong staff supervision and support.

NVPPA is a cooperative agreement carried out over a single 12-month period of performance, September 30, 2026 through September 29, 2027. The Deputy Director is accountable for delivering the program on time, within budget, and in compliance with the terms of the award.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Program Implementation and Deliverables***

- Lead program start-up so that intake, staffing, data tools, and referral protocols are in place as clients arrive, with interpretation and device support where access is a barrier.
- Set and enforce service standards across a high-volume, light-touch model, including a completed Professional Advancement Plan (PAP) and documented career navigation for every enrolled participant.
- Oversee delivery of training, job development, and placement support, and ensure related records are maintained.

***Grant Compliance and Award Management***

- Ensure the program is implemented in accordance with ORR policy, the terms of the cooperative agreement, applicable federal award regulations and cost principles, and IRC policies on data protection, client confidentiality, and safeguarding.
- In partnership with the Senior Director, serve as the program's primary point of contact with the ORR program officer and coordinate with ORR staff, partners, and technical assistance providers.
- Protect the integrity of program eligibility, ensuring eligibility rules are applied consistently and documentation is collected and retained for every enrolled participant.
- Own the internal control environment for direct financial assistance, including documentation before disbursement, alignment with the participant's approved PAP, vendor and training provider verification, and application of IRC Global Supply Chain protocols.
- Maintain audit-ready documentation and ensure required program and financial reports are accurate and submitted on schedule.
- Identify, escalate, and resolve compliance risks, including suspected fraud, working with IRC finance, compliance, and award management colleagues on corrective action.

***Budget and Financial Oversight***

- With the Finance Manager, manage the program budget, monitor spending, and ensure full and timely spend-down and closeout of the award.
- Where a shortfall is projected, provide revised projections and propose reallocation to additional eligible services or a budget revision, at ORR's direction.

***Data, Performance, and Quality Assurance***

- Ensure Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) is configured to program requirements and serves as the system of record, working with the data team on data quality, reporting, and staff training.
- Monitor performance against outcome targets and use data to identify barriers and adjust the service model.
- Establish and oversee a routine quality assurance cycle covering case files, PAPs, and assistance documentation, with findings tracked to resolution.

***Supervision and Staffing***

- Lead recruitment, hiring, and onboarding of a newly formed, fully remote team, and ensure all staff are trained on eligibility rules, eligible uses of funds, documentation standards, and the database.
- Directly supervise the NVPPA Supervisor and the Customer Service Representative, and manage performance, workload distribution, and professional development, and structure staffing so that direct service capacity can be adjusted as enrollment volume becomes known.

***Coordination and Representation***

- In close collaboration with the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR), oversee guidance on appropriate co-enrollment with PIR and other ORR programs, such as Matching Grant, so that participants can meet initial self-sufficiency requirements while pursuing career goals.
- Establish referral and coordination protocols with sister resettlement agencies, IRC offices, and other service providers so that eligible clients can access the program regardless of which agency resettled them, and represent the program to IRC office leadership and external partners.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS**

**Position reports to:** Senior Director, Economic Empowerment

**Directly supervises:** NVPPA Supervisor; Customer Service Representative

**Indirect supervision:** Direct service team, through the NVPPA Supervisor

**Key relationships:** Internally, the NVPPA team, Economic Empowerment Technical Unit, IRC office leadership, and headquarters finance, compliance, and award management colleagues. Externally, ORR, PIR providers, sister resettlement agencies, training providers, and employers.

**Requirements:**

- University degree in Business, Public Administration, Social Work, Economics, Community Development, or a related field required; comparable work and/or lived experience may be substituted.
- Minimum of 10 years of experience with progressive responsibility in the design, development, and implementation of workforce, employment, or broader economic empowerment programming, including program monitoring and evaluation.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience managing staff, including remote or geographically distributed teams, with demonstrated ability to coach staff and manage performance directly and through supervisors.
- Demonstrated experience managing federally funded awards and their compliance and reporting requirements; ORR or other HHS award experience strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated experience overseeing client-level direct financial assistance or comparable payment processes, with a strong grasp of internal controls, required; experience with audits or funder monitoring preferred.
- Demonstrated ability to launch a program quickly and manage a budget of comparable scale through spend-down.
- Demonstrated understanding of refugee resettlement and employment services in the U.S. context; familiarity with credential evaluation and professional licensing pathways preferred.
- Excellent communication and organizational skills, including a track record of reporting difficult information to funders accurately and on time.
- Microsoft Office Suite required; ETO or comparable client database experience preferred.
- Commitment to anti-racism and ongoing learning, and English fluency, required.

**Working Environment**

Fully remote, U.S.-based position requiring reliable high-speed internet, a private work space suitable for confidential discussions, and scheduling flexibility across U.S. time zones; occasional travel may be required.

**Compensation:** ($94,000 - $105,000 \[GEO 1\]). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403(b) retirement savings plan with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Ecosystem Mapping Consultant
jobs.description:
**Strengthening Media Capacity and Civil Oversight for Accountability in Lebanon**

## **Project Background**

Lebanon's governance environment is heavily impacted by systemic crises and erosion of the national integrity system. This project aims to strengthen the organizational capacity of six Lebanese media and civil society organizations (CSOs) to evaluate public data sources, apply advanced analytical workflows, and execute evidence-based accountability work.

The project integrates cutting-edge technology, AI-assisted research routines, and automated data monitoring workflows to enhance the analytical capacity of independent media and CSOs scrutinizing public procurement, registries, and financial data in Lebanon.

This project is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in partnership with Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT). It is funded by Germany through the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

## **Role Objective**

The Ecosystem Mapping Consultant conducts comprehensive mapping, desk research, dataset auditing, and structured interviews to identify candidate partner organizations and evaluate the technical feasibility of data-driven oversight in Lebanon.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Desk Research & Data Inventory:** Review media freedom reporting (CPJ, RSF, SMEX, SKeyes), donor reporting (CFI Qarib), and audit public data platforms (PPA portal, CDR procurement data, Central Bank, commercial registers, TI Lebanon Ekhbar platform).
- **Structured Stakeholder Interviews:** Conduct structured interviews with 12–15 independent media outlets, investigative platforms, and CSOs across Lebanon to assess editorial mandates, technical capacities, legal exposure, and digital security.
- **Organisational Profiling:** Produce standardized organizational profiles detailing institutional readiness, technical appetite, and risk profiles for all interviewed entities.
- **Shortlisting & Validation Session:** Develop a prioritized shortlist of candidate partner organizations with documented rationale; present findings at the Beirut Validation Session.

## **Key Deliverables**

1. Detailed Data Access & Platform Inventory Report.
2. Comprehensive interview notes and 12–15 standardized Organizational Profiles.
3. Final Ecosystem Mapping Report containing the prioritized candidate shortlist, selection rationale, and risk matrix.
4. Presentation materials for the Beirut Ecosystem Validation Session.

## **Qualifications & Requirements**

- Advanced degree in Journalism, Media Studies, Sociology, Political Science, or Governance.
- Minimum 7 years of experience mapping Lebanese media landscape, civil society networks, or civic technology ecosystems.
- Demonstrated track record in qualitative research, stakeholder interviewing, and technical baseline studies.
- Native Arabic speaker with fluent English writing skills.

**Hours:** You will be required to work the hours as are necessary for the proper discharge of the duties with the notional requirement being 35 hours per working week. Work will normally be undertaken in office hours, Monday to Friday, but weekend and evening working will be required

**Remuneration:** Up to £52,890 GBP gross per annual (dependent on experience)

**Duration:** 12 months, with the possibility of extension subject to funding

**Location:** Manchester, UK (hybrid working available), with an expectation of up to 80% international travel/deployment as required by UK-Med. *(Open to candidates based in the UK or internationally, with a preference for UK-based candidates due to operational considerations.)*

**We are seeking a highly experienced Medical Doctor with specialist expertise in infectious diseases, outbreak preparedness and response, alongside a strong background in international humanitarian health, to provide senior technical leadership across UK-Med's emergency health programmes and responses.**

UK-Med is a frontline humanitarian medical NGO, delivering life-saving healthcare in emergencies and strengthening health systems in some of the world’s most challenging environments. As a key partner of the UK Emergency Medical Team (UK EMT), we work closely with the UK Government, WHO, Ministries of Health and international partners to respond rapidly when crises strike.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced humanitarian clinician with a strong background in outbreak management and a broader understanding of emergency healthcare delivery across all-hazard humanitarian settings. Our teams have responded to some of the world's most complex crises, including conflicts, disease outbreaks, natural disasters and public health emergencies. Current and recent programmes have included humanitarian responses in Gaza, Ukraine and Sudan, alongside infectious disease preparedness and response activities in countries such as DRC.

The successful candidate will provide senior clinical and technical leadership across UK-Med's humanitarian responses, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, outbreak preparedness and response. Reporting to the Deputy Health Director with oversight of the Health Director, you will provide technical guidance and mentoring to UK-Med's deployed Medical Coordinators and register members, helping to ensure safe, effective and high-quality healthcare across our programmes. You will also line manage the Health Department’s Outbreak Referrents and contribute to response planning, clinical governance, technical standards, programme development and organisational preparedness.

Whilst the core specialist function of the role is outbreak response, this is a broader humanitarian health leadership role. You will be expected to support and deploy to a range of emergency settings. These may include conflict-affected areas, natural disasters, disease outbreaks and other complex humanitarian environments. Deployments may be at short notice, involve rapid health assessments, establishing or strengthening healthcare services, providing senior technical and clinical leadership, supporting multidisciplinary teams and addressing operational gaps where required. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a supportive and collaborative working environment and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to humanitarian health outcomes worldwide.

Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified **Liaison and Partnership officer**.

## **About the job**

The Liaison and Partnership Officer supports DRC's access, operations, and partnerships across East (and South Libya when needed), under the line management of the Country Director and the technical supervision of the Partnerships Coordinator. This includes helping to build and maintain relationships with local authorities, civil society actors, humanitarian partners, and community leaders to support current and future programming.

The role requires a strong communicator who can navigate administrative systems and foster collaboration to support humanitarian goals, and who supports partner mapping, contract/sub-grant agreement (SGA) tracking, documentation and field follow-up in close coordination with the Partnerships Coordinator.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**1. Liaison and Representation**

- Serve as a focal point with local authorities including ministries and municipalities, and relevant entities in East and South Libya.
- Facilitate approvals, permits, and coordination required for operations, staff movement, and program implementation.
- Represent DRC in relevant coordination meetings and stakeholder forums to promote organizational interests and ensure alignment with local frameworks.
- Monitor and interpret local administrative and context developments that may impact operations.
- Jointly with DRC's partnership unit, liaise with sub-grant partners to ensure the process is clear and all documents are received and updated on the system.
- Demonstrate competencies in drafting official letters in both languages (Arabic and English).

**2. Operational and Program Support**

- Support field teams in obtaining timely approvals for program activities, site access, and logistical facilitation.
- Assist in resolving access challenges, bureaucratic bottlenecks, and operational impediments.
- Coordinate with logistics, security, and program teams to ensure smooth field operations and staff deployments.

**3. Engagement and Entry Point Analysis**

- Identify and assess opportunities for expanding or initiating programming in under-served or priority areas.
- Provide contextual analysis, local dynamics, and potential partners or entry points.
- Support needs assessments, field visits, and donor missions by organizing meetings and access arrangements with local actors.

**4. Partner Mapping, Contract and SGA Tracking**

- Support the mapping and regular updating of information on current and potential partner organizations (national/local NGOs and CSOs) operating in the area of coverage.
- Maintain and update the partnership database/tracker, ensuring partner profiles, capacity information and contact details are accurate and up to date.
- Ensure proper filing and archiving of partnership-related documents (MoUs, agreements, amendments, assessments, correspondence) in line with DRC's document management procedures.
- Maintain an up-to-date tracker of partner agreements/SGAs, including start and end dates, budget lines, deliverables and reporting deadlines.
- Follow up with partners and relevant internal teams on the status of agreement modifications, amendments, no-cost extensions and renewals, flagging any delays to the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Support the collection and compilation of documentation required for partner selection, due diligence and capacity assessment processes.

**5. Field Monitoring and Partner Follow-up**

- Support field visits to partner-implemented activities to follow up on progress against agreed targets and identify implementation challenges.
- Follow up on partners' compliance with agreement commitments and action points arising from monitoring visits, review meetings and audits.
- Document field visit findings and share reports/updates with the Country Director, relevant teams and the Partnerships Coordinator.

**6. Reporting and Documentation**

- Maintain records of key meetings, communications, and agreements with stakeholders.
- Support drafting of MoUs with partners, routing them for review and validation, and following up until finalization.
- Provide regular updates and analysis on access, coordination, and liaison matters to senior management.
- Contribute to reporting requirements for donors, clusters, and internal management as needed.
- Support the collection and follow-up of partner and community feedback related to partnership activities.
- Contribute inputs to internal partnership reports, trackers and dashboards for the Country Director and the Partnerships Coordinator.
- Flag any irregularities, compliance concerns or incidents identified during field visits or partner engagement to the line and technical manager.

**Note:** this job description must remain flexible, to respond to additional tasks or changes as identified by the line and/or technical manager.

## **About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have At least 2-3 years of relevant experience in humanitarian or development sectors, with exposure to liaison, coordination, external relations or partnership/grants support functions.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

**Required**

- Strong understanding of the context and humanitarian landscape in East and South Libya.
- Experience engaging with local authorities, community leaders, and civil society actors.
- Experience maintaining trackers/databases and working with Excel or similar tools for data and document tracking.
- Excellent communication, negotiation, cultural sensitivity, and interpersonal skills.
- Willingness to travel frequently and work in dynamic field environments.

**Desirable:**

- Experience working with both government and INGOs and/or UN agencies in a liaison role.
- Prior experience in access negotiation, humanitarian coordination, or partnership/grant support.
- Knowledge of humanitarian principles and operational standards; knowledge of donor compliance basics is an asset.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

## **We offer**

- Contract length: Open Ended Contract
- Band: NMH2
- Designation of Duty Station: Benghazi Based (with regular travel to South and West of Libya plus Tunis when needed)
- Suggested Start date: 01 Nov 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Us.

## **Application process**

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV (no longer than four pages) in English. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Closing date for applications: 27 October 2026**

For further information about the Danish Refugee Council, please consult our website [drc.ngo](https://drc.ngo/).

jobs.title: ICLA Project Manager CAR Bouar
jobs.description:
**Contexte**

La République centrafricaine continue de faire face à d’importants besoins humanitaires, de protection et de relèvement, résultant de plusieurs années de conflit, de déplacements de populations et d’un accès limité aux services de base. NRC est présent en RCA depuis 2014 et continue de mettre en œuvre ses programmes à travers une présence réduite mais stratégique.

Les principaux secteurs programmatiques qui seront renforcés au cours de la prochaine période comprennent **l’Information, le Conseil et l’Assistance juridique (ICLA), l’Éducation, les Abris et l’Eau, l’Hygiène et l’Assainissement (WASH), ainsi que la Protection contre la violence (PfV)**.

**Le programme ICLA** est au cœur de l’action du NRC en RCA. Il vise à renforcer la protection juridique des personnes déplacées internes, retournées ou affectées par des crises, en facilitant leur accès aux droits liés au Logement, à la Terre et à la Propriété (LTP), à l’identité juridique, tout en soutenant la prévention et la résolution pacifique des conflits fonciers. En RCA, ces enjeux sont particulièrement critiques en raison de la complexité des systèmes fonciers, de la faiblesse des mécanismes de sécurité d’occupation, des risques d’expulsions forcées et du manque de reconnaissance juridique des documents essentiels. Dans ce cadre, NRC joue un rôle de premier plan en tant que Lead au sein du Groupe de travail Logement, Terre et Propriété (LTP), coordonné au sein du nouveau Cluster SLSC. NRC joue également un rôle clé dans le cadre du processus de redynamisation de la plateforme nationale de coordination de l’état civil en RCA.

Dans le contexte de la transition RCA–Cameroun, NRC passera d’un modèle de bureau pays autonome en RCA à une présence opérationnelle intégrée sous la responsabilité du bureau pays du Cameroun. Cette transition représente une adaptation du modèle opérationnel visant à maintenir une présence ciblée, conforme aux exigences de NRC et orientée vers les programmes, tout en améliorant l’efficacité des coûts, la supervision et la durabilité.

Afin de contribuer à répondre aux défis de protection et de garantir la continuité d’une mise en œuvre efficace et de qualité de ses projets, NRC recrute un(e) Responsable de Projet ICLA, en appui aux opérations terrain en RCA et dans la façade Est du Cameroun.

**Ce que nous cherchons**

Le/la Project Manager ICLA est chargé(e) de la mise en œuvre de la stratégique opérationnelle et technique du programme d’Information, Conseil et Assistance Juridique (ICLA) en RCA et dans la façade Est du Cameroun en appui au projet SOLID II si confirmé. Il/elle est responsable de la planification, de la mise en œuvre, du suivi et du reporting des activités ICLA conformément aux standards de qualité, aux lignes directrices de NRC, ainsi qu’aux exigences des bailleurs. En étroite collaboration avec les spécialistes techniques et sous la supervision du Responsable de Programme de zone/Area Programme Manager, il/elle encadre les équipes ICLA sur le terrain, renforce leurs capacités et garantit la pertinence, l’impact et la conformité des interventions. Ses responsabilités couvrent notamment deux des domaines de compétence clés du programme ICLA, à savoir les droits liés au logement, à la terre et à la propriété (LTP), ainsi que l'identité juridique.

**1.Rôles et responsabilités**

1. Assurer la gestion hiérarchique du personnel de projet, y compris le recrutement, et veiller au bon encadrement des équipes.
2. Le processus de gestion de la performance; définir des objectifs clairs alignés sur la stratégie et les priorités de la mission, puis assurer le suivi et l’appui nécessaires pour permettre au personnel d’atteindre ces objectifs.
3. Être responsable des processus clés tels que la planification des effectifs, le recrutement, l’intégration et le développement du personnel, et veiller au respect du devoir de protection (*Duty of Care*) envers son propre personnel.
4. Contribuer à l’élaboration des stratégies pays, de zone et du programme ICLA ; initier et participer au développement des projets pertinents dans le domaine ICLA. 2.
5. Mettre en œuvre les projets ICLA dans les zones concernées, en garantissant une qualité technique élevée, conforme aux stratégies ICLA en RCA et assurant des synergies avec les autres compétences sectorielles.
6. Appuyer la préparation des propositions de projets (aspects techniques, financiers et narratifs) pour les zones d’intervention et le bureau pays.
7. Développer, gérer et suivre les budgets conformément au Manuel financier du NRC et aux exigences des bailleurs, en coordination avec le Responsable de programme de zone et les coordinateurs ICLA.
8. Fournir des rapports d’avancement réguliers au Responsable de programme de zone, au Responsable de zone et au Spécialiste ICLA, en mettant en avant les réussites et les défis opérationnels.
9. Évaluer, revoir et assurer le contrôle qualité des projets ICLA en cours et achevés dans la zone concernée.
10. Veiller à ce que les projets ciblent les bénéficiaires ayant les besoins de protection les plus urgents ; identifier et proposer des approches plus efficaces d’assistance.
11. Renforcer les capacités du personnel du projet et des partenaires et assurer le transfert des compétences clés.
12. Représenter ICLA dans les forums internes et externes; développer des partenariats au sein de la communauté humanitaire dans la zone concernée et coordonner avec les autorités locales.

**2.Compétences**

**Compétences professionnelles**

- Diplôme de Master (BAC+4/5) minimum en sciences sociales, droit ou tout autre domaine pertinent des sciences humaines.
- Minimum de 3 ans d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le domaine d’expertise ICLA.
- Solides connaissances techniques du secteur humanitaire.
- Expérience préalable dans des contextes complexes et instables.
- Capacité avérée à travailler de manière autonome dans un environnement multiculturel, multitâche et orienté vers les résultats.
- Expérience dans les programmes d’assistance juridique et/ou de droits humains, avec une bonne compréhension des enjeux de protection et des compétences liées aux responsabilités du poste.
- Expérience dans la gestion d’équipe.
- Maîtrise des applications Microsoft.
- Excellente maîtrise du français, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit.
- La connaissance de l’anglais constitue un atout.

***Compétences techniques et expériences spécifiques requises***

- Connaissance du contexte de la RCA, de la dynamique des mouvements et besoins humanitaires en présence le long de la frontière avec le Cameroun (Façade Est)
- Expérience dans les processus de réforme légale en RCA dans le cadre de l’identité juridique et sur le foncier
- Expérience en matière de genre et d’intégration de la dimension genre dans la mise en œuvre des projets.
- Expérience avérée dans les domaines de la protection et du plaidoyer, notamment dans le cadre du programme ICLA ou d’assistance juridique ou d’un programme similaire.
- Solide expérience dans la mise en œuvre de réponses ICLA, tant en contexte volatile que de relèvement.
- Expérience confirmée en gestion des projets liés à l’assistance juridique, aux droits fonciers et à la documentation civile suivant une dimension transfrontalière notamment avec le Cameroun
- Expérience de travail avec des bailleurs de fonds et maîtrise de leurs cadres techniques, priorités stratégiques et exigences en matière de rapports (ex. : ECHO, UE, NORAD, SIDA, etc.).
- Compréhension approfondie des processus de suivi-évaluation (M&E) et capacité à concevoir et adapter des outils pertinents au contexte.
- Expérience dans la production des outils de visibilité et de capitalisation des réalisations du programme
- Expérience dans la conduite d’évaluations multisectorielles et d’analyses contextuelles.
- Aptitude à travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes terrain et intersectorielles.
- Excellentes compétences en communication, représentation, flexibilité et négociation.
- Capacité démontrée à transmettre des connaissances à des publics variés, à travers des formations, du mentorat et d’autres méthodes formelles ou informelles.
- Sensibilité aux dynamiques politiques et culturelles.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Capacité à travailler en équipe.
- Aptitude à évoluer dans des environnements sécuritaires instables.
- Réflexion stratégique.
- Capacité à responsabiliser les autres et à instaurer la confiance.
- Proactivité et capacité à initier des changements.
- Esprit d’analyse.

***Profil de leadership***

- Construire des relations solides et significatives
- Agir avec intégrité
- Donner aux équipes les moyens d’agir
- Obtenir des résultats

Veuillez trouver la [JD - ICLA PM CAR Bouar.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQD1k3mu8bRfSoq1o5kwVXoCAYV-HFIKbnyJLFk31OrV-c8?e=EQ5OUU)

**Ce que nous offrons**

- **Contrat National**: CDD de 12 mois
- NRC échelle: 8
- Lieu d’affectation: Bouar, CAR
- Une chance de rencontrer et de travailler avec des personnes qui sont les meilleures dans leur domaine.

\*\* **Ce poste est réservé aux candidat(e)s de nationalité centrafricaine\*\***

[Apprenez sur les avantages de travailler avec NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

**Informations importantes:**

- Pour postuler en tant que candidat interne, connectez-vous avec votre adresse électronique officielle ou cliquez sur Opportunity MarketPlace.
- Lors de la création de votre profil, indiquez votre nom complet tel qu'indiqué sur votre passeport.
- Remplissez tous les champs requis par le système concernant l’expérience, les antécédents professionnels et l’éducation.
- Déposez votre candidature et votre CV en français ou en anglais, en prenant soin de joindre votre dernier CV.
- Les candidatures ne répondant pas aux normes minimales en termes d’expérience ou de qualifications ne seront généralement pas prises en considération. Les candidatures spontanées non liées à cette offre d'emploi spécifique ne seront pas prises en compte.
- Seuls les candidats sélectionnés seront contactés. Nous recevons de nombreuses candidatures pour chaque poste vacant.
- Si vous avez des questions sur ce rôle, veuillez envoyer un e-mail à cwa.recruitment@nrc.no avec le titre du poste comme objet.

**Pourquoi NRC?**

Le Conseil norvégien pour les réfugiés (NRC) est une organisation humanitaire indépendante qui vient en aide aux personnes contraintes de fuir. Nos 15 000 collaborateurs travaillent lors de crises dans 40 pays, apportant chaque année une assistance vitale et à long terme à des millions de personnes.

Regardez [cette courte vidéo](https://vimeo.com/736782633) pour voir NRC en action.

Nous recherchons des personnes passionnées par l’aide aux réfugiés et aux personnes contraintes de fuir. Êtes-vous une de ces personnes? Si tel est le cas, NRC vous offre la possibilité de :

- effectuer un travail exigeant et professionnel, souvent dans des contextes difficiles
- rejoignez une culture de travail qui permet à chaque employé de partager des idées et d'assumer ses responsabilités
- faire partie d’une communauté accueillante et solidaire engagée envers la dignité humaine

jobs.title: Watsan Mobile Support Specialist (MSS)
jobs.description:
## **MSF Ubuntu is looking for a Watsan Mobile Support Specialist (MSS)**

*Do your skills and experience not precisely match the requirements? At MSF EA, we strive to create a safe, diverse and inclusive workplace, recognising the need to increase access to professional opportunities for historically underrepresented groups. If you're interested in this position but your experience doesn't align perfectly with the selection criteria, we encourage you to apply anyway. You might be the ideal candidate for this or other positions.*

*Firmly committed to safeguarding patients, community members, staff, and all those in contact with the organisation from all forms of abuse, including sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), we will take all necessary steps, through rigorous vetting processes, to ensure that confirmed perpetrators of abuse do not join the organization.*

*For this position, contact level with patients and children is categorized as **Low** risk and will be monitored with this in regard.*

## ***Introduction***

Médecins Sans Frontières/Doctors Without Borders (MSF) is an international independent medical humanitarian organisation that provides assistance to people affected by conflicts, epidemics, and natural or human-made disasters and excluded from healthcare. We provide this assistance without discrimination, irrespective of race, religion, creed or political affiliation.

## ***About MSF Ubuntu***

**MSF Ubuntu** is the newest Operational Directorate of Médecins Sans Frontières, grounded in the philosophy of Ubuntu – “I am because we are”. With a strong emphasis on interdependence, interoperability, and locally grounded action, MSF Ubuntu aims to strengthen medical humanitarian response by placing communities at the centre of decision-making.

## ***Rationale/Objective for Position***

The Watsan MSS is the technical focal point for Water Supply, Hygiene, Sanitation and Vector Control (WHS and VC) within the Med-Ops Cell. S/he provides 1st and 2nd line (remote and/or in person) technical support to MSF Ubuntu country programs within their Med-Ops Cell, covering both operational implementation of activities and the strategic definition of Watsan approaches and priorities across the portfolio, in line with the Logistics & Watsan Strategy.

The role supports country programme staff in the design, planning, implementation and review of Watsan interventions, ensuring that programme proposals are technically sound, context-appropriate, and aligned with MSF protocols, standards and procedures, the MSF Ubuntu Strategic Plan, including Med-Ops programming priorities, and the Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028.

The Watsan MSS contributes to capacity building of country programme staff through the application and transfer of technical know-how, to strengthen programme quality, support country programs in optimal working conditions and maximize the impact of MSF Ubuntu's projects.

This position will be ***hierarchically*** accountable to the ***Cell Logistics & Supply Advisor*** and ***functionally*** accountable to the **Watsan Technical Coordinator** and **Deputy Med-Ops Cell Manager (Med)** – joint functional line.

## ***Tasks & Responsibilities***

- Following up the Watsan activities in her/his portfolio countries within the Med-Ops cell.
- Reporting systematically on progress in implementing the MSF Ubuntu Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028, the application of related policies and performance against Watsan KPIs, to inform strategic and operational decisions.
- Ensuring understanding and alignment of the Watsan interventions with MSF Ubuntu priorities and standards, as per MSF Ubuntu’s Strategic Plan, including the “Logistics/Watsan Basics” minimum standard.
- Supporting and guiding the definition and the revision of the Watsan strategy for the country programs, in line with the MSF Ubuntu Logistics & Watsan Strategy 2026–2028 and medical priorities and advising on current and future medical and logistics operations when pertinent.
- Carrying out a functional evaluation of the Watsan set-up, assessing the applicable technical installations, systems, structures, equipment and HR set-up, the compliance with procedures, policies and guidelines, within the framework of MSF standards to identify the main areas for improvement.
- Assessing and validating local suppliers and local (sub-)contractors for quality of materials, systems, installations, parts etc. to ensure compliance with MSF quality standards.
- Developing and initiating the implementation of the improvement plan based on the recommendations arising from the functional evaluation.
- Assisting the logistics team with the design and installation of new (complex) systems and/or with the implementation of (new) protocols, tools etc.
- Monitoring and supervising established and ongoing work, systems and installations in the field of expertise and providing technical advice and solutions when necessary.
- Assisting the logistics team in their HR tasks such as recruitment & selection of technical staff, briefing and debriefing of focal persons and logisticians.
- Identifying training needs and contributing to the definition of training content for WHS and VC.
- Facilitating team training and providing on-the-job training on technical basics related to area of specialization according to MSF standards to enable effective implementation of relevant methodologies, systems and tools and ensure best practice is delivered.
- Upon request of the Watsan Technical Coordinator and in coordination with the Cell Logistics & Supply Advisor and Deputy Med-Ops Cell Manager, develop new policies, tools, protocols and SOPs related to his/her area of expertise (with a local, regional or even global approach).
- Drafting reports and action plans following field visits to capture experiences and “lessons learnt”.
- Contributing to the research and development of programme tools, practices, guidelines and policies based on insights gained in the job.
- Proposing and testing/piloting innovative solutions to overcome recurrent problems and technical challenges.
- Developing and maintaining knowledge of practices and approaches within the area of expertise and sharing this knowledge with others to enhance operational effectiveness.
- Carrying out field visits to the portfolio countries as needed or requested by the programme teams.
- Close collaboration with the IPC MIO advisor in relevant areas related to WASH and IPC, in line with MSF policies and standards.
- Participating in the Med-Ops Cell Health Programme Support Team (HSTP) meetings on a regular basis, ensuring a strong link and collaboration between medical and logistics strategies and priorities.
- Supporting emergency/outbreak WASH response primarily within their Med-Ops Cell portfolio; extending support to other Cells only upon request from the Head of Logistics or activation of the MSF Ubuntu Emergency Response Strategy.
- Ensuring WASH facilities and services are designed for privacy, gender-appropriateness, accessibility and safe usage, and are aligned with MSF Ubuntu's safeguarding and community-accountability approach .
- Mapping and engaging local WASH actors — public, community-based and private — in the portfolio, and contributing to targeted WASH partnerships for operational delivery where these strengthen or complement existing local systems .
- Acting as the Med-Ops Cell focal point and technical reference for Watsan, ensuring coherent, timely and context-appropriate technical guidance to country programmes across the portfolio.
- Reviewing and advising on country programme proposals, intervention designs and operational plans related to Watsan, to ensure technical quality, feasibility, relevance and alignment with MSF Ubuntu priorities, standards and strategies.
- Contributing to strategic discussions and decision-making within the Med-Ops Cell on Watsan priorities, approaches and operational orientations for the portfolio countries.

## ***Qualifications***

**Education**

- Essential: Degree in civil engineering, environmental sciences, environmental health, public health engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.
- Desirable: Postgraduate qualification in water and sanitation, public health, or humanitarian studies.
- Essential: Sphere Watsan standards; water treatment and quality testing; excreta and wastewater management; healthcare waste management; community Watsan methodologies; vector control principles.
- Desirable: MSF Watsan protocols and tools; GIS and EPANET.

**Experience**

- Essential: Minimum 2 years of NGO Watsan field experience; community and HCF Watsan, outbreak response; adult training facilitation; ability to work in remote and insecure settings.
- Desirable: MSF Watsan experience; EASTEN and southern Africa Experience in Watsan interventions or infrastructure design in climate-vulnerable or climate-affected contexts.

**Languages**

- Essential: English (fluent written and spoken).
- Desirable: French.

**Competencies**

- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Collaboration
- Flexibility
- Intercultural Sensitivity

***Conditions and Benefits:***

- The role requires regular travel to countries of operation and MSF Ubuntu hubs.
- Travel at short notice may be required during emergencies, assessments or critical incidents.
- The post-holder may be required to work extended or irregular hours during crises.
- The role requires high levels of discretion, resilience, political judgement and emotional intelligence.
- The position will operate in a growing Operational Directorate and will require adaptability as MSF Ubuntu’s structures, systems and portfolio evolve.
- **Job Location**: This position will be based in one of the countries within its portfolio (to be confirmed). For the initial two years, the duty station is expected to be in Harare (Zimbabwe), Johannesburg (South Africa), or Nairobi (Kenya). After two years, the successful candidate accepts flexibility to move to the final duty station, that is still to be confirmed.
- **Contract**: 1 year (renewable) full-time contract.
- **Start date**: As Soon As Possible.
- **Annual Salary and other benefits**: In line with MSF reward policy, Subjected to local conditions.

**If based in Nairobi, the benefits below shall apply:**

- **Salary:** An annual salary of **EUR 27,145 at HQ Grade 8** based on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- **Work-life balance financial benefit;** ranging between **EUR 620 to 1,159/month** based on individual & administrative status. This amount may be used to cover accommodation and utilities, transportation, etc.
- **Other benefits include;**
- **Annual Leave:** 25 days of annual leave per year.
- **Other Holidays:** sick leave, circumstantial leave, maternity leave (21 weeks), paternity leave (4 weeks), own affairs days off, etc.
- **Employer Pension contribution**: 10% of basic salary:
- **International insurance** for both medical and disability**.**
- **Relocation support**; based on MSF EA terms/conditions.
- **Work-life balance**: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- **School fees benefits**: for eligible dependents, based on individual & administrative status.
- **Diverse team composition**; Collaborate with a global network of talented professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world.
- **Career Development**: MSF provides many learning resources (online learning resources, regular trainings – including language, Peer to peer learning.
- **Mobility**: You will have opportunities to travel abroad for work, meetings, trainings and workshops; giving you a chance to experience different cultures and broaden your professional network.
- **Annual home leave ticket**: To be taken once every year for both staff and eligible dependents back to their home country for vacation. Only applicable to non-Kenyans and based on individual & administrative status.

**If based in Johannesburg, the benefits below shall apply:**

- **Salary:** An annual salary of **ZAR 520,889 at HQ Grade 7 based** on a full-time appointment with an annual increment of 2% every year up to a maximum of 10 years.
- 13th Cheque in November.
- 100% Medical aid contribution.
- 10% additional pension allowance.
- Transport allowance.
- Cell Phone Allowance.
- Work-life balance: Daily flexi-hours and 2 days working from home possible.
- Diverse team composition; Collaborate with a global network of talented
professionals, bringing diverse perspectives and expertise from around the world
- Resources needed such as working space, computer, internet, stationery, and other resources will be made available.

6\. Être responsable des ressources du bureau de terrain, y compris les responsabilités de gestionnaire budgétaire pour les lignes budgétaires du bureau de terrain (programme et soutien), les achats et la gestion des actifs.

7\. Veiller à la mise en œuvre rapide, efficace et de qualité des opérations sur le terrain, conformément aux politiques et procédures de la NRC.

8\. Diriger la gestion de la sécurité au sein du bureau de terrain, y compris les négociations d’accès, les évaluations des risques et la mise en œuvre des procédures d’accès humanitaire et de sécurité.

9\. Veiller à la mise en œuvre effective du devoir de diligence de la NRC et des mécanismes de responsabilité envers le personnel et les populations touchées sur le terrain.

10\. Veiller au respect et à l’application des politiques, des directives et des procédures de la NRC.

jobs.title: Chief of Party – ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions
jobs.description:
**What we’re looking for:**

NRC is seeking an experienced **Chief of Party to lead the ‘Catalyst Fund’ for Locally Led Humanitarian Response & Solutions,** an ambitious new initiative transforming how humanitarian assistance is financed and delivered.

You will provide strategic leadership across countries, partners and workstreams, driving programme delivery, locally led partnerships, learning and humanitarian systems change. The Fund aims to strengthen local leadership in neglected displacement crises, initially in Africa, by combining rapid, flexible emergency response with locally led recovery, protection and sustainable pathways to solutions.

Beyond immediate impact, you will help shape a scalable model that strengthens local systems, promotes self-reliance, and influences wider humanitarian financing, policy and practice. The role is expected to begin with a six-month inception phase to establish the Fund’s operational model, partnerships, governance and learning systems, subject to final approval.

The ideal candidate must have a strong understanding of NRC’s internal systems, processes, and operational context.

**What you will do:**

**Strategy**

- Set the strategic direction of the Fund and ensure the effective functioning of its activation, assurance and accompaniment arrangements across all levels of governance and implementation.
- Working closely with the donor(s) and the Fund's governing bodies, develop and implement the Fund's multi-year strategy, including its results matrix, control measures and key performance indicators.
- Accountable for robust risk mapping of Fund activities and implementation of appropriate risk mitigation measures.
- Responsible for monitoring and reporting on progress against strategic objectives and KPIs to NRC leadership, donors, and the Fund's governing bodies.
- Co-responsible (with NRC Management and the donor) for identifying and developing additional funding opportunities and co-donor partnerships to grow the Fund.
- Responsible for the Fund's transition/continuity planning, including succession from the inception-phase support arrangements.

**Fund Management Team**

- Ensure the Fund has the appropriate capacity and expertise required for effective delivery, and lead/support the recruitment of dedicated Fund positions.
- Provide strategic and functional leadership to staff and functions supporting the Fund, through line management, and/or functional relationships, as appropriate to the final organisational set-up.
- Establish effective working relationships with relevant NRC functions and teams, including the Emergency Response, Operational Support and Governance, and Global Programme Sections, ensuring coherent and timely support to the Fund across programme, grants, partnerships, finance, MEAL, learning, communications, policy and advocacy, and other relevant functions.
- Maintain effective coordination with external or shared functions supporting the Fund, including the ICVA Local Coordination Adviser, as relevant.
- Budget holder for the Fund, managing its budget, assets and resources.
- Responsible for the review and submission of quality donor reports (programmatic and financial), evaluations, audits, and partner agreements/awards.
- Ensure Fund functions (grants, finance, MEAL, communications, learning) provide effective and timely support to country teams and partners.
- Ensure effective risk management, compliance and mitigation across the Fund Facility.
- Accountable for the Fund's legal and regulatory compliance, including donor agreements and relations with the donor.

**Governance**

- Convene and service the Fund's governing bodies (Steering Committee/Board), ensuring agreed courses of action are implemented, reported on and monitored.
- Responsible for presenting the Fund's roll-out and delivery to the Steering Committee/Board and participate in board discussions as the Fund's representative.

**Delivery**

- Review and sign off on Fund activations and awards, ensuring adherence to the Fund's proportionate due diligence and assurance model.
- Responsible for ensuring high-quality implementation of Fund-supported responses, and accountable for control measures for monitoring delivery, in coordination with the roving staff deployed and country-level structures.
- Ensure close coordination with Country Office management teams in the delivery of the response.
- Ensure that NRC policies on safeguarding, Safe and Inclusive Programming and community engagement, and equitable partnerships are upheld in the delivery of the response
- Ensure effective coordination with relevant NRC technical and thematic functions, drawing on their expertise and quality assurance to support delivery of the Fund's humanitarian response, localisation and solutions objectives.

**Representation, Learning and System Change**

- Represent the Fund with external stakeholders (the donor(s), other donors, UN agencies, INGOs, local actors, coordination bodies such as ICVA), with the aim of advancing the Fund's strategic objectives and catalysing buy-in from key stakeholders.
- Working with the Global Learning Advisor, drive the Fund's Learning Agenda, ensuring learning is captured and used to influence humanitarian policy, financing and coordination practice in support of locally led approaches.

Please download a more detailed[ **JOB DESCRIPTION**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAJ-eEOULz8QL83qm6OBgM0AW43y3fnlgu7FkFqncRmupo?e=yLbQDq) for more specific duties and responsibilities.

**What you will bring:**

- Minimum 7 years' experience in a senior management role (e.g. Country Director, Head of Programmes, Fund/Grant Facility Director) in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Strong understanding of NRC’s internal systems, processes and operational context.
- Proven experience managing humanitarian pooled funds, grant facilities, or complex multi-partner consortia.
- Experience in localisation and locally-led humanitarian response approaches.
- Effective communication, interpersonal, facilitation and diplomatic skills, including the professional credibility to provide coordination and guidance to a multi-disciplinary global team.
- Documented results related to the position's responsibilities.
- Fluency in English , both written and verbal, with strong writing and editing skills.
- Prior expertise in Sub-Saharan Africa displacement contexts is an advantage.
- French language skills are an advantage, given the Fund's initial geographic focus.
- Prior experience with fund facility programmes, or similarly structured multi-donor mechanisms, is an advantage.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: NRC’s HO in Oslo, Rep Offices in Berlin, Brussels and London, as well Employer of Records (EoR) listed countries. The position could also be hosted in Dakar and/or Nairobi on a Resident contract.
- Contract: 24 months
- Travel: Up to 40%.
- Salary/benefits: grade 11 on NRC’s Resident/National salary scale, with accompanying terms and conditions.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[*Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC*](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

**Hours:** You will be required to work the hours as are necessary for the proper discharge of the duties with the notional requirement being 35 hours per working week. Work will normally be undertaken in office hours, Monday to Friday, but weekend and evening working will be required

**We are seeking an experienced Medical Doctor or Registered Nurse with significant expertise in international humanitarian responses, including conflict, disasters and/or public health emergencies, to provide expert technical leadership across UK-Med's growing portfolio of emergency health programmes.**

UK-Med is a frontline humanitarian medical NGO, delivering life-saving healthcare in emergencies and strengthening health systems in some of the world’s most challenging environments. As a key partner of the UK Emergency Medical Team (UK EMT), we work closely with the UK Government, WHO, Ministries of Health and international partners to respond rapidly when crises strike.

This is a unique opportunity for a highly experienced humanitarian health professional, with a medical or nursing background, who is passionate about emergency response and willing to deploy internationally in support of UK-Med's operations. Our teams have responded to some of the world's most complex humanitarian crises, including conflicts, disease outbreaks, natural disasters and public health emergencies. Current and recent programmes have included conflict responses in Ukraine, Gaza and Sudan, as well as support to Ebola preparedness and response activities in DRC, and disaster responses in countries including Venezuela.

The successful candidate will play a key role in shaping humanitarian health programmes, providing technical expertise, supporting programme design and strategy, contributing to funding proposals and deploying overseas to provide leadership to multidisciplinary health teams when required.

You will bring significant experience in emergency and humanitarian health, strong technical credibility and the ability to work effectively with health authorities, WHO and international partners in complex and fast-moving environments. Join us and be part of a passionate, purpose-driven organisation making a real difference where healthcare is needed most.

We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a supportive and collaborative working environment, and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to humanitarian health outcomes worldwide. UK-Med is a dynamic and ambitious organisation with a dedicated team of staff, volunteers and Register members committed to delivering high-quality healthcare where it is needed most.
