Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Directrice Régionale des Opérations du Pool Afrique de l'Ouest, Australe et de la Mission France, vous contribuez à la définition et au développement de la stratégie des bureaux pays d'ACF. En étroite collaboration avec les directeurs-trices pays, les directeurs-trices adjoint programmes et l'équipe du pool que vous encadrez. Vous accompagnez la mise en oeuvre des orientations stratégiques et le développement des activités.
Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront de :
Manager l'équipe du Pool sous son rattachement hiérarchique
recruter les membres de l'équipe en lien avec les référent.es fonctionnement et le département RH du siège
assurer la gestion quotidienne de l'équipe
fixer les priorités, veiller au respect des règles internes et à la bonne interaction entre les membres de l'équipe
initier et suivre les plans d'actions individuels de l'équipe
assurer les entretiens d'évaluation
organiser des points individuels avec les membres de l'équipe
Accompagner la définition et la mise en oeuvre des stratégies pays
Co-animer la réflexion stratégique (programmatique et budgétaire) avec le DRO entre les missions et le pool
S'assurer de compatibilité et d ela cohérence des programmes à fort enjeux stratégiques avec les stratégies pays
Apporter appui et conseil aux missions sur les stratégies de financement
s'assurer de l'organisation des évaluations externes des programmes
en accord avec le DRO, exercer un rôle et des responsabilités directes sur la mission
Accompagner la définition et faciliter le financement de programmes régionaux, multi-pays, multi-acteurs à fort enjeux stratégiques
Conseiller les bureaux pays dans l'élaboration de nouveaux programmes en fonction des besoins
contribuer à la coordination du réseau ACF-IN
Contribuer au recrutement et au développement des RH dans sa filière métier (DPA programmes, grant writer,..)
Valider techniquement les candidatures des directeurs-trices pays adjoint programmes, responsables de département programmes et coordinateur-trice de consortium
assurer les briefings et debriefings des membres de la coordination
assurer le suivi régulier, l'accompagnement et le support aux DPA programmes.
animer des sessions de formation au siège, en région, sur le terrain.

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master 2 en sciences sociales ou politiques ou équivalent. Vous avec au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle en mission humanitaire sur des postes de coordination dans les domaines d'activité d'ACF (Nutrition, Santé, Sécurité Alimentaire, Eau Assainissement Hygiène, Santé Mentale et Soutien Psychosocial ou fonctions Support).
Vous êtes reconnu-e pour vos qualités d'encadrement d'équipe et de leadership.
Votre connaissance de l'Afrique de l'Ouest et Australe, et/ou vos expériences terrains dans cette zone géographique sera un atout.
Vous maîtrisez l'ensemble des leviers des bailleurs institutionnels (écritures de propositions, financements, orientations, conformité).
Vous êtes autonome, diplomate et proactif-ve. Vous avez la capacité à porter une vision et à insuffler une dynamique d'équipe. Vous avez d'excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et orales en français et en anglais.

Conditions d'emploi

Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDD de 3 mois
Temps plein
Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)
Rémunération :De 47K à 52Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up): Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)
Télétravail :Télétravail ouvert à tous et toutes depuis le territoire métropolitain
Il a été défini pour ce poste une présence obligatoire au siège de 1 jour par mois
Temps de présentiels collectifs imposés / également obligatoires par l'employeur : pour les réunions et événements collectifs (jusqu'à 3 jours par mois) et 2 jours de présence obligatoire lors de votre intégration dans l'équipe
Indemnités de télétravail
Formation: Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning TalentSoft
Conditions particulières: Possible demande de déplacement (urgence, gap filler) et selon le contexte économique de l'organisation : Côte d'Ivoire, Libéria, Sierra Leone, Burkina Faso
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Analyst, METAL
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of seven teams which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Wellbeing, Governance, Health, Violence Prevention and Response, MEAL, and Grants & Operations.

**Measurement, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning.

**This is a hybrid position open to candidates based in New York, US, Kenya and UK. Other Limited IRC Locations may also be considered. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.**

**Job Overview**

The METAL Quality Assurance Analyst will be part of the METAL team which is responsible for delivering products that support day-to-day implementation of CRRD Programs as well as the collection, management, visualization of KPIs relevant to higher-level decision-making.

The QA Analyst is a team member responsible for developing, testing, implementing, and supporting CRRD’s data toolkits, for which the tech stack includes CommCare, Microsoft Power BI, and Microsoft SQL server Azure-based data warehouse.

The Data Toolkits are essential for CRRD’s data collection, management and analysis so it is critical for the success of the team that the QA Analyst have strong skills related to testing data transformation and visualization.

Working in partnership with staff at various levels and locations, the QA Analyst will perform a key role in testing, assuring quality, and improving Data Toolkits with a successful rollout. Should demonstrate a solid focus on responsive application design and an understanding of the diverse subject areas involved in developing user-centric and impactful applications.

Position key attributes are multi-tasking, detail orientation, fast learning, and self-organizing. The candidate is required to not only test the technology products, but also to identify, create, and implement complex use case scenarios; take a lead in efforts to find requirement/specification gaps and work very closely with business teams/analysts to seek answers. Find a balance between keeping high-quality standards without overly exerting on the release timeline. Build a good working relationship between development and product management teams. Be able to turn around testing and regression testing within timelines without compromising on quality.

This role reports to the Product Manager. Program Technology. The QA Analyst will work closely with METAL Developers. They will have a technical line to the Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and maintain regular contact with the QA team to ensure that METAL is following the best practices of the wider organization.

**Major Responsibilities**

Primary responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Translate functional requirements and specifications into detailed test plans, encompassing functional, system, integration, performance, regression, and user acceptance testing. The individual in this role will implement Agile Software Testing with Scrum principles.
- Work with the project management team closely to ensure that testing processes are implemented and followed by all core team members.
- Maintain high quality of applications developed in CommCare/Microsoft PowerApps meet user needs.
- Perform in-depth data testing of PowerBI dashboards and underlying data pipelines, including data verification across systems, data migration testing, data validation testing, and A/B testing, to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and quality of visualized data and the overall user experience.
- Review products to match design specifications, with an eye to user experience issues such as fonts, colors, and screen size breakpoints with responsive design.
- Verify multiplatform capabilities, cross-browser testing (Chrome, IE, Firefox, Edge, Safari), and mobile testing (iPad, iPhone, android phone, tablet) for build products.
- Ensure all testing is planned, implemented, and delivered per the latest industry standards, and to our quality expectations while meeting ambitious timelines.
- Fully own the assigned project’s testing stream – Perform requirement analysis and proactively find requirements gaps; discover and write test cases in Jira; create and maintain regression test case documents; sign off for release; do release smoke test.
- Identify application defects, seek resolution, process gaps, and make recommendations to improve the functionality and usability of the application.
- Call for the test case review meetings with the core team.
- Clearly communicate the testing timeline for each testing phase. Help the team set a realistic release timeline such that a testing effort is not overlooked or overly simplified.
- Ensure all identified risks from testing are raised and mitigated appropriately

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Product Manager, Program Technology
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance

**Key Internal Relationships:**

- METAL Technology Development Lead
- METAL Developers

**Desired Experience and Skills**

- 3+ years of data application testing experience, with proven experience managing and executing the full testing lifecycle, including UAT testing support
- 2+ years of Quality Assurance experience testing data processes and products: ETL pipelines, dashboards/reports, etc
- 2+ years of working with CommCare or similar ODK based platforms or any low-code application as an application developer or quality analyst is highly desirable.
- Some Performance and Load Testing experience with open-source tools
- 1 year of automation experience
- Solid ability to lead a project by him/herself from all quality assurance, and quality control aspects.
- Experienced testing in low to no-code environments and processes such as mobile data collection and/or case management tools such as CommCare, Ona, Kobo or Microsoft PowerApps, PowerBI dashboards and Azure.
- Understanding and experience with T-SQL, Azure SQL Server, Data Factory, SSIS/other ETL tools, data modeling and data warehouse.
- Experience testing multilingual platforms along with multicurrency verification preferred.
- Manual functional testing, system testing, along with some automation, and performance testing
- Have great collaboration with all teams involved in the project with self-directed.
- Meticulous in maintaining excellent organization and prioritization skills
- Experience using Jira for bug and test management.
- Experience with full software development process with Agile methodology
- Experience with any open-source performance/stress testing tool e.g., JMeter
- Possess excellent oral and written communication skills
- Self-motivated and a problem solver
- Fast and independent learner
- Work with distributed teams
- Intercultural competence

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree or experience in computer science or information systems.
- CSQA, CSTE, or any certification software testing/ quality assurance

**IRC is dedicated to reducing the gender gap in leadership roles and has implemented supportive measures like parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols, and other benefits to create an inclusive environment for women.**

**Applicants with varied career paths are welcomed, recognizing that employment gaps don't define potential. IRC values transferrable skills and is committed to investing in the growth and development of its team members.**

**The organization strives to offer competitive and equitable Compensation and Benefits programs to attract, motivate, and retain employees who adhere to the IRC Way Standards for Professional Conduct.**

**Compensation:** (**USA:** $68K - $74K / **UK:** GBP 34,653 GBP 41,150). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Haiti - Coordinateur.trice Terrain - Artibonite
jobs.description:
## QUE FAISONS-NOUS...

**Date de début souhaité:** ASAP
**Durée de la mission:** 6 mois
**Localisation**: Artibonite

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## LA MISSION

La mission Haiti a actuellement une base à Port au Prince et le bureau de la coordination. Les projets concernent la WASH et la SAME/NUT en consortium avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Elle est financée par OCHA, CDCS, SDC, ECHO, UNICEF, IFSAN entre autre. Depuis deux ans, la mission a connu une bonne croissance en terme d'opérations et de budget, répondant aux urgences dans la Zone Métropolitaine de Port au Prince mais également développe des actions de plus long termes. C'est dans cette dynamique que la mission Haiti a décidé d'ouvrir une nouvelle base en Artibonite, basée à Saint Marc afin de répondre aux besoins en EHA des populations dans ce département. La base est en début d'ouverture à l'heure actuelle, la mission principale du.de la CT aura pour but de régulariser la base après son ouverture et de la terminer.

17 expatriés et 80 staffs nationaux dans l'unique base et coordination de Port au Prince. Un premier set-up de 2/3 expats et une petite vingtaine de staffs nationaux est à entrevoir pour la base d'Artibonite.

## DESCRIPTIF DE POSTE

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Coordinateur.trice Terrain a un rôle de Directeur Pays (DP) par délégation sur l'Artibonite pour SI.
Il/elle propose en fonction du contexte géopolitique et humanitaire la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et s'assure de sa mise en œuvre une fois validée.
Il/elle contrôle et garantit que les projets se déroulent en adéquation avec la charte de Solidarités International et dans
le respect des procédures internes et contractuelles.
Il/elle mobilise les moyens matériels et financiers nécessaires à la bonne conduite des programmes et en supervise la gestion.
Il/elle coordonne les équipes en place et est le garant de leur sécurité sur sa zone d’affectation.
Il/elle est l’interlocuteur.trice direct.e et privilégié.e du/de la DP

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

Ce poste est une création suite à l'ouverture de la base Artibonite. Nous attendons un.e CT expérimenté sur ce type de niveau sécuritaire mais aussi possédant une grande expérience dans la structuration d'une nouvelle base après la phase d'ouverture.
Les enjeux sécuritaires - niveau 4 chez SI - sont nombreux notamment dans le cadre d'une base nouvelle.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS**

Gestion et de la mise en place des projets

Gestion opérationnelle de la sécurité sur la zone et continuité du travail d'accès engagé

Support au développement de nouvelles propositions de projets sur la zone

Travailler en interne sur la structuration de la base, finaliser les recrutements, finaliser l'installation de la base vie et bureaux, formation au travail chez SI, mise en place des procédures.

Accompagner la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et continuer son développement

Contribuer à renforcer le lien avec nos partenaires locaux et internationaux et les clusters de la zone

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

Haiti est catégorisé en Niveau 4, La sécurité est très volatile/dégradée en Artibonite dû à la présence des groupes armés et d'affrontements quotidiens, mais n’empêche pas la conduite des activités. Les règles de sécurité de la mission sont strictes (couvre-feu au coucher du soleil).

## VOTRE PROFIL

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Niveau Master

Experience dans le secteur humanitaire : 5 ans et plus

Experience sur un poste similaire : 3/4 ans

**COMPETENCES**

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES

1. Capacité à suivre et analyser le contexte humanitaire, politique, culturel, social, économique
2. Compétences pour garantir la coordination, le développement, le suivi et l’évaluation des programmes mis en œuvre sur sa zone d’intervention
3. Proposer le dimensionnement humain, financier et logistique pour sa zone d’intervention ainsi que son organisation
4. Gestion des RH, recrutement, induction, création de dynamiques d'équipes, mise en place de la relation base éloignée - coo pour Haiti (l'autre base est à Port au Prince, directement en lien avec la coo)
5. Etre responsable de la sécurité des équipes et des biens sur sa zone d’affectation, sur délégation de la DP

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSALES

1. Analyse, décision et gestion de crise : capacité à évaluer les risques, anticiper, décider et agir sous pression.
2. Leadership et communication : encadrer, former, sensibiliser et transmettre des consignes claires aux équipes et partenaires.
3. Diplomatie et adaptabilité : négocier avec divers acteurs, entretenir des relations de confiance et s’ajuster à un environnement instable.

**LANGUES**

1. Français
2. Anglais apprécié

## SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES...

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 750.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

A l'heure de l'ouverture de ce poste, la mission n'a pas commencé l'ouverture, aucun lieu de vie n'est pour l'instant défini. D'ici l'arrivée du.de la CT, la mission aura identifié un lieu de vie et de bureau.
A Saint Marc, la sécurité reste volatile avec des restrictions sécuritaires importantes. Vie sociale limitée à quelques restaurants et à la présence de MSF et NRC.

jobs.title: SIEGE – Référent santé – H/F
jobs.description:
**A propos de la Chaîne de l’Espoir**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir est une ONG internationale fondée en 1994. Elle a pour vocation de renforcer les systèmes de santé pour donner à chacun et en particulier aux enfants les mêmes chances de survie et de développement.

Nous intervenons dans 28 pays par une approche globale, centrée sur l’enfant mais également sur les mères et les communautés défavorisées :

- Prévention et dépistage dès le plus jeune âge, notamment dans le cadre de programmes de santé à l’école.
- Soin et chirurgie, afin de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des enfants et de leurs mères.
- Formation et transferts de compétences aux équipes locales grâce à notre réseau international d’experts dans tous les domaines de la chirurgie.
- Construction et équipement de structures hospitalières adaptées aux besoins locaux.

**Poste et missions**

Au sein de la Direction Santé et Ingénierie Hospitalière, et en lien fonctionnel fort avec la Direction des Opérations le Référent Santé joue un rôle essentiel dans la définition, la mise en œuvre et la supervision des programmes de La Chaîne de l’Espoir, en apportant un appui technique aux équipes de coordination des programmes.

Il est placé sous la responsabilité du Responsable du Département médical. Il exerce ses missions en lien étroit avec les équipes de la Direction des Opérations, et en collaboration étroite avec l’ensemble des équipes de la Direction de l’Expertise c’est-à-dire le Département médical et le Département Infrastructure et équipement biomédical.

Par ailleurs le Référent santé réalise toutes tâches et missions nécessaires confiées par sa hiérarchie et qui permettent de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs du Département médical et de la Direction Santé et Ingénierie Hospitalière.

- **Appui RH:** Contribution à l’élaboration des fiches de postes du personnel médical et paramédical terrain.

Participation au processus de recrutement des postes de coordination médicale et de responsables de programme de santé.

Contribution aux briefings et débriefings des personnels médicaux.

Participation aux entretiens d’appréciation professionnelle technique des coordinateurs santé terrain.

- **Stratégie Santé Pays et Siège:**

Soutien technique aux équipes siège et terrain dans la préparation et le suivi des missions exploratoires

Collaboration avec les équipes siège et terrain pour l'élaboration des stratégies opérationnelles et le montage des projets, en ligne avec la stratégie globale de l’association

Identification et analyse des besoins médicaux des pays d’intervention.

- **Soutien Technique aux Projets:**

Apport d'un soutien technique aux équipes programmes pour garantir la qualité des programmes médicaux

Appui technique des équipes de terrain tout au long du cycle de projet, notamment via des missions dans les pays d'intervention

Supervision des préparations et validation des commandes médicales, en s’assurant de leur pertinence et cohérence

- **Suivi et Qualité des Projets:**

Émission de recommandations pour assurer la qualité des projets lors des suivis réguliers à distance et des visites terrain

Participation à la définition et à l’élaboration de la politique qualité, avec une mise à jour des cadres de référence

Contribution à la capitalisation des activités médicales, incluant la rédaction de rapports, la relecture des rapports bailleurs et l’analyse des missions médicales

- **Renforcement des Capacités:**

En fonction des besoins, élaboration et animation de formations internes ou auprès de nos partenaires opérationnels. Appui à la coordination et au pilotage techniques des programmes de La Chaîne de l’Espoir.

Accompagnement des équipes terrain pour le pilotage des actions de ses partenaires sur le terrain au besoin.

## Profil recherché

**Formations et expériences**

**Formation :**

- Niveau Master (BAC +5), formation médicale ou paramédicale, formation en Santé publique. Un profil de sage-femme sera très apprécié

**Expérience :**

- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans le domaine médical ou paramédical.
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans le secteur de la solidarité internationale dont au moins une expérience significative sur le terrain.
- Expérience avérée dans la mise en œuvre, gestion, suivi de projets et/ou dans la définition de stratégies opérationnelles.

**Compétences**

- Excellentes compétences rédactionnelles en français et en anglais
- Anglais courant indispensable
- Sens du relationnel, esprit d’équipe
- Force de proposition, sens de l’initiative, autonomie
- Sens de l’organisation, rigueur, esprit d’analyse, respect des délais
- Adhésion aux principes éthiques de l’association

**Conditions**

- CDI
- Date de démarrage souhaitée : 4 janvier 2027
- Déplacements ponctuels à prévoir
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 80%
- Remboursement abonnement transport à hauteur de 50 % ou indemnité mobilité durable (vélo) de 45 euros/mois
- Tickets Repas d’une valeur de 12,10€ pris en charge à 60%
- Charte de télétravail : 2 jours/semaine
- 23 jours de RTT annuel
- Salaire proposé : 45 600€ – 50 400€ sur 12 mois selon profil et expérience
- CE: chèques cadeaux

jobs.title: ICT Officer
jobs.description:
**DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Service Desk and User Support**

- Provide first- and second-line support by telephone, service desk, remote-support tools and desk-side assistance across regional offices and remote locations.
- Log, categorize, prioritize, diagnose, resolve and document incidents and service requests; escalate high-impact or unresolved issues appropriately.
- Provide discreet, responsive support to Executive Management and communicate technical solutions clearly to non-technical users.
- Create and maintain support documentation, knowledge articles, user guides and troubleshooting records.

Microsoft 365, Identity and Endpoints

- Support Microsoft Teams, Exchange Online/Outlook, SharePoint Online, OneDrive and Microsoft 365 Apps.
- Perform delegated Microsoft Entra ID and Active Directory administration, including account, password, group and access support under approved procedures.
- Support device enrolment, configuration, compliance and application deployment through Microsoft Intune or the approved endpoint-management platform.
- Build, deploy, maintain and securely retire Windows 11 computers, mobile devices and other approved endpoints; coordinate warranty and repair cases.
- Ensure operating systems, applications, endpoint protection and encryption remain current and compliant.

**Server, Linux and Infrastructure Support**

- Provide delegated operational support for Windows Server 2019/2022, including routine health checks, patching, monitoring, backups, and file and print services.
- Support Ubuntu and Debian Linux servers through package updates, service checks, log review, storage monitoring, user access and documented troubleshooting.
- Assist with virtual infrastructure, storage and backup platforms within assigned access and approved procedures.
- Provide smart-hands support for regional server rooms, network equipment, rack-and-stack work, cabling, power checks and vendor-assisted maintenance.

**Networks, FortiGate and Security**

- Support LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi, internet, DNS, DHCP and VPN services and coordinate escalation to service providers.
- Provide delegated operational support for FortiGate firewalls and Fortinet services, including monitoring, VPN support, configuration-backup checks and change preparation. Production changes must follow approval and change control procedures.
- Triage suspected phishing, malware, account compromise, data loss and other security events, preserve evidence and escalate through the incident-response process.
- Support vulnerability remediation, patch compliance, access reviews, backup verification, restore tests and disaster-recovery exercises.
- Deliver practical cyber-awareness and safe-computing guidance to staff.

Assets, Vendors Management and Reporting

- Maintain accurate ICT assets, warranty, assignment, location and lifecycle records across regional offices.
- Coordinate vendors, internet service providers and repair centers, track service levels and communicate service status.
- Assist with technical specifications, quotations, procurement planning, delivery checks and service acceptance.
- Prepare service reports covering incidents, recurring problems, patch and compliance status, asset exceptions, risks and improvement actions.

**SKILLS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED**

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.

• At least 3 to 4 years of progressively responsible ICT support or systems-support experience, preferably in a multi-site or distributed organization.

• Hands-on experience with Microsoft 365, Windows 11, Microsoft Entra ID, Active Directory, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive.

• Practical experience supporting Windows Server 2019/2022 and Linux systems, particularly Ubuntu and Debian.

• Experience supporting FortiGate firewalls, remote-access or site-to-site VPNs, LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi and internet connectivity.

• Experience with endpoint management, patching, antivirus/EDR, device encryption, mobile-device support and IT service-management tools.

• Understanding of backup, restore, monitoring, virtualization, UPS/power protection and server-room operations.

• Experience supporting users across countries, cultures, time zones and variable connectivity conditions is strongly desirable.

**Preferred Professional Certifications**

• Current Microsoft 365, Azure/Entra/Intune, Windows client or Windows Server certification or demonstrated training.

• ITIL 4 Foundation or equivalent service-management training.

• Cisco CCNA, CompTIA Network+/Security+, a current Fortinet certification, or equivalent networking/security training. • Linux administration certification or demonstrable equivalent practical capability.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Strong diagnostic, analytical and root-cause investigation skills.
- Excellent spoken and written communication, customer service and user-training skills.
- Ability to prioritise competing incidents, meet service targets and remain effective during outages or security events.
- High integrity, discretion and respect for confidentiality, privacy and privileged access.
- Accurate documentation and attention to detail in tickets, configurations, inventories and reports.
- Ability to work independently in a regional office and collaboratively with a geographically distributed ICT team.
- Vendor-management, planning, escalation and follow-through skills.
- Willingness to travel regionally and provide occasional out-of-hours support when required.

jobs.title: Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies
jobs.description:
ILGA World is seeking an Advocacy Specialist on Treaty Bodies, who will work as part of our advocacy programme and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with [the United Nations human rights treaty body system](https://www.ohchr.org/en/treaty-bodies).

**Deadline for applications:** Tuesday, 10 November 2026 – 23:59 (Central European Time, CET)
**Start of the position:** January/February 2027, subject to successful work authorisation and any applicable notice period

## Who can apply?

Anyone

- with dedication to – and experience in regard to – the human rights of persons with diverse sexual orientations, [**gender**](https://ilga.org/glossary/gender/) identities, gender expressions and [**sex characteristics**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sex-characteristics/)
- who meets the requirements set out below

is welcome to apply.

## Overview

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies is part of ILGA World’s advocacy prgramme and coordinates the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the [**United Nations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/united-nations/) human rights treaty body system.

The role advances the rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC by connecting grassroots, national and regional advocacy with international human rights mechanisms. It provides technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions and human rights defenders; supports strategic engagement with treaty bodies; and helps ensure that movement priorities, evidence and lived realities inform [**country reviews**](https://ilga.org/glossary/country-reviews/), normative developments, jurisprudence and follow-up at national level.

Working under the strategic direction of the Advocacy Senior Manager and closely with colleagues across the advocacy programme, ILGA regions, member organisations and partner organisations, the Specialist monitors treaty body processes and opportunities, coordinates submissions and briefings, supports strategic litigation and national follow-up, analyses recommendations and jurisprudence, develops capacity-strengthening resources, and maintains relationships with treaty body members and OHCHR staff. The role also works across ILGA World programmes to connect advocacy with knowledge production and movement strengthening.

## Responsibilities

The Advocacy Specialist: Treaty Bodies reports to the Advocacy Senior Manager and is responsible for the day-to-day coordination and delivery of ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies portfolio within the Advocacy Programme.

### Specific to this position, this includes:

- Implement ILGA World’s Treaty Bodies advocacy workplan and coordinate the organisation’s day-to-day engagement with the UN human rights Treaty Body system, serving as the organisational focal point for Treaty Bodies-related advocacy.
- Monitor Treaty Body sessions, reporting cycles, country reviews, lists of Issues Prior to Reporting (LOIPRs) under the Simplified Reporting Procedure, follow-up procedures, general comments, individual communications and other developments, identifying timely and strategic opportunities for SOGIESC advocacy.
- Develop and implement advocacy strategies to advance the human rights of people and communities of diverse SOGIESC through country reviews, normative development, individual communications and other relevant Treaty Body procedures.
- Provide technical assistance to ILGA World members, regions, LGBTI organisations and human rights defenders engaging with Treaty Bodies, including advocacy planning, reporting, preparation of written and oral submissions, briefings and follow up strategies.
- Coordinate and contribute to ILGA World and joint submissions, shadow report inputs, briefing materials, statements, position papers and other advocacy products in consultation with affected communities, members, regions, partners, and external legal experts
- Facilitate the meaningful participation of human rights defenders in Treaty Body processes, including organising briefings and engagement with Treaty Body members and OHCHR staff.
- Coordinate ILGA World’s strategic litigation engagement before Treaty Bodies, including identifying appropriate opportunities, supporting individual communications and third-party interventions, and contributing to follow-up on decisions in collaboration with members, partners and relevant legal experts.
- Monitor, systematise and analyse SOGIESC-related [**concluding observations**](https://ilga.org/glossary/concluding-observations/), recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence, decisions and other Treaty Body outputs, and contribute to compilations, briefings and analytical resources.
- Support ILGA World members and human rights defenders to use Treaty Body recommendations, decisions and jurisprudence in national advocacy, including follow up and implementation, and document relevant results, challenges and good practices.
- Develop and deliver training, webinars, guidance and other capacity strengthening resources to strengthen civil society engagement with the Treaty Body system.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with Treaty Body members, OHCHR staff, civil society organisations, legal experts, academics and other relevant stakeholders, and represent ILGA World in relevant meetings, consultations and external spaces.
- Monitor and contribute to discussions concerning Treaty Body strengthening, accessibility, effectiveness and other institutional developments affecting the system.
- Work across ILGA World programmes and advocacy portfolios to strengthen coherence between Treaty Bodies, the Human Rights Council, Universal Periodic Review, Special Procedures and thematic advocacy, and ensure that relevant ILGA World research and monitoring data inform Treaty Body engagement.
- Contribute to planning, budgeting, monitoring, evaluation and learning, donor reporting and funding proposals relating to the Treaty Bodies portfolio, and work with the Communications team to make relevant opportunities, developments and outcomes accessible to members, partners and wider audiences.

### **General**

- Actively contribute to promoting and achieving the organisation’s objectives.
- Engage and collaborate with colleagues across the Advocacy Programme and other ILGA World teams to strengthen a shared organisational culture and ensure coordinated, movement-informed work.
- Ensure that all activities are carried out with full regard to ILGA World policies.
- Work as a part of the ILGA World staff team.
- Perform other duties as required.

### **Relationships with colleagues**

ILGA values creative and inclusive approaches to work and management that have been achieved through cross-service area working and the participation of staff at all levels in the organisation. Staff have line management arrangements and specific key relationships, which are detailed in their job descriptions, but they will also need to work collaboratively with their colleagues in order to achieve their agreed targets and outcomes to the required standards.

## Performance of duties, remuneration, and benefits

- This position requires relocation to Geneva, Switzerland.
- This position is subject to the successful granting of the necessary Swiss work authorisation.
- Where required, ILGA World will submit and support the work permit application for the selected candidate. However, the relevant Swiss authorities make decisions on work authorisation, and ILGA World cannot guarantee that an application will be successful. Any offer of employment and appointment to the position is therefore conditional upon the required work permit being granted. If the necessary authorisation cannot be secured, ILGA World will not be able to confirm or proceed with the appointment.
- The position is advertised at 100% of a full-time position.
- ILGA World remunerates under a three-tiered salary matrix structure. The annual salary offered for the 100% position is 81,060 CHF.
- In addition, ILGA World offers 32 days, inclusive of legal holidays (“bank holidays”) and annual leave and contributions to health care costs.
- ILGA World operates under a flexible working system that – among others – includes flexible working hours.
- The weekly working time is 40 hours on a 100% position.

## Requirements

### **Education and qualifications**

- A master’s university degree or equivalent in [**international human rights law**](https://ilga.org/glossary/international-human-rights-law/), law, political science, international relations or a related field, combined with 6 years of relevant work experience

or

- A first-level university degree in combination with 8 years of relevant and qualifying experience

or

- 10 years of relevant and qualifying experience instead of a master’s or first-level degree

### **Experience**

- A minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in human rights advocacy, policy or legal work, preferably within an international, regional or national civil society organisation, multilateral institution or similar setting.
- At least 2 years of direct engagement with United Nations human rights mechanisms, including substantive experience working with one or more UN Treaty Bodies.
- Experience developing and implementing advocacy strategies relating to Treaty Body country reviews, normative development or other treaty body procedures.
- Experience drafting shadow reports, written submissions, briefing materials, statements, position papers or other advocacy documentation for international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience providing technical assistance, guidance or capacity strengthening to civil society organisations and human rights defenders engaging with international human rights mechanisms.
- Experience analysing international human rights standards, concluding observations, recommendations and/or jurisprudence and translating complex legal developments into accessible advocacy guidance.
- Experience with or strong familiarity with strategic litigation, individual communications or other forms of legal advocacy before international or regional human rights mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience working collaboratively with grassroots organisations, LGBTI human rights defenders and diverse stakeholders across different national, cultural and political contexts.
- Experience in project coordination, including planning, monitoring, evaluation, learning and narrative reporting, including in donor-funded work.
- Experience building and maintaining working relationships with UN officials and experts, civil society organisations, legal practitioners, academic partners and other relevant stakeholders.

### **Technical requirements**

- Advanced skills in legal and policy analysis, with strong knowledge of international human rights law and its application to [**sexual orientation**](https://ilga.org/glossary/sexual-orientation/), gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics.
- Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of the UN human rights Treaty Body system, including country review processes, normative outputs, follow-up procedures and individual communications.
- Ability to monitor, systematise and analyse Treaty Body recommendations, general comments, jurisprudence and other outputs and identify strategic advocacy opportunities.
- Strong research and drafting skills, including the ability to present complex legal and policy developments clearly and accessibly to different audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain partnerships with member organisations, human rights defenders, UN officials, civil society organisations and other stakeholders.
- Strong understanding of SOGIESC human rights issues and commitment to feminist, decolonial, intersectional and anti-oppressive approaches to advocacy.

### **Other requirements**

- Strong communication, facilitation and diplomatic skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with diverse audiences
- Excellent organisational skills, sound judgement and the ability to prioritise work, meet deadlines and adapt to changing advocacy opportunities
- Proven existing professional relationships with the [**Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights**](https://ilga.org/glossary/office-of-the-high-commissioner-for-human-rights/) (OHCHR) Secretariat staff and/or independent Treaty Body experts.
- Ability to work proficiently in English (mandatory). Knowledge of Spanish, French or another UN official language is an asset
- Adherence to and alignment with the ILGA World Code of Conduct, including a strong capacity for confidentiality, tact, discretion and respectful collaboration

jobs.title: Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships
jobs.description:
**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The **Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships** is responsible for delivering an efficient, effective, and high-quality award management function across the Kenya Country Office. The post holder will provide strategic leadership for award management throughout the award lifecycle, ensuring compliance with donor requirements, Save the Children policies, and organisational standards.

The role leads the management of all awards and partnerships within the Country Office, ensuring robust systems, processes, and controls are in place to support effective programme delivery, donor compliance, portfolio performance, and risk management. The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships will establish and promote best-practice award management processes, working closely with the Programme Development and Quality (PDQ), Finance, Operations, and Programme teams to ensure the successful implementation and oversight of awards.

In addition, the role provides strategic leadership on localisation and partnership development, strengthening engagement with local actors and ensuring the Country Office's localisation commitments are embedded throughout programme design, implementation, and partnership management. The post holder will serve as the focal point for members and donors on award-related matters, fostering strong relationships and ensuring responsive, solution-oriented communication.

The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships is accountable for the performance of the award portfolio, monitoring risks and opportunities, driving timely corrective actions, and ensuring award management systems and processes are consistently applied across all departments. Through effective leadership, coordination, and stakeholder engagement, the role contributes to the achievement of programme objectives, sustainable partnerships, donor confidence, and the overall strategic growth of the Kenya Country Office.

**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

**Reports to:** Country Director

**Staff reporting to this post: 4 staff -** Awards and Partership Coordinator, Awards and Finance Officer, Awards and Partnership Assistant and Awards and Partnership Intern..

**Budget Responsibilities**: None

**Role Dimensions**: The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships is responsible for managing a portfolio of high-, medium-, and low-risk awards within the Kenya Country Office, providing strong leadership and oversight, particularly for high-risk and complex awards. The role requires extensive internal and external coordination, stakeholder engagement, and strategic support across all aspects of award management, including award contracting, donor compliance, reporting, and portfolio performance management.

The post holder is accountable for ensuring compliance with Save the Children's Award Management Essential Standards and Award Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across the Kenya portfolio. Acting as the central coordination point between PDQ, Finance, and Operations, the Awards Manager ensures effective award management throughout the entire award lifecycle. The role serves as the primary focal point for Members and donors, maintaining responsive, solution-oriented communication and fostering strong working relationships.

The Head of Awards, Localisation and Partnerships leads the partnership portfolio and locally led delivery modality, ensuring high-quality programs are delivered at scale through strategic and equitable partnerships. The role drives the operationalization of the localisation strategy across its seven dimensions and embeds partners throughout the full programme cycle, from design to implementation and learning, while strengthening systems, processes, and risk-sharing practices. The role is responsible for monitoring award performance, proactively identifying and escalating risks and issues, and ensuring timely implementation of mitigation measures. The position also ensures that award management systems, processes, and controls are effectively implemented and adhered to across all departments, with a particular focus on donor compliance, reporting quality, financial stewardship, and timely delivery of award obligations. Through strong coordination and leadership, the role contributes to maximizing funding opportunities, reducing compliance risks, and enhancing the overall effectiveness and efficiency of the Country Office portfolio.

**Travel:** Occasional

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY :**

**Portfolio Planning, Development, and Management:**

- Coordinate the submission of all required information and documentation into AMS by relevant functions in a timely manner as new funding opportunities are identified.
- Review award agreements to identify potential risks and provide summaries of key risk areas.
- Participate in go/no-go decision-making processes with Members and the Senior Management Team (SMT), including opportunity and risk assessments.
- Develop funding optimization strategies in collaboration with the Finance team, including match plans, CAM, and other funding mechanisms.
- Support the Country Director (CD) and SPD Manager in strengthening engagement and relationship management with Members and donor representatives on award management and compliance matters.
- In collaboration with the PDQ team, provide strategic portfolio information to the SMT and Save the Children Members through a monthly portfolio analysis report, highlighting pipeline opportunities, active awards, awards under amendment, high-risk awards, and closed awards.

**Award Management and AMS Management:**

- Ensure all award lifecycle processes are completed through AMS workflows in a timely manner and that all relevant information is accurately maintained within the system and in hard-copy files where required.
- Liaise directly with Members to ensure timely issuance of workflows and fund summaries following award approval.
- Establish mechanisms for disseminating award information to ensure all key staff understand award requirements and expectations throughout the award lifecycle.
- Ensure kick-off meetings are conducted promptly for all new awards and that coding structures and budgets are effectively communicated to budget holders.
- Lead Member engagement and relationship management as the SCI focal point for awards, coordinating SCI/Member reviews and revisions of proposals, budgets, and agreements.
- Provide regular updates to the Finance Manager on new awards that impact Master Budget gap analysis and co-lead the maintenance of the CAM calculator.
- Lead the analysis of Budget versus Actual Expenditure (BVA) reports for monthly award review meetings. Work with budget holders to develop and implement corrective action plans and monitor progress against agreed actions.
- Coordinate monthly award review meetings and maintain a tracker of action points and outstanding issues.
- Provide guidance on budget coding and reallocations in collaboration with budget holders.
- Coordinate budget realignments, amendments, cost extensions, and no-cost extension requests to Members and donors in a timely manner.
- Work closely with Programme Operations to ensure timely award close-out meetings. Ensure all meetings are documented, minutes are filed in AMS, and follow-up actions are completed.
- Ensure AMS is accurately maintained, up to date, and provides a complete audit trail for all awards and sub-awards.
- Support Programme Managers in budget development, cost allocation, budget monitoring, phasing, and forecasting, ensuring that phased award budgets are uploaded into Agresso.

**Reporting to Members and Donors:**

- Coordinate the award reporting process to ensure high-quality reports are submitted within agreed timelines.
- Share the award reporting schedule with the Extended Senior Management Team on the first working day of each month.
- Support the preparation of financial reports, with responsibility transitioning to Finance once appropriate staffing capacity is established.
- Review all award reports prior to submission to Members and donors to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance.
- Share Members' qualitative feedback on reports with relevant stakeholders on a monthly basis.
- Ensure donors and Members are informed of any significant award-related issues.
- Manage contractual relationships with donors and Members through effective communication on reports, contracts, amendments, and audits.
- Collaborate with relevant functions and Members to strengthen project staff capacity in quality reporting.

**Donor Compliance:**

- Ensure donor compliance requirements, including reporting deadlines, amendment procedures, audit requirements, and SCI award management policies, are clearly understood and adhered to.
- Ensure potential compliance issues and amendment requests are promptly communicated to donors through the relevant Save the Children Member.
- Develop business cases and support negotiations where donor waivers or derogation requests require detailed justification.
- Collaborate with Member focal points to ensure all donor compliance requirements are captured in AMS before fund summary workflows are initiated.

**Localisation:**

- Lead the implementation of the Country Office Localization Strategy, in line with Save the Children’s Global Partnership Framework, Localization Policy, Grand Bargain commitments, and CHS standards.
- Ensure partnership and localization priorities are fully integrated into country strategic planning, annual plans, and humanitarian response strategies.
- Drive the operationalization of localization across its seven dimensions, identifying and addressing operational bottlenecks and influencing systems, processes, and decision-making.
- Coordinate periodic self-assessments on partnerships and localization, ensuring action plans are developed, implemented, monitored, and reported to SMT

**Partnership Management:**

- Provide capacity-building and compliance support to both new and existing partners, working closely with Programme Operations to ensure partner performance meets donor expectations.
- Conduct regular spot checks to ensure all partner documentation, including reports, is uploaded and maintained within AMS.
- Lead and coordinate partner scoping, mapping, assessment, and selection processes in collaboration with PDQI and program teams. ( implementing the Equitable Partnership Management Cycle)
- Ensure partners are actively engaged in programme design, proposal development, planning, and budgeting, including adequate resourcing of partner support and capacity strengthening.

**Staff Management and Development:**

- Strengthen the capacity of the Award Management Team in award lifecycle management and build the capacity of budget holders on their award management roles and responsibilities.
- Manage the performance of direct reports through effective application of SCI's Performance Management System.
- Address underperformance through clear documentation, performance improvement plans, and structured development work plans.
- Foster a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and professional development within the team.

**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice**)

**Accountability:**

- holds self accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
- holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

**Ambition:**

- sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same
- widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others
- future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

**Collaboration:**

- builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters
- values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
- approachable, good listener, easy to talk to

**Creativity:**

- develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
- willing to take disciplined risks.

**Integrity:**

- honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- Bachelor’s degree in International Development, Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, or a related field.
- Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA, or equivalent) is highly desirable.
- Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in award, grant, portfolio, or financial management, preferably within an international NGO or donor-funded environment, *including at least 7 years in a senior leadership role.*
- Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-donor portfolios and leading cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality programme and award management outcomes.

**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**

**Essential**

- Proven experience in staff management, supervision, coaching, and capacity building, particularly in award and grant management.
- Significant experience managing complex award portfolios and donor-funded programmes.
- Proven track record in grant and contract management, including sub-award administration and donor compliance.
- Strong knowledge of major institutional donor requirements and regulations, including but not limited to USAID, FCDO, ECHO, EU, UNICEF, WFP, and other bilateral and multilateral donors.
- Experience developing and implementing award management systems, processes, and controls across the award lifecycle.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively and influence stakeholders in a complex, multicultural environment.
- Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, facilitation, and relationship management skills.
- Strong financial management skills, including budget development, forecasting, financial analysis, and budget monitoring.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with strong attention to detail.
- Proven ability to identify, assess, and mitigate award-related risks.
- Strong planning, organizational, and coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet tight deadlines.
- Ability to remain flexible, adaptable, and responsive in a fast-paced and changing environment.

jobs.title: Regional Business Development Manager- SWANA
jobs.description:
**About The Role**

**Team Purpose**
Institutional funding is key for operationalizing Oxfam’s mandate globally and in the region. Institutional sources (including multilateral and bilateral agencies and donors) typically have decentralised operations, budgets and decision-making structures throughout the world. To engage effectively with these organisations Oxfam has an established global architecture that mirrors its key institutional relationships, builds stronger partnerships and delivers greater impact and influence at country, regional and global levels. This operational architecture also enables Oxfam to more readily purse multi-country / regional opportunities that are offered by institutional donors to address transnational issues such as migration, climate change, natural disasters and conflicts. Humanitarian crises which often cross-national borders also require standing capacity at regional levels to most effectively mobilise resources.

**Job Purpose**
The Regional Business Development Manager will lead on new business development in support of all countries in their region; creating, identifying and accessing new funding opportunities; maintaining a consistent standard of donor relationship and high-quality proposal development across variable country contexts; and will actively seek to grow income for the confederation through multi-country funding opportunities and consortium partnerships.

The Regional Business Development Manager will also support the Regional Director in providing strategic leadership on resource mobilisation across all countries in the region. They will be responsible for developing and implementing the regions resource mobilisation strategies; supporting the Regional Director in building partnerships with regional donors and civil society stakeholders; identifying new funding opportunities; addressing key financial and reputational risks; and ensuring that there are strategies in place to maintain adequate skills and capacity, staffing and income within the portfolio of countries in the region.

The post holder will be expected to work across the confederation of Oxfam affiliates and the Oxfam International Secretariat in achieving the regional funding strategy and be the primary link for accessing technical fundraising assistance and support from the confederations fundraising architecture.

jobs.description:
**Purpose of the Post**

The Documents Management Assistant supports the Documents Control function and IMODOCS (IMO's electronic document repository and distribution system) with documents in the six languages of the Organization.

The incumbent will manage the frontline Document Counter service during meetings, taking timely, independent decisions on document management under strict timeframes, including out-of-hours and night shifts, and is responsible for the timely internal and external distribution of documents to interpreters, Member States, NGOs and the Secretariat.

The post holder provides office support for all systems during virtual and hybrid meetings, coordinates with the relevant technical Divisions and Sections to ensure efficient distribution of documents, and supports interpreters through the timely provision of documentation. The role also assists the Senior Printer with the printing and distribution of documentation sets for interpreters, delegates and the Secretariat.

**Required Competencies**

1\. High degree of initiative and sound judgement, with a solutions-oriented approach and consistent emphasis on deadline delivery under high-pressure conditions.

2\. Technological awareness: proactive use of document management systems and tools, with the ability to identify and propose improvements to work processes.

3\. Demonstrated ability to coordinate independently with internal and external stakeholders — technical Divisions, interpreters, language sections, delegates and the Secretariat — building and maintaining effective working relationships at all levels.

4\. Tact, discretion and sensitivity in providing frontline client service within a multicultural, international environment, including autonomous decision-making under strict timeframes.

5\. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, and flexibility with regard to work hours, including willingness to work night and early shifts to ensure meeting delivery.

**Professional Experience**

At least four years' experience in document management, meetings/events management or a related field, within an international, multilingual environment is required. Experience in publishing and/or logistics management is desirable. Prior experience within the United Nations system, or another international organization, in a similar function is an advantage.

**Education**

Secondary education or equivalent to university entrance standard.

**Language Skills**

Excellent command of English, both written and oral, is required. Working knowledge of other official languages of the Organization would be an advantage.

**Other Skills**

Proficiency in MS Office applications and document management software is required. The ability to use technology confidently and effectively, and to adapt quickly to new systems and digital tools, is required. Knowledge of IMODOCS and related IMO systems, printing machinery and software is a strong asset. Familiarity with support services to translation and interpretation in the context of conference management is an advantage.

**Main Duties & Responsibilities**

***Documents control***

1 Monitor internal document management systems, including gDoc and IMODOCS, to ensure timely and accurate processing and distribution of all IMO meeting documents and other jobs (e.g. certified copies).

2 Liaise directly with submitting officers regarding any queries and transmit corrections, as appropriate, to the translation sections involved.

3 Publish final documents on IMODOCS in all working/official languages, without direct input from the line manager.

4 Coordinate with the relevant technical Divisions and translation sections during meetings to ensure timely processing of in-session documents.

***Documents Counter service***

5 Provide frontline assistance to IMO delegates at the Document Counter, independently answering a wide range of individual queries and requests, drawing on sound knowledge and recollection of decisions and practice from past meetings.

6 Distribute hard copies to Member States and NGOs prior to and during meetings according to priorities, and ensure timely distribution of in-session documents, both electronic and in hard copy.

7 Work out-of-hours and night shifts independently at the Document Counter, taking timely decisions on document management under strict timeframes.

***Printing and meeting preparation***

8 Assist the Senior Printer in the delivery of hard copies, including batch printing of sets (print-on-demand) to support interpreters and the Secretariat.

9 Coordinate with the relevant IMO Divisions and Sections involved in IMO meetings to ensure efficient distribution of documents (working papers, briefs, status reports).

10 Calculate printing figures for each meeting based on the meeting registration system (OMRS) to ensure PaperSmart distribution of documents.

1 Provide documentation (e.g. J papers) to delegations ahead of the start of each meeting in the Plenary Hall, and undertake internal posting of meeting documents to the Secretariat in a timely manner, including preparation of sets for the podium.

***Support to interpreters***

12 Provide interpreters with select background publications during meetings, choosing resources based on an understanding of the key issues under discussion.

13 Ensure timely transmission of statements received from delegations, in electronic and hard copy, to interpreters' booths and the Secretariat within critical deadlines.

14 Distribute meeting documents to interpreters prior to and during each meeting, and liaise with interpreters on documentation issues, including updating publications and reports in the interpreters' booths.

***Other***

15 Provide office support for all systems during virtual and hybrid meetings.

16 Work night shifts independently, as required, to ensure meeting delivery.

17 Undertake other duties connected to the work of the Documentation and Language Technologies Section as may be assigned.

**Contract Information**

\*Local status requires applicants to have unhindered permission to live and work in the UK.
