jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP has achieved significant progress in making gender equality and women’s empowerment integral to its work on human development. The new UNDP Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029 complements the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, approved by Executive Board consensus, which defines gender equality as one of three accelerators of human development on a healthy planet. The Strategy acknowledges that success in every area of the Strategic Plan depends on realizing gender equality and the empowerment of women. It retains the ambition of the previous strategy, with a central focus on transforming the systems and power structures that generate gender inequalities. It calls on UNDP to help governments place gender equality at the core of political, economic, and environmental decisions, with the goal of expanding development choices that work for all. The Strategy defines gender equality priorities across each strategic objective and accelerator of the Strategic Plan. It focuses on areas where UNDP has a strong comparative advantage and where solutions can be scaled, building on successful initiatives and partnerships. UNDP also recognizes that mechanical or compliance approaches will not suffice to address the scope of discrimination, and the importance of renewing emphasis on partnerships, including with the private sector. The Strategy proposes institutional transformation inspired by UNDP Gender Equality Seal Certification principles and aligned to the United Nations system-wide Action Plan on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN-SWAP) and Gender Equality Action Plan (GEAP) standards. UNDP recognizes that external impact and delivery mirror internal policies, structures, culture and ways of working.

The Gender Team (BPPS) has the leading role in the implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029, including through the implementation of Gender Equality Global Programme.

Duties and Responsibilities

Reporting directly to the Head of Gender in New York, the Gender Specialist, Accountability and Reporting will ensure UNDP is accountable for its commitments to gender equality in line with the Strategic Plan 2026-2929 and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029; lead the implementation of the UN-SWAP and the GEAP to advance UN-System wide commitments on gender equality and interagency coordination; lead UNDP’s efforts to track financial investments for gender equality; and lead and provide reliable gender-related data for decision-making.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Ensure UNDP is accountable for its commitments to gender equality in line with the Strategic Plan 2026-2929 and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029.

- Coordinate and deliver UNDP’s reporting on gender equality including the Annual Report on the Implementation of the UNDP Gender Equality Strategy (official and glossy version), the GEAP Annual Report, the UN-SWAP Annual Report, and the ECOSOC reports.

- Provide technical and coordination support for the preparation, convening and follow-up of the Gender Steering and Implementation Committee (GSIC), as the main mechanism for monitoring implementation of the GES 2026-2029.

- Provide advice and technical support to ensure performance assessment criteria for all senior and middle managers include implementation of the GES 2026-2029, in close collaboration with key bureaus and teams (OHR/BMS, Gender Equality Seal for Development, among others).

- Act as evaluation and audit focal point for the Gender Team, including by liaising with the UNDP Independent Evaluation Office and the Audit Office; engaging in corporate gender evaluations or audits; preparing management responses; tracking the implementation of evaluation recommendations; and delivering the reports and evaluation of the Gender Equality Global Programme 2023-2025.

- Ensure the gender equality data powerhouse is updated.

Lead the implementation of the UN-SWAP and the GEAP to advance UN-System wide commitments on gender equality and interagency coordination.

- Develop and lead UNDP’s Action Plan for the effective implementation of its commitments in the framework of the UN-SWAP and GEAP.

- Liaise with key teams and units (HQ, RH and CO) to ensure UNDP meets UN SWAP/GEAP standards.

- Engage closely with the UNDP Gender Equality Seal for country offices, as the primary global initiative to operationalize the GES 2026-2029.

- Represent UNDP and the Gender Team in key global UN interagency coordination spaces, such as IANGWE, UN-SWAP and GEAP.

- Support UNDP’s participation in intergovernmental conferences and high-level inter-agency events related to system-wide commitments for gender equality.

Lead UNDP’s efforts to track financial investments for gender equality.

- Lead implementation of UNDP’s gender marker as the main tool to track budgets and expenditures for gender equality at all levels (HQ, RH and CO).

- Ensure UNDP’s gender marker meets UN system wide quality standards; coordinate quality assurance and periodic reviews to ensure accuracy.

- Provide technical support to HQ’s Teams, RH and COs to help them meet UNDP’s gender marker targets (GES 2026-2029); foster learning and knowledge sharing.

- Coordinate the development of financial and narrative annual reports/snapshots for leadership decision-making (i.e., global, by region, by priority), including analysis of progress towards the targets established in the GES 2026-2029.

- Represent UNDP in inter-agency fora on the implementation of gender markers and other mechanisms to track financial investments for gender equality.

Lead and provide reliable gender-related data for decision-making.

- Collect and analyze relevant corporate data from different sources (i.e., Gender Marker, ROAR, Gender Equality Seal, including AI driven analytics) for evidence-based decision-making and programming.

- Develop dashboards and visualizations to communicate complex findings in clear, compelling ways.

- Prepare policy briefs, reports, and presentations that translate data into actionable recommendations for stakeholders.

- Liaise with Regional Hubs’ Gender Teams and Country Offices to identify their data needs and interests; and contribute to strengthening their capacities in data collection and analysis for decision-making and programming.

- Provide content for the activities of the Global Gender Equality Community of Practice (CoP) and the Gender Equality Seal Learning Plan, drawing from data and lessons learned from the different workstreams.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Monitoring and Evaluation on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment.

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Data and Research on Gender Equality.

2030 Agenda People – Gender

- Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Development - Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches.

- Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management - Working with Evidence and Data

- Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Business Management - Portfolio Management

- Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity.

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment.

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in statistics, feminist economics, data science and analytics, gender studies and/or relevant related fields is required; OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor´s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with two additional years of relevant work experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of five (5) years (with Master’s degree) or seven (7) years (with Bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in accountability, reporting and/or data analysis is required.

- Technical expertise in gender equality is desired, with feminist economics as an added plus.

- Proven knowledge and experience in data science and analytics, including preprocessing, exploration, use and visualization of data for decision-making is desired, with AI driven data analytics as an added plus.

- Proven experience in producing quality reports in English is desired.

- Proven experience in coordination with diverse partners and stakeholders is desired, with experience in coordination with UN-System entities as an added plus.

- Proven knowledge and experience working with UN accountability tools is desired, with experience with UNDP accountability tools as an added plus.

- Proficiency in statistical software and data visualization tools is required.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

As part of the Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding Hub, UNDP’s Global Programme for Strengthening the Rule of Law, Human Rights, Justice and Security for Sustainable Peace and Development provides programmatic, policy and financial support to national partners in over 100 countries and territories. The Global Programme is widely recognized for its ability to mobilize funds, provide technical and strategic expertise, and collaborate and coordinate across UN entities to enable more holistic, coherent and comprehensive responses to rule of law, justice, security and human rights challenges. Phase V of the Global Programme for Strengthening the Rule of Law, Human Rights, Justice and Security for Sustainable Peace and Development, builds on experience, lessons and achievements during Phase IV and is guided by and aligned to UNDP’s 2026-2029 Strategic Plan.

The United Nations Team of Experts on the Rule of Law and Sexual Violence in Conflict (Team of Experts), based at the UN Headquarters in New York, deploys regularly to some of the world’s most challenging contexts. It has a unique “co-lead” structure comprised of the Department of Peace Operations (DPO), the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Sexual Violence in Conflict (SRSG-SVC) and UNDP.

Under the overall supervision of the Policy Advisor / Deputy Team Leader of the Team of Experts, within UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Team, the IPSA holder will support UNDP and the Team of Experts in advancing the implementation of the Framework of Cooperation on the Prevention and Response to Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (CRSV) between the Government of Ukraine and the United Nations. In addition, the IPSA holder provide support with outreach to Member States and EU institutions.

- Providing strategic and technical advice to the Ukraine team of the Team of Experts on the various workstreams implemented in Ukraine by the Team of Experts.

- Assisting in the full operationalization of Team of Experts’ projects in Ukraine, including the case management system procured for the Office of the Prosecutor General of Ukraine.

- Supporting the organization of training activities for Ukrainian authorities by drafting training materials and coordinating human resource and logistical.

- Deploying to Ukraine in support of the above-listed tasks.

2. Assist with outreach to Member States, including by:

- Supporting fundraising efforts for the Team of Experts through in-person and virtual engagement with Member States and the private sector.

- Organizing events to raise the profile of the Team of Experts.

- Accompanying senior leadership on key visits as requested, including the preparation of necessary background notes and talking points.

- Drafting and submitting project proposals in collaboration with relevant colleagues and following up with the Member States to which project proposals were submitted.

- Facilitating engagement and partnership-building with relevant UN entities and non-governmental organizations in Geneva and representing the Team of Experts at key events.

3. Foster the partnership between OSRSG-SVC/Team of Experts and EU institutions, including by:

- Maintaining regular contact with key EU officials to keep them updated on the Team of Experts' programmatic activities, while staying abreast of important political developments in Brussels.

- Organizing and assisting senior leadership with engagements in Brussels that raise the visibility of the conflict-related sexual violence mandate.

Lead workshops with senior level officials and stakeholders.

- Support establishment of knowledge platforms and innovative mechanisms for capturing and disseminating knowledge from the project; and ensure development of knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Within the Bureau for Management Services, the Office of Human Resources provides strategic leadership and advisory services to enable UNDP to attract, develop, engage and retain the people required to deliver on its mandate. The People Experience, Performance and Culture Unit (PEPCU) leads UNDP-wide approaches to employee experience and engagement, performance management, culture, respectful workplaces, and duty of care, including mental health and well-being.

The Mental Health and Well-being Team develops and coordinates organization-wide initiatives that prevent and address psychosocial risks, promotes a healthy and inclusive working environment, and enables personnel and managers to access timely information, resources and support. Its work is aligned with UNDP's People for 2030 Strategy, the United Nations System Mental Health and Well-being Strategy, and applicable ethical, confidentiality and data-protection standards.

The UNDP Well-being Coordinator supports two core pillars of the Well-being Function: Psychosocial Risk Management and Early Intervention, and Access to Psychosocial Support Services. The role coordinates psychosocial risk monitoring and follow-up, including analysis of Well-being Index and service-utilization data, identification of emerging risks and service gaps, and support to targeted intervention planning with offices, bureaux, business partnering team and other stakeholders. It also facilitates timely and equitable access to confidential psychosocial consultations, short-term support, referrals, care navigation, manager and HR consultations, and deployment-related psychosocial resources. The role contributes to limited individual or group psychosocial support, as well as the programme’s prevention, communications or learning portfolios.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Coordinate psychosocial risk management and early intervention

- Coordinate collection, validation and analysis of Well-being Index, service-utilization and other relevant data to identify psychosocial risk trends, offices requiring attention and emerging service gaps.

- Maintain a structured risk-monitoring process, including risk flags, office profiles and follow-up records, in line with confidentiality, data-protection and records-management requirements.

- Support consultations with Country Offices, Regional Bureaux, HR Business Partners, managers and staff counsellors to understand identified risks and contextual factors.

- Coordinate the development, documentation and follow-up of targeted psychosocial risk mitigation and early-intervention plans, escalating clinical or organizational concerns to the appropriate technical lead.

- Prepare quarterly psychosocial risk reports, leadership and HR briefings, dashboards and recommendations to support timely organizational decision-making.

2. Coordinate access to psychosocial support services

- Serve as a confidential coordination point for personnel, managers and HR colleagues seeking psychosocial consultation, information or support, and facilitate timely access to the appropriate service.

- Conduct initial psychosocial needs screening within professional competence, identify urgency and appropriate next steps, and escalate high-risk, complex or clinical cases to staff counsellors or emergency services in accordance with established protocols.

- Coordinate short-term psychosocial support pathways, referrals and care navigation to internal and external providers, including follow-up on access barriers and continuity of support.

- Maintain accurate, secure and confidential records of support requests, referrals, utilization and follow-up, ensuring appropriate separation of personal case information from aggregate programme reporting.

- Coordinate pre-deployment psychosocial briefings, resilience resources and referral information for personnel serving in high-risk or challenging operational contexts, in collaboration with the designated service provider and relevant units.

3. Manage service data, monitoring and reporting

- Maintain service-utilization, referral and case-management datasets and apply quality-control procedures to ensure completeness, consistency and confidentiality.

- Develop and maintain indicators, dashboards and reporting processes covering demand, access, response times, utilization, referral outcomes and geographic equity.

- Analyse quantitative and qualitative evidence to identify demand patterns, service gaps and emerging psychosocial risks, while safeguarding anonymity in organizational reporting.

- Prepare concise statistical reports, briefing notes and presentations for management and contribute relevant inputs to corporate well-being reporting.

- Use feedback and evaluation findings to recommend improvements to risk-monitoring processes, referral pathways, resource allocation and service accessibility.

4. Coordinate service delivery arrangements, partnerships and resources

- Coordinate external providers and internal partners supporting counselling, referrals, deployment support and other psychosocial services, and monitor service standards, coverage and follow-up.

- Maintain and periodically update the Referral and Care Navigation Framework, including clear pathways for routine, urgent, specialized and location-specific support, as needed.

- Maintain the Psychosocial Support Resource Hub with approved self-help materials, service information, referral guidance and deployment-related resources.

- Support service administration, including provider coordination, procurement, budget monitoring, documentation for payments and identification of delivery risks requiring management attention.

5. Contribute to prevention, communications, learning and broader programme delivery

- Contribute technical and coordination inputs to organization-wide prevention and mental health literacy initiatives led under other pillars of the Well-being Function.

- Support the development and delivery of awareness campaigns, such as October Mental Health Day, global well-being communications, webinars, learning sessions and practical resources for personnel and managers.

- Provide evidence from psychosocial risk monitoring and service-utilization trends to inform prevention priorities, learning content and targeted communications, while safeguarding confidentiality and anonymity.

- Assist with stakeholder coordination, event logistics, resource development, reporting and other programme responsibilities required to deliver the broader Well-being Function workplan, as needed.

The incumbent performs other duties within the functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization. Subject to professional qualifications, established protocols and available capacity, this may include brief individual or group psychosocial support, initial assessment and referral. The role does not independently manage emergencies, complex clinical cases or long-term counselling.

6. Institutional Arrangement

The Well-being Coordinator will report to the HR Specialist - Mental Health and Well-being Team Lead BMS/OHR/PEPCU.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking:

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Direction & Strategy - Effective Decision Making:

- Ability to take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one’s authority, area of expertise and resources.

Business Development - Human-centered Design

- Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process.

Business Management - Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Management - Risk Management

- Ability to interact with different levels of management and across different agencies and offices to obtain information, develop legal approaches and resolve issues, this skill includes liaison with counterparts and determining the best sequence in which to pursue an issue, were information, particularly for UNDP, may be across different independent UN agencies.

Legal - Managing Client Relations

- Ability to interact with different levels of management and across different agencies and offices to obtain information, develop legal approaches and resolve issues, this skill includes liaison with counterparts and determining the best sequence in which to pursue an issue, were information, particularly for UNDP, may be across different independent UN agencies.

HR Talent Management - Employee Engagement

- Knowledge of theories and models of human motivation and engagement including the predictors of employee engagement;

- Knowledge of and ability to guide application of tools, techniques, and processes to increase employee engagement;

- Knowledge of tools and methodologies to measure employee engagement and to identify its specific drivers;

- Knowledge of tools and methodologies to ensure regular engagement with personnel on key workplace matters, with a view to identifying the most pressing workplace issues.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Clinical or Organizational Psychology, Counselling, Social Work or Psychiatry required. OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum 2 years (with master’s degree) or 4 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in psychosocial programming, psychosocial risk monitoring, mental health service coordination, counselling, referral management or closely related work.

Required skills

- Experience in psychosocial risk assessment, needs analysis, early-intervention planning or the interpretation of workforce well-being data.

- Experience coordinating confidential psychosocial support requests, referrals, care navigation and follow-up across multiple locations or service providers.

- Knowledge of professional ethics, confidentiality, safeguarding, data protection and escalation protocols applicable to psychosocial services.

- Strong analytical, coordination, documentation and reporting skills, including the ability to translate evidence into practical recommendations for offices, managers and HR stakeholders.

Desired Experience, Knowledge, and skills

- Experience with the UN system, international organizations or geographically dispersed workforces.

- Experience using surveys, dashboards or case-management systems to monitor psychosocial risk, service demand, access and outcomes.

- Training or certification in trauma-informed practice, psychological first aid, suicide-risk response, case management or cross-cultural counselling.

- Experience coordinating psychosocial support for personnel in high-risk, crisis or deployment contexts.

Required Language(s) (at working level)

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in French is desired.

- Working knowledge of other UN language is an asset.

Professional Certificates

- Registration/License as a mental health professional in the country of origin or elsewhere is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, United Nations Organizations, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

Within UNCDF’s thematic are of nature, climate and energy financing, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Sustainable Energy 2 program, a 5 year program funded by the Central African Forestry Initiative (CAFI) and Fonds National de REDD+ (FONAREDD DRC), aims to scale up clean energy solutions to reduce deforestation and emissions, through building a diversified investment portfolio across clean fuels, renewable electrification, and sustainable biomass.

To continue driving these objectives, UNCDF seeks to hire an Administration and Finance Analyst for the Sustainable Energy 2 Program. The Administration and Finance Analyst will support the Energy Investment Program Manager in the day-to-day operations, reporting and activities, to ensure that the program is efficiently executed against donor-committed timelines.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administration and Finance Analyst will provide support in the effective financial management, administrative support, and compliance with UNCDF/UNDP rules and procedures. The incumbent will play a critical role in supporting program operations, managing budgets, overseeing procurement, and ensuring transparent and efficient use of resources.

Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Support to Project Planning and Management

- Assist in standardizing finance and accounting systems in accordance with UNDP and UNCDF procedures.

- Support preparation of annual work plans, budgets, budget revisions, procurement plans, and ensure proper system entry.

- Review budget revisions, financial plans, and ensure timely reporting and submission to relevant stakeholders.

Financial Management and Reporting

- Assist in monitoring project expenditure and cash flows to ensure compliance with approved budgets.

- Support quarterly Fund Authorization and Certification of Expenditures (FACE) reviews, cashbook and bank reconciliations.

- Prepare and maintain detailed financial records and reports, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

- Prepare and monitor budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.

- Ensure support in compliance with UNCDF/UNDP financial regulations and donor requirements.

- Support the consolidation of investee financial reports to inform annual financial reporting and plans, to the donor and to UNCDF.

Procurement and Contract Administration

- Support procurement processes, including preparation of requests for quotations/proposals and contract management in adherence to procurement policies and procedures.

- Maintain accurate records of procurement activities and vendor performance in line with UNCDF standards.

Administrative Support

- Oversee office operations, logistics, and asset management.

- Assist with events management, travel arrangements, and documentation and records management.

- Facilitate communication between project teams and partners.

Audit and Compliance

- Facilitate internal and external audits, ensuring timely submission of required documentation.

- Support the implementation of risk management and compliance measures.

Program Support and Coordination

- Support data collection for companies during due diligence process, when necessary.

- Provide administrative and financial input for program planning and reporting.

- Liaise with partners, government counterparts, and stakeholders on financial and administrative matters.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Knowledge of procurement processes and adherence to UNDP procurement policies.

Education:

• A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced (Master´s) University Degree in Finance and/or Accounting is required. Or

• A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

• Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

• Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.

• Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).

• Candidates with MBA or master’s in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Experience:

• Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience. Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of Finance and Operations in a national or international organization implementing the development projects, and/or leading and managing projects.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

• Familiarity with energy, climate, or investment-related programs.

Travels within the DRC for on-site project monitoring and financial spot check support may be required and will be paid for by UNCDF, in accordance with UNCDF travel policies. jobs.title: Executive Associate- [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
This vacancy is open to UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments of all nationalities. Other applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, or Switzerland.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy.

The Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan. BPPS’s staff provides technical advice to Country Offices; advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, South-South and Triangular cooperation initiatives, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts in close coordination and thematic synergy with the Crisis Bureau (CB).

The Front Office of BPPS is responsible for the smooth and seamless management of the substantive flow of information to and from BPPS, coordinating effective internal communications with BPPS teams, other Bureaus, the UNDP Executive Office, as well as communications with external partners. The Front Office plans and coordinates the BPPS Director and BPPS Deputy Director’s internal and external interactions and interventions based on priorities and agendas, in close collaboration with technical teams and other Bureaus as needed, ensuring the Director and Deputy Director’s successful provision of political leadership, strategic guidance, and managerial as well as programmatic priorities in full compliance with UNDP’s mandate.

With the opening of a new UNDP office in Madrid, where the BPPS Deputy Director and a number of BPPS teams will be relocating in the course of 2026, the Executive Associate will play a key role in supporting the establishment and smooth running of the new office, and its efficient interactions with the two other main BPPS locations (New York and Bonn).

Position Purpose:

Under the direct supervision of the BPPS Deputy Director and in coordination with their Special Assistant, the Executive Associate ensures that the Deputy Director receives the immediate administrative and operational support needed to execute their managerial functions. The incumbent works closely with both the Special Assistant and the Executive Associate of the Assistant Administrator and Director of BPPS, to strengthen coordination and complementarities in the Office of the Director and contribute toward the overall operations of the Front Office.

As one of the first points of contact with the Bureau for senior UNDP/UN staff and the full range of representatives of UNDP’s constituencies, the Executive Associate must deal with a heavy volume of requests and a wide range of highly sensitive matters under heavy time pressure.

Given the demands of protocol and interaction, often at high levels, the Executive Associate is required to perform the role with a calm demeanor under stressful circumstances, demonstrating efficiency and effectiveness in personal communication, knowledge of protocol, discretion and independent judgment, motivation and proactive attitude.

The key functions of the Executive Associate are to ensure:

- Effective and efficient functioning of the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS;

- Effective communications support to the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS;

- Support for effective relationship management by BPPS Directorate;

- Support the establishment and management of the new UNDP Office in Madrid

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensures effective and efficient functioning of the office of the Deputy Director, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Coordination and maintenance of calendar of meetings and activities of the Deputy Director, including organizing meetings, confirming the Deputy Director’s participation in senior and high-level meetings and events, drafting replies to invitations and meetings and implementing protocol procedures;

- Management of the Deputy Director’s missions and representation schedule, including travel arrangements, communications with meeting organizers/country offices on logistics; itinerary, travel requests in Quantum, follow-up on authorization, clearances, visas, accommodation, and tickets necessary for travel;

- Ensuring compliance with respect to administrative procedures, rules, regulations and systems,;

- Use of automated office management systems for effective functioning of the Deputy Director’s office; maintenance of contact lists and rosters of high-level partners;

- Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to the Deputy Director;

- Finance/accounts management support (i.e. processing payment requests, requisitions and claims pertaining to travels and retreats/ events) to the Deputy Director and Directorate;

- Support daily management of requests for reviews, approvals and clearances by the Deputy Director via email and DocuSign;

- Coverage and backstopping for the Executive Associate to the Director during peak times and absences

2. Ensures effective communications support to the office of the Deputy Director of BPPS, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Effective monitoring and screening of correspondence arriving in and/or leaving the Deputy Director’s office. Review of incoming correspondence for the Deputy Director’s attention and prioritizing of documents according to action required; review, proofreading, and editing of all correspondence for proper clearance prior to the Deputy Director’s signature;

- Presentation of proposals to the Deputy Director and/or Special Assistant to streamline office procedures between the BPPS front office and other Headquarters units;

- Drafting and preparation of correspondence, directives, comments on behalf of the Deputy Director for their signature and ensuring follow-up as needed;; and

- Appropriate filing, including through automated filing systems, and ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials.

- Acts as secretary to meetings as requested by the Deputy Director, including drafting minutes, follow-ups, and reporting;

- Supports liaison with local counterparts in Spain, including the front offices of local/ federal Ministry officials and other UN agencies.

3. Supports effective relationship management by BPPS front office, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Collaborate with the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director and broader BPPS front office in facilitating the Deputy Director’s interactions (in sensitive, political, diplomatic, and other instances) with various external partners of BPPS, such as ambassadors, donor country delegations, parliamentarians and high-level senior officials, as well as the Administrator and his office;

- Assist the Special Assistant to the Deputy Director in the research, obtaining and analysis of background materials for the preparation of presentations, talking points, briefings, meetings, official missions and appointments;

- Assist in the preparation of public information materials and folders, as requested;

- Support the organization of BPPS events such as townhalls, retreats or workshops, both at Headquarters and off-site; management of procurement of services, logistics, travel, visa, etc.

- Process the Deputy Director’s travel requests and post-travel functions in UNAll, in line with UNDP POPP, including calculation of DSA entitlements and claims and ensuring the timely settlement of claims.

- Process the Deputy Director’s travel fares in coordination with the local travel service (e.g. AMEX) in advance of missions.

4. Supports the establishment and smooth running of the new UNDP office in Madrid, in collaboration with the BMS focal point in Madrid, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Office management, including coordinating with BMS for the necessary inventory of the Deputy Director’s office supplies and IT needs, and ensuring the readiness or usability of office/ meeting/ event spaces (e.g. good connection of video conferencing equipment for hybrid meetings);

- Orientation for BPPS colleagues relocating to Madrid in collaboration with the BMS focal point in Madrid, including advising on necessary local registrations (e.g. to obtain the TIE [foreign ID card]), support for obtainment of UN Grounds Pass, and office security registrations;

- Act as liaison with New York and Bonn BPPS offices in order to optimize the new configuration of BPPS across three main offices;

- Act as point of contact to prepare visits from UNDP leadership, including coordinating with Headquarters on the visit programme, facilitating the necessary travel documents for visas, support to secure UN Grounds Pass where needed, and liaising with counterparts/ Ministries in Spain on logistics and the needful security protocols.

- Acts as logistics coordinator for events involving the Madrid office staff and/or premises (e.g. preparation for official meetings or events hosted in the Madrid office, procurement of services or meeting supplies etc.).

5. Facilitate knowledge building and management.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Organize specialized training as required.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is a pragmatic problem solver, and makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open-minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in the face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confronts discrimination

- Administration & Operations-Travel Policy and Procedures: Knowledge of travel policy and procedures; ability to interpret travel policy, the Staff Rules, administrative circulars, and financial regulations and rules on travel-related matters.

Background

Organizational Context

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, for six decades, UNDP works in some 170 countries and territories. UNDP has shaped the progress of human development, providing integrated support at scale to improve lives for millions of people worldwide. UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2026-2029 helps countries and communities in their progress towards high human development while protecting the planet through four strategic objectives – prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and healthy planet. The plan is powered by three accelerators: digital and AI transformation; gender equality; and sustainable finance. All are underpinned by a commitment to human rights and to leaving no one behind.

The Bureau for Advocacy and External Relations lead and supports UNDP to build and deliver essential strategic relationships and alliances. It creates and delivers a strong public narrative about the organization, impact of our work, and how we align with partners to identify and build solutions towards achieving sustainable development. The Bureau also leads UNDP’s work with traditional donors, as well as building innovative and diversified funding relationships. BERA communications enable strong political and financial backing by providing partners and supporters with a clear understanding of what UNDP does and how our mission, capabilities and services reinforce global, regional, and national development priorities. BERA leads efforts to optimally position UNDP within the UN Development System, with Member States and in the inter-governmental and inter-agency fora. It identifies strategic opportunities to partner with agencies through multi-stakeholder and bilateral platforms. It provides intelligence, advises on relationships with key political constituencies, incl. UN Member states, G77 and China, WEOG, EU, Executive Board and develops strategies. BERA coordinates and sets corporate standards across the functions of political positioning, partnerships, marketing and communications within UNDP and leads on internal communications.

Within BERA, the Communications Group leads and manages external communications through strategy, media, digital communications, marketing, branding and global storytelling. The Visibility and Impact for Partnerships (VIP) Team supports UNDP’s flexible funding goals by enhancing visibility for and with partners and demonstrating the alignment between partner priorities and UNDP’s work, results and impact. The Team develops targeted partner visibility and engagement approaches; equips the organization with messages, creative assets, tools and guidance; and works to strengthen partner recognition and reach priority audiences. The Team also helps connect Goodwill Ambassadors, advocates and other influential voices to donor communications, high-profile engagements and resource mobilization priorities.

Job Purpose

Communications Specialist, Celebrity Relations is part of the Visibility and Impact for Partnerships Team. Under the guidance and direct supervision of the Team Leader, Visibility and Impact for Partnerships, the incumbent will lead UNDP’s corporate Goodwill Ambassador and celebrity relations function and manage communications initiatives and opportunities involving Goodwill Ambassadors, Advocates, influencers and other high-profile supporters.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling of multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration

Duties and Responsibilities

1) Organize and manage the day-to day Goodwill Ambassador Programme

- Working closely with the Visibility and Impact for Partnerships Team Leader, act as the corporate focal point and relationship manager for existing global Goodwill Ambassadors and Advocates, working with them to plan engagement with UNDP.

- Position Goodwill Ambassadors across media and social media platforms, at events, in country visits and in engagement with partners.

- Initiate and contribute to drafting and editing of communications materials, including speeches and talking points, press kits, fact sheets, infographics and multimedia products, relevant to Goodwill Ambassador events, appearances, participation in campaigns and other communications outreach.

- Contribute to organizing relevant press events and media moments, and position UNDP senior staff and Goodwill Ambassadors in press launches and media coverage.

2) Expand and strengthen the Goodwill Ambassador Programme

- Develop and implement comprehensive corporate communications planning for Goodwill Ambassadors and other celebrity supporters, including developing targets for outreach and impact, and integrating Goodwill Ambassadors into resource mobilization efforts.

- Identify and recruit potential new Goodwill Ambassadors, work to orient them and continue to support them in their engagement with UNDP.

- Work as the HQ Coordinator with the UNDP Geneva Office for the Match Against Poverty and European-based sports Goodwill Ambassadors, helping to strengthen the Match Against Poverty into an integrated communications and resource mobilization initiative.

- Support Goodwill Ambassador field missions and engagement with UNDP’s donors and partners.

3.) Advice and support other UNDP offices with celebrity management and artist relations.

- Advise Country Offices and Bureaus on recruitment and management of national or regional GWAs.

- Coordinate with Country Offices and other Bureaus to connect global UNDP Goodwill Ambassadors to national or regional efforts as appropriate.

4.) Advise and support the wider work of the Visibility and Impact for Partnerships Team as and when required and facilitate knowledge management

- Identify opportunities to use Goodwill Ambassadors, Advocates, influencers and other high-profile supporters in targeted partner communications and visibility plans, including in priority donor countries and emerging partner markets.

- Design integrated engagement plans for partner events, country visits, campaigns and other high-profile moments, with clear objectives, audiences, roles, risk considerations, content requirements and follow-up actions.

- Work with the Partnerships Group, Representation Offices, Regional Bureaux, Country Offices and corporate communications teams to align celebrity engagement with partner priorities and produce communications content that showcases UNDP’s results and the value of partner contributions.

- Provide substantive and sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice including corporate communications repositories.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized SEAH, IT forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership.

Position Purpose

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) functionally reports to the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, under the overall supervision of the Deputy Director (Investigations). Under the supervision of the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1, the primary role of the Team Lead (HQ/LAC) is to oversee, supervise and conduct investigations into alleged misconduct that falls within OAI’s mandate, as outlined in ‘Organizational Context’ above, and that relates to UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean region.

The Investigations Team Lead (HQ/LAC) will supervise the work of the team, including but not limited to Investigators at the P3 level and all other personnel assigned to the investigation team covering UNDP Headquarters and the Latin America and Caribbean, and will complete their annual performance appraisals.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

Lead investigations management and lead and manage Headquarters / Latin America and Caribbean (HQ/LAC) team

- Under the overall supervision of the Chief, Investigations, provides day‑to‑day operational leadership of the HQ/LAC Investigations Team, ensuring the effective delivery of investigative activities in line with OAI priorities, policies, and performance expectations.

- Manages the assigned investigative portfolio, including allocation of cases, prioritization of workstreams, workload balancing, and monitoring of progress to ensure investigations are completed timely, efficiently, and to a high professional standard, escalating risks and capacity issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Overseas and directs investigations, ensuring that appropriate investigative strategies are developed, all relevant lines of inquiry are pursued, and investigative resources are deployed proportionately and effectively.

- Reviews and edits of investigation reports prepared by team investigators and other relevant documents to ensure they are of a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations.

- Leads and personally conduct investigations only in complex, high‑risk, or sensitive matters, while otherwise providing technical direction, oversight, and quality assurance to investigations conducted by team members.

- Provides first line managerial and functional supervision to investigators and other personnel assigned to the team, including setting expectations, clarifying priorities, and ensuring alignment with OAI standards and values.

- Conducts regular and structured case and performance reviews with team members to assess investigative progress, identify quality or procedural gaps, and provide corrective direction where necessary.

- Holds direct accountability for the quality, timeliness, and defensibility of investigative outputs produced by the team prior to submission to the Chief, including investigation reports, findings, and recommendations.

- Identifies and addresses underperformance, skills gaps, or conduct issues at first instance through coaching, feedback, and performance management measures, escalating matters to the Chief in accordance with UNDP procedures where required.

- Ensures that investigations conducted by the team comply with international investigative standards, UNDP legal and policy frameworks, and OAI Investigation Guidelines and Standard Operating Procedures.

- Ensures due process, confidentiality, information security, and victim‑centered approaches are consistently applied, particularly in sensitive cases involving sexual misconduct, retaliation, or abuse of authority.

- Oversee the collection, handling, analysis, and safeguarding of evidence, ensuring proper chain of custody and appropriate handling of physical, digital, and testimonial evidence.

- Identifies investigative, procedural, or institutional risks emerging from casework and escalates systemic or high‑risk issues to the Chief to inform broader oversight, mitigation, or proactive responses.

- Oversees and promotes the effective use of investigative technologies, including case management systems, analytical software, open‑source intelligence tools, and artificial intelligence–enabled solutions, to enhance investigative efficiency, accuracy, and timeliness.

- Guides team members in the responsible and ethical use of AI and advanced analytics, ensuring compliance with confidentiality, due process, and information security requirements.

- Identifies opportunities to streamline investigative processes, improve workflows, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives under the strategic direction of the Chief.

- Acts as a key operational interlocutor with internal stakeholders (including legal services, HR, ethics, procurement, and management) on investigative matters, escalating sensitive or high‑impact issues to the Chief as appropriate.

- Ensures that case records, databases, and documentation for matters under the team’s responsibility are accurate, complete, and up to date, supporting institutional accountability and auditability.

- Formulates and recommends case closure decisions, including assessments of evidentiary sufficiency and proportionality, for review and approval by the Chief.

- Supports the Chief through the provision of operational briefings, trend information, and case‑related inputs relevant to regional or functional oversight.

- Undertakes and, where appropriate, leads investigative missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including in hardship or hazardous duty locations, providing on‑site leadership and oversight for investigative activities.

- Sets the appropriate professional tone and workplace culture within the team, leading by example through ethical conduct, collaboration, and respect; fosters a culture of constructive, collective problem‑solving, open dialogue, and shared accountability; and actively models and reinforces behaviors that support teamwork, learning, and continuous improvement.

- Performs other duties within the functional profile as required for the effective functioning of the Investigations Section and the Office.

- Plans the work of the HQ/LAC Team and distributes workload among the HQ/LAC Team appropriately.

- Provides senior expertise and advice to the HQ/LAC Team so that the work of the HQ/LAC Team is performed in the most professional, efficient and timely manner.

- Appraises the performance of the HQ/LAC personnel.

- Recruit personnel for the HQ/LAC Team as necessary.

- Leads by example, setting the tone for the HQ/LAC Team. Consciously builds a supportive, collegiate and positive team culture within the HQ/LAC Team.

- Works collectively and professionally with peers to provide thought leadership and constructive challenge to ensure that the HQ/LAC Team is a dynamic, reflective unit that keeps pace with best practice.

- Actively engages and promotes discussions aimed at continued improvement of the HQ/LAC Team and the investigation function, ensuring highest impact and efficient, effective practices.

- Supervises staff and non-staff personnel in the HQ/LAC Team and provides clear, fair, support, and balanced performance feedback and reviews.

- Engages productively, professionally, collaboratively and efficiently with peers, team members, and parties internal and external to the Section to problem-solve as necessary, seek solutions and achieve positive and impactful collective outputs.

- Actively employs management techniques that ensure balance in prioritizing quality output of a high standard and a healthy workplace culture.

- Ensure field work and mission travel, which are mandatory for the position.

Ensure efficient Client Services.

- Maintains a role as a visible, active and accessible team leader, including by liaising with senior officials within the region and bureau; sharing insights from the caseload with senior managers; receiving and considering feedback on OAI investigation services; participating in regional or country level conferences or meetings to raise awareness of fraud and other control risk mitigation services.

- Liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, Regional Offices and counterparts, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

- Liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

- Where appropriate, provides advisory support to policy managers to help strengthen risk controls within UNDP, drawing on insights gleaned from the caseload.

Facilitate knowledge management and other tasks

- Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI.

- Assesses the potential for misconduct in UNDP offices and operations.

- Contributes to risk assessment planning.

- Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

- Keeps abreast of the jurisprudence of the United Nations Dispute Tribunal (UNDT) and United Nations Appeals Tribunal (UNAT).

- Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Chief, Investigations, Unit 1 and/or Deputy Director (Investigations).

- Contributes to knowledge‑sharing, lessons‑learned, and capacity‑building initiatives within OAI, supporting the strengthening of investigative practice across the Section.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervise and manage Investigation Specialists and support staff, Non-personnel, Interns.

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.
