jobs.title: Operations Associate, Volunteer Lifecycle Management (Open to internal & external applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of Work

The Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end UN Volunteer lifecycle services, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant execution of operational processes from onboarding through separation across multiple countries and stakeholders.

3.1 Provision of Volunteer Lifecycle Services

- Facilitae processing of assignments from offer issuance through entry on duty and separation, including offer and/or contract generation and management, benefits & entitlements, life events, separations, verification of documentation and required clearances.

- Review, validate and follow up on pre-assignment requirements, including PII updates, mandatory courses, beneficiary information, banking details, medical clearance, etc.

- Administer volunteer contracts and manage lifecycle processes, including benefits, entitlements, claims, and life events in line with the UNV Conditions of Service.

- Handle complex and sensitive cases, including medical and security evacuations, contract amendments, resignations, terminations, and recovery of overpayments, ensuring confidentiality and compliance.

- Administer and certify processing of benefits in full compliance with applicable provisions of the UN COS.

3.2 Data Management and Compliance

- Review validate, and record supporting documentation and transactions in corporate systems to ensure accuracy for payroll processing, reporting, and audit purposes.

- Support payroll-related administration by reviewing payment requests, ensuring completeness and alignment with the COS, following up on HR data corrections, and coordinating on payroll and banking exceptions, including returned or rejected payments where applicable.

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date records and case history in relevant systems, ensuring full traceability and proper documentation of all actions.

- Ensure all activities are compliant with applicable policies, procedures, and internal control frameworks.

3.4 Coordination and Client Service Delivery

- Liaise with Regional Offices, Field Units, UN entities, and internal teams to coordinate service delivery and resolve operational queries and ensure consistent application of policies and procedures.

- Provide guidance to stakeholders, including UN Volunteers, on lifecycle processes, documentation requirements and service-related matters, and ensure timely follow-up on pending actions and exceptional case.

- Support handling, follow=up, and escalation of operational queries and cases in line with established workflows, ensuring appropriate communication and resolution.

3.5 Monitoring, Issue Resolution and Risk Management

- Monitor the progress of lifecycle cases and service transactions across deployment, contract administration, payroll and separation.

- Identify risks, delays, or inconsistencies and escalate issues as appropriate.

- Support timely resolution of operational issues, coordinating with relevant teams and service providers where required.

3.6 Knowledge Management

- Contribute to the review and continuous improvement of workflows, standard operating procedures and templates by identifying bottlebecks and operational gaps.

- Provide inputs for preparation of knowledge articles, frequently asked questions (FAQ) and best practices. Support knowledge sharing through development of training materials, guidance notes, and lessons learned.

- Participate in knowledge networks and communities of practice.

3.7 The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Operations Associate will report to the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the location under the substantive guidance of the P3 Operations Specialist and overall leadership of Deputy Chief, Volunteer Services Centre (VSC).

Competencies

CORE

Achieve Results

- Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

- Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

- Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

- Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

- Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

- Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

- Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Managing Compensation and Benefits

- Ability to design compensation plans which are aligned to current and future organization needs and market conditions; knowledge of and ability to apply the ICSC compensation methodologies and principles.

- Knowledge of and ability to design benefits-related processes, programmes, and tools, including benefit enrolment and amendments.

Payroll management:

- Knowledge of and ability to apply mechanisms and tools to collect payroll data, process payroll and manage payroll reports.

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

- Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy.

- Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests.

- Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Operations management

- Ability to effectively plan, organize, and oversee the Organization’s business processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner.

- Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skillfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for content, or responsive to a stated need.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary Education with at least six (6) years relevant work experience, or Bachelors’ degree in Human Resources, Business or Public Administration, with relevant work experience of at least three (3) years will be given due consideration.

Experience:

- Minimum Minimum 3-6 years of experience in client services provision, is required at the national or international level, including some experience in the area of HR transactions, recruitments, benefits and entitlements administration

Required Skills

- Advance user of MS Office packages (MS Word, Excel etc.).

- Experience in handling of web-based management systems.

- Proficiency in using collaboration tools, as well as familiarity with digital platforms and new technologies.

Desired skills

- Demonstrated knowledge of integrated HR management systems.

- Experience working in web-based management/CRM systems.

- Experience in an international or non-profit context would be an asset.

- Experience working with volunteers would be an asset.

Languages:

- Fluency in English, French and Arabic is required.

Professional Certificates:

- HR certification desirable although not required.

Disclaimer:

- Only short-listed applicants will be contacted.

- The successful candidate will hold a UNDP NPSA contract.

- This vacancy announcement is open to all applicants

- Open to nationals of Tunisia ONLY

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: ICT Analyst, Short-Term
jobs.description:
Background

Over the past three decades, corruption has remained one of the most persistent and structurally embedded challenges confronting the Republic of Moldova. The anti-corruption reforms initiated over the years have, for the most part, been normatively correct, yet lacking in real transformative impact in practice. At the same time, the phenomenon affected multiple sectors and manifested in increasingly sophisticated forms, ranging from petty administrative corruption to organised crime, large-scale fraud, and money laundering. The combination of perceived impunity, selective enforcement, and lengthy proceedings in corruption-related cases has contributed to a general belief that accountability mechanisms remain fragile. This environment has, in turn, affected citizens’ trust in the state’s ability to prevent, detect, investigate, and sanction corruption and related financial crimes in an effective and impartial manner.

In this context, UNDP has been engaged in the implementation of the EU funded “Support in Combating and Preventing Corruption and Organized Crime in the Republic of Moldova” project.

The project seeks to reduce corruption and financial crime, including money laundering, by strengthening effective, efficient, independent, and accountable justice, prosecution, and investigation systems. It responds to persistent weaknesses in Moldova’s anti-corruption framework, including fragmented institutional interventions, limited inter-institutional coordination, uneven implementation of integrity mechanisms, gaps in specialized expertise, and insufficient use of analytical and risk-based approaches. These challenges have limited the ability of public institutions to translate policy and legislative reforms into sustainable and measurable results.

The project is closely aligned with Moldova’s European Union accession agenda, the National Programme for Accession to the European Union 2025–2029, and the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme 2024–2028. The latter provides the principal national framework for mainstreaming integrity and anti-corruption measures across public institutions, while the National Anti-Corruption Centre is responsible for coordinating, monitoring, and evaluating its implementation. The project will support the application of EU standards and relevant OECD and GRECO recommendations, strengthen institutional ownership, and promote preventive, risk-based, and evidence-driven approaches to integrity management.

Digital transformation will serve as an important enabling element of the UNDP-led component, supporting more effective monitoring, reporting, analysis and institutional coordination. The project will facilitate the development, adaptation and use of digital tools and platforms for cross-institutional data collection, visualization, analytical reporting, integrity monitoring, risk identification, learning and stakeholder engagement. This may include digital dashboards, improvements to existing governmental and civic platforms, online learning solutions, and interoperability between relevant information systems. The interventions will be developed in close cooperation with beneficiary institutions to ensure that the solutions are user-friendly, responsive to institutional needs, technically sustainable and capable of supporting evidence-based decision-making, policy adjustments and long-term institutional ownership.

Through these interventions, the component is expected to establish a more coherent, preventive and data-informed integrity system, improve institutional accountability and interoperability, strengthen national ownership of digital solutions, and enable public authorities to identify and address corruption risks more systematically. The ICT Analyst will support the implementation of this digital portfolio by ensuring that the solutions developed or enhanced under the component are technically feasible, secure, interoperable, user-centred and sustainable within the national institutional environment.

Duties and Responsibilities

The ICT Analyst will support the end-to-end implementation of digital solutions under the UNDP-led component, ensuring structured planning, technical design, procurement support, implementation monitoring and quality assurance in line with UNDP standards and beneficiary requirements. The Analyst will translate institutional and analytical needs into functional and technical specifications, support the selection and coordination of external service providers, monitor technical deliverables, and help ensure that developed solutions meet agreed requirements and are fit for institutional use.

The Analyst will also support testing, validation, deployment and handover of digital tools, including monitoring dashboards, analytical solutions, interoperability arrangements and enhancements to relevant government or civic platforms. Particular attention will be given to system usability, data quality, interoperability, sustainability, and effective knowledge transfer to beneficiary institutions.

Through this support, the ICT Analyst will help ensure that digital interventions under Component 3 are coherent, practical, institutionally owned and capable of strengthening data-driven monitoring, integrity risk analysis, reporting and evidence-based decision-making across public institutions.

In addition, the ICT Analyst will serve as the principal technical focal point between UNDP, the National Anti-Corruption Centre, other beneficiary institutions, government ICT entities, service providers and relevant stakeholders, ensuring that digital solutions under the UNDP-led component are appropriately designed, procured, implemented, integrated and handed over in line with institutional needs, applicable national requirements and UNDP quality standards

The ICT Analyst applies and promotes the principles of results-based management (RBM), as well as a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. S/he is responsible and accountable to the Project Board for the project results within the limits of the assigned project.

The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

1. ICT advisory and digital solution design:

- Conduct ICT needs assessments covering existing systems, databases, reporting processes, institutional workflows and user capacities.

- Translate institutional and operational requirements into functional and technical specifications for digital products and system improvements.

- Provide technical advice on the design and configuration of digital monitoring dashboards for the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme.

- Support the development of digital tools for cross-institutional reporting, data collection, validation, analysis, visualization and preparation of data-driven reports.

- Support the configuration of dashboards for monitoring integrity and work ethics guidelines, mitigation measures and sectoral corruption risks.

- Advise on indicators, reporting templates, data fields, validation rules, visualization formats and access permissions.

- Advise on the use or adaptation of existing governmental platforms, including MLearn, reLAWed, e-Expertise and Particip.gov.md, where relevant.

- Assess interoperability requirements between project-supported solutions and existing government information systems.

- Advise on data governance arrangements, including data ownership, access rights, institutional responsibilities and data-quality requirements.

- Support the standardization of data structures, definitions and reporting formats across participating institutions.

- Recommend appropriate technologies, hosting arrangements, licensing options and maintenance approaches.

- Ensure that proposed digital solutions are user-friendly, accessible, interoperable and suitable for sustainable administration by beneficiary institutions.

- Liaise with third-party service providers and technical partners to ensure effective collaboration, coherent implementation

2. Procurement and vendor support:

- Prepare technical inputs for Terms of Reference, technical specifications, statements of work and evaluation criteria for ICT products and services.

- Define functional requirements, minimum technical standards, expected deliverables and acceptance criteria.

- Develop technical requirements for software development, dashboard configuration, hosting, system integration, maintenance and technical support.

- Support market assessments and comparative analyses of available ICT solutions.

- Review licensing, intellectual property, data ownership and maintenance provisions for proposed solutions.

- Participate in the technical evaluation of proposals, bids, demonstrations and prototypes in accordance with UNDP procedures.

- Prepare technical clarification questions and provide technical inputs during procurement processes.

- Review suppliers’ proposed methodologies, technical solutions, implementation approaches and deliverables.

- Liaise with service providers and beneficiary institutions to clarify technical requirements and address implementation issues.

- Review technical deliverables submitted by contractors and provide recommendations on their acceptance or revision.

- Provide independent quality assurance of the developer’s deliverables, verifying compliance with functional specifications and agreed standards.

- Review and validate system functionalities and workflow configurations delivered by the developer, flagging risks, gaps, or deviations in a timely manner.

- Support the project team with regular status updates, including progress tracking, identification of bottlenecks, and recommended priority actions.

3. Implementation, quality assurance and capacity building:

- Coordinate technical activities with the Project Team, beneficiary institutions, government ICT entities, suppliers and relevant development partners.

- Facilitate consultations between institutional users, policy specialists, data specialists and ICT service providers.

- Participate in technical working groups, project meetings and coordination forums, as required.

- Monitor the technical implementation of ICT activities and identify delays, dependencies and implementation challenges.

- Provide regular technical updates on progress, outstanding issues and recommended actions.

- Prepare technical assessments, briefing notes, progress inputs and recommendations for UNDP and beneficiary institutions.

- Monitor institutional adoption and use of the digital solutions, including functionality, data quality and user feedback.

- Document technical decisions, implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices.

- Identify opportunities for compatibility and complementarity with other national digitalization initiatives.

- Perform other ICT-related tasks required for the effective implementation of Component 3.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The ICT Analyst will work under the supervision of the Project Manager and Effective Governance Cluster Lead, in close cooperation with Programme, Operations, Communications and other teams in the Country Office (CO) for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery.

In addition to internal collaboration, the incumbent maintains effective working relationships with implementing partners, government counterparts, civil society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders. This includes participating in coordination meetings, joint planning processes, and field missions, where applicable. The role also involves contributing to knowledge exchange and lessons learned within the project and across the broader UNDP portfolio. Throughout the assignment, the Analyst ensures full compliance with UNDP’s operational standards and promotes the organization’s values, including transparency, inclusivity, and accountability.

He/She will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment. The PSA holder will be responsible for providing her/his own working station (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, specific software, etc.) and must have access to a reliable internet connection. All communications and documentation related to the assignment will be in Romanian and/or English.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Information Management & Technology - User Experience and Business Analyst

- Capacity to translate efficiently users’ needs into IT requirements around human-centered design principles. Knowledge of Oracle Cloud, Service Now, SalesForce.com, and Microsoft product an asset.

Information Management & Technology - IT Project Management

- Capacity to manage ICT projects, using IT methodologies and approaches such as agile deployment and/or waterfall system development methods. PMP and PRINCE2 certification or equivalent desirable.

Business Management - Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Information Management & Technology - Solutions Architecture

- Ability to design and manage the Information system architecture supporting corporate business processes.

- Design integration strategies and approaches to integrate one or more applications or services to maintain a coherent and effective IT architecture.

- Knowledge of OWASP, ITIL, ISO/IEC 270002 and IT operations.

Information Management & Technology - IT Quality Management

- Ability to manage quality of IT services. ISO 9001, 20000.Certification in ITIL desirable.

Digital - Digital product management

- Ability to design and lead digital product development including testing, ongoing product iteration, product strategy and delivery.

2030 Agenda: People - Gender

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybernetics, IT Management or a related field relevant to the position is required; OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s Degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of Master`s degree.

Experience:

Required skills:

- Demonstrated experience in supporting the implementation, enhancement or management of information systems, digital platforms or other ICT solutions.

Desired skills:

- Demonstrated experience in conducting ICT/business needs assessments and translating institutional or operational requirements into functional and/or technical specifications.

- Professional experience in user administration, and/or information security, accessibility requirements, and/or the application of internationally recognized ICT standards and best practices in ITC project implementation (e.g. OWASP, ITIL, ISO/IEC 27001/27002).

- Professional experience in applying the Republic of Moldova’s ICT policies, regulatory framework and engaging with key sector-related stakeholders.

- Previous professional experience in supporting public institutions and/or law enforcement bodies.

- Practical knowledge of business intelligence, analytical dashboards and data visualization tools, including Microsoft Power BI or equivalent solutions.

- Previous professional experience in working with international organizations, including UN Agencies, USAID, World Bank, etc.

jobs.title: Finance Specialist (Payroll Finance Oversight (PFO)) - Open to internal and external applicants who are nationals of the EU, EEA and Switzerland)
jobs.description:
Background

The Bureau for Management Services’ Office of Financial Resources Management (BMS/OFRM) supports the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in the implementation of the 2030 agenda and UNDP’s Strategic Plan. It achieves this by developing and making fully operational a dynamic and harmonized integrated resource management framework based on comprehensive analysis that enhances UNDP’s financial and administrative performance, as well as facilitating UN reform and coherence. The primary role of BMS/ OFRM is to maintain the financial integrity of UNDP through providing functional leadership, supporting the efficient and effective management of its financial resources, promoting financial sustainability and responsible resource allocation. This is accomplished by the development and implementation of sound financial policies and practices, oversight of corporate financial management performance, and flexible scalable support to resource allocation. BMS/OFRM serves as a business partner to Bureaux and Country Offices, providing sound financial management, advisory and analytical services, with a view to continuously improve the financial management performance of business units and support Bureaux in the exercising of their oversight functions.

Within OFRM, the Financial Performance Management & Reporting (FPMR) is responsible for oversight of financial reporting, the preparation and integrity of UNDP’s financial statements, and providing timely and accurate financial information in accordance with international accounting standards. FPMR fosters trust and accountability through leadership in financial policy, robust internal financial controls, and close engagement with auditors to support an unqualified audit opinion, while also delivering expert accounting and financial advisory support, addressing complex and non-routine financial issues, and overseeing financial risk related to implementing partners, enabling informed senior decision-making and sustained audit assurance.

Within FPMR, there are four units:

Corporate Financial Reporting (CFR): Responsible for promoting clear accountability for financial transactions and for producing UNDP’s corporate financial statements.

Financial Performance Management (FPM): Responsible for managing aspects of financial performance, including the administration of the Annual Representation exercise and the Statement of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting; monitoring of financial risks related to financial statement integrity; and management of the implementing partners policy framework, including the agency-wide Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers (HACT) framework.

Payroll Finance Oversight (PFO): Responsible for the financial oversight of payroll accounting functions, as well as the reporting of employee benefits and liabilities for all UNDP personnel.

Finance Integration & Technologies (FIT): provides expert, structured financial analysis to resolve complex, non-routine issues and enhance the quality and timeliness of senior decision-making.

Scope of Work:

The Payroll Finance Oversight (PFO) function provides financial oversight and governance over UNDP’s global payroll operations. PFO ensures the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of payroll-related financial information by establishing and monitoring controls, reviewing payroll accounting, overseeing compliance with applicable policies and financial rules, and assessing payroll-related financial risks. In fulfilling its mandate, PFO partners closely with and interacts regularly with the Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) to align operational processes with financial governance objectives. The function acts as a critical second-line capability, supporting management through analysis, issue resolution, and coordination with service providers and internal stakeholders, while safeguarding the organization against financial, compliance, and reputational risk arising from payroll activities.

Within the Payroll Finance Oversight (PFO) function, the Finance Specialist provides specialized technical expertise and serves as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) on payroll accounting, providing technical oversight, monitoring, and analysis of payroll expenses and related balance sheet accounts. The Finance Specialist works closely with the Global Payroll Services (GPS) and Benefits Entitlement Services (BES) teams within the Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) to strengthen payroll finance processes, advise on payroll system configuration and accounting treatments to mitigate risk, and review higher-risk transactions, providing assurance over IPSAS-compliant financial recording and reporting and contributing to reduced audit risk.

Duties and Responsibilities

Establish effective payroll finance oversight and policy implementation:

- Review and maintain payroll-related financial policies, procedures, and accounting treatments affecting the financial statements, including inter-agency balances, payables, and employee benefit liabilities.

- Assess and strengthen the payroll control environment, including Quantum ERP (Oracle HCM) application controls, system configuration, and audit trails, proposing process and system improvements to enhance efficiency and risk management.

- Lead the review of payroll accounting mappings and centralized processes from Quantum ERP (Oracle HCM) through to the General Ledger, including review of segregation of duties and compliance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) and industry best practices.

- Design, develop and maintain payroll oversight tools and reports (e.g. exception reports, dashboards, and models) to support monitoring, analysis, and periodic reporting of payroll costs and employee benefits.

- Provide technical oversight of payroll-related financial risks, including employee benefits, staff receivables and advances, inter-agency transfers, and unrecovered balances.

Contribute to the preparation of IPSAS-compliant financial statements and other corporate financial reports, including:

- Planning and preparation activities, including researching applicable reporting requirements, assessing materiality, and determining reporting scope. This requires in-depth knowledge of IPSAS standards, including complex areas such as revenue recognition, leases, transfer expenses, financial instruments, employee benefits, property, plant and equipment, intangible assets, provisions and contingencies, foreign currency translation, consolidation…etc.

- Leading, as required, the financial statement compilation process and preparing the primary financial statements and related notes.

- Overseeing or performing analytical reviews, including year-over-year trend analysis, ratio analysis, and investigation of variances, for management review.

- Preparing draft briefing notes and talking points, including high-level insights on financial performance and the impact of changes in accounting standards, assumptions, or estimates.

Establish payroll controls to comply with the Statement of Internal Control over Financial Reporting (SICFR):

- Develop and maintain payroll-related risk and control matrices in line with SICFR requirements, clearly documenting risks, key controls, and ownership.

- Lead annual control testing (as needed) for payroll processes and accounts, including walkthroughs, sample-based testing, and assessments of control design and operating effectiveness.

- Lead on identification of control gaps, recommend remediation actions, and oversee completion of corrective measures to timely closure, providing management with control effectiveness assessments for SICFR assertions.

- Lead preparation of payroll-specific inputs and documentation to support SICFR certification and overall financial reporting assurance.

- Liaise with OAI and external auditors on payroll-related SICFR testing, documentation, and evidence requests.

- Lead and promote strong SICFR compliance by advising on documentation standards, evidence retention, and control responsibilities, and by recommending system and process enhancements (including Quantum ERP (Oracle HCM) and GL configuration) to strengthen the payroll control environment.

Perform payroll finance oversight and analytical functions, including:

- Design, implement and maintain an efficient and effective monitoring strategy for payroll-related General Ledger (GL) accounts, with a focus on material and higher-risk balances and transactions.

- Perform periodic reviews of payroll-related GL accounts, transactions, reconciliations between Quantum ERP (Oracle HCM) and the GL, and related adjustment journals to ensure compliance with IPSAS and UNDP policies.

- Oversee staff advances and payroll receivable accounts, provide aged balance analyses to offices, and support the resolution of outstanding balances, including guidance on write-offs in line with established procedures.

- Liaise with offices, ITM, and system vendors to troubleshoot payroll accounting issues and support system configuration, enhancements, and testing related to payroll GL accounts.

- Conduct complex analyses and engage with actuaries and third-party administrators to assess employee benefit liabilities (including ASHI, pensions, medical insurance, and leave) and review third-party administrator performance and stewardship reporting.

Establish risk-informed financial policies and procedures, as follows:

- Lead research and risk analysis to inform the development of financial policies aligned with UNDP’s risk management framework and appetite.

- Lead in drafting and updating financial policies and procedures that incorporate risk mitigation measures and reflect operational needs.

- Benchmark policies against international standards and peer organization practices to ensure quality and relevance.

- Engage stakeholders to gather feedback and ensure policies are risk-informed, user-friendly, and contextually appropriate.

- Lead ongoing policy review and refinement based on implementation feedback, emerging risks, and evolving best practices.

Support internal and external audit and assurance processes, including the annual UNDP financial audit conducted by the United Nations Board of Auditors (UNBOA), by:

- Managing audit requests and queries through professional and timely responses; preparing and validating transaction samples and audit evidence tied to the general ledger and source documentation; and facilitating walkthroughs of key financial processes and internal controls.

- Supporting post-audit follow-up and year-round audit readiness, including contributing to management responses and representation letters, reviewing audit reports and financial statement adjustments, documenting lessons learned, maintaining robust audit trails and reconciliations, and supporting internal control assessments and continuous improvement initiatives.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and sharing:

- Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in Finance.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement:

- The position is part of a team of three staff members, including the supervisor, and has no direct reports.

Competencies

Core:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3:

- Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3:

- Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3:

- Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3:

- Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3:

- Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3:

- Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3:

- Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical:

Finance - Accounting (general):

- Knowledge of accounting concepts, principles, frameworks, standards, regulations, policies and trends, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations.

Finance - Financial risk management:

- Ensures financial resilience through proactive assessment of risk, implementation of controls and taking mitigating action.

- Understands risk and reward in relation to collaborative and commercial projects. Ensures a culture of positive risk management.

Finance - Financial and process innovation:

- Financial and business process engineering expertise required to innovate, design, change and implement new financial business models, financial instruments, financing opportunities, business processes, policies and procedures, and technological solutions

Finance - Finance Business Partnering:

- Able to support business units and add value by innovating and providing solutions to financial issues/queries, including through FAQs, financial tools, advisory, etc. Influences and appropriately challenges non-finance colleagues for whom the service is being provided. Understands the operations, opportunities and challenges of the organization.

- Holds a commercial outlook, demonstrating accountability towards organizational goals.

Finance - Audit Risk Management:

- Ability to address risks and audit issues raised in the course of an audit and propose solutions in order to ensure a true and fair audit opinion is achieved.

Business Management - Portfolio management:

- Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment.

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

Business Direction & Strategy - Systems thinking:

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Finance or Accounting, and/or a professional accounting qualification from an accredited institute of accountancy is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree

- Those with professional accounting qualifications from an accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

- Candidates with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

- Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete UNDP Finance Training and certification Programme (FTCP),if recruited.

Experience:

- Minimum 5 years (with master´s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor´s degree) of experience in financial management, accounting or auditing.

- Proven experience and a sound understanding of IPSAS/IFRS required.

- Experience with ERP financial systems is required (preferably Oracle).

- Strong analytical and report-writing skills with a proven track record.

- Demonstrated experience in AI, digital transformation, and process automation and demonstrated ability explore and apply new technologies.

- Experience as a collaborative team player with flexibility to work across global time zones.

Desirable Criteria:

- Audit experience (internal and/or external) is an asset.

- Experience with project costing and time and labour distribution and timecards would be an asset.

- Experience in working with actuaries and actuarial reports would be an asset.

- Experience working in the UN system would be an asset

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language is an advantage.

Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

jobs.title: Senior Nurse [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP works in about 170 countries and territories, helping to eradicate poverty, reduce inequalities and exclusion, and build resilience so countries can sustain progress. As the UN’s development agency, UNDP plays a critical role in helping countries achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Our people are united by a common call to action: building a fairer and more inclusive world for those in need through sustainable development.

The Nurse NSPA 7 position will support the health and wellbeing of UN staff and their dependents in Zimbabwe through effective medical care, emergency management, and health promotion activities, ensuring high standards of healthcare services in collaboration with local health authorities and other UN agencies.

The Nurse NSPA 7 will provide high-quality nursing care, manage emergency cases, assist in health promotion, ensure clinic operational efficiency, and support the UN Physician in all medical services. This role is integral to facilitating health and wellbeing within the UN community.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. This is a recognition of the interconnected nature of development risks & crises that the world is facing and that call for assembling multidisciplinary teams for an integrated & systemic response. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across issues, units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

General communication and assistance of patients.

- Reception and assistance of patients for treatment by the UN Physician.

- Reception and assistance of clients for attention by the UN Counsellor.

- Assisting visitors, responding to patient bookings and other enquiry calls.

- Giving advice to International and local UN staff and their dependants on available medical services in the country.

- Translation to doctor / patient into English / local language of Shona / Ndebele

- Networking with other Health Professionals including referrals for specialist Services

Treatment and care of patients.

- Management of emergency cases at the clinic.

- Treatment of minor ailments through nurse consultation including dressings.

- Dispensation of doctor’s prescriptions including injections and immunizations.

- Basic counselling on psycho-social issues and referrals to UN Counsellor.

- Collection of laboratory samples from clients / patients, handing them to the laboratory scientist and subsequent follow of results as need be.

Maintain clinic in good order and security of equipment

- Ensuring the clinic is clean and in a welcoming state.

- Safe record keeping of patient files and their accessibility when needed.

- Security of clinic movable and immovable equipment.

- Ensuring confidential record keeping of patient’s records

- Safe keeping of medicines and maintenance of adequate stocks

Administrative work attached to clinic

- Planning, organizing and conducting Health Promotions among UN Agencies in Zimbabwe.

- Production of patient medical reports, clinic mid-year and end of year reports.

- Supervisory duties as designated by the UN Physician.

- Mentoring and coaching of other clinic staff members.

- Ensuring the smooth running of the clinic processes.

- Administration of petty cash.

Assisting the UN Physician with procedures and other delegated duties and responsibilities

- Processing of medical examinations: entry, periodic and exit.

- Referral of patients to other UN Doctors and professional management of emergency cases in the absence of the UN Physician.

- Referrals of patients for other medical services which are not offered at the clinic such as family planning, child immunizations, women’s health etc.

- Attending to emergencies after hours as requested by the UN Physician.

- Escorting patients for specialised treatment at local major hospitals and subsequent evacuations to South African Hospitals as necessary.

- Planning and implementation of the Health Promotion program for all UN Agencies in Harare and Sub-offices outside Harare.

- Ensuring smooth running of the UN Doctor’s Outreach Program, Doctor’s Conferences, Health meetings and other meetings in and outside the country.

- Ensuring professional and up to standard Clinic Services and Part-time counselling Services in the absence of the UN Physician and UN Counsellor.

- Any other administrative duties as requested by the UN Physician.

Institutional Arrangement

The Senior Nurse will report to UN Physician and work closely with the UN Clinic staff, UN Common Services and the operations team to ensure provision of efficient medical emergency care and nursing services to UN staff and their eligible dependents.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategies. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in Tajikistan has been active since 1994 and is guided in its work by the Country Programme Document, which in turn builds upon the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP has made a significant contribution to developing the National Development Strategy, with an outline of policies and investments necessary to reach the SDGs by 2030. Together with the Government of Tajikistan, civil society and the people of Tajikistan, UNDP works towards identifying local solutions to global and national development challenges. Its main focus is reaching sustainable development by enhancing accountability of the current governance system, mitigating natural disaster threats, and contributing to environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.

The Climate Change, Energy and Environment (CCEE) Cluster of UNDP Tajikistan manages a diverse and growing portfolio of various projects currently under implementation across the country. The Cluster provides strategic, technical, and operational support to national counterparts in addressing Tajikistan’s key environmental, climate, and energy challenges, in line with national development priorities and international commitments. The Cluster’s programmatic focus spans several interrelated thematic areas, including climate change adaptation and mitigation, integrated water resources management, sustainable land management, urban resilience to disaster and climate risks, promotion of renewable and green energy solutions, and biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

In particular, with regard to biodiversity conservation and it’s biodiversity portfolio, UNDP's Country Office in Tajikistan is currently supporting the country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) update and implementation in alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). As countries move from updating their NBSAPs towards implementation, targeted support is required to translate national biodiversity priorities into concrete actions and address critical implementation gaps.

In this context, the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account Multi-Partner Trust Fund (NBSAP AAA MPTF) provides targeted support to countries to accelerate implementation of their NBSAP priorities and translate national biodiversity commitments into concrete action. The Fund supports high-priority interventions that address critical policy, institutional, technical and financing gaps and that have not been sufficiently covered through other available resources. Its support is intended to strengthen national readiness for sustained biodiversity action, increase implementation ambition and create foundations for further investment in achievement of national biodiversity priorities and the KMGBF.

In Tajikistan, the project directly contributes to the objectives of the NBSAP AAA MPTF by providing targeted support for NBSAP implementation, with a particular focus on operationalizing KMGBF Target 6 on invasive alien species (IAS). The project will strengthen the scientific, technical and policy basis for the prevention, monitoring and management of IAS, including through establishment of a national IAS database and development of the country’s first State Programme and Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species. These interventions will help address critical data and policy gaps, strengthen national capacities for ongoing biological risk monitoring and management, and establish a more coherent framework for coordinated action on invasive alien species.

The project further contributes to strengthening the core functions of NBSAP implementation through institutional capacity development and strategic policy support, applying a “whole-of-government” and “whole-of-society” approach. It also contributes to KMGBF Target 23 on gender equality by integrating gender-responsive approaches and promoting the equitable participation of women and vulnerable groups within IAS knowledge, monitoring and policy systems. The initiative will additionally promote youth engagement and digital innovation in biodiversity information management, thereby supporting an inclusive, sustainable and potentially scalable approach to implementation of KMGBF priorities in Tajikistan.

Under the direct supervision of UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project interventions, liaise with national partners and support effective teamwork and strong partnerships. The Project Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality project results that strengthen national capacities, data systems and policy frameworks for the prevention and management of invasive alien species, in line with Tajikistan’s NBSAP and the KMGBF.

He/she will ensure implementation mechanisms and technical working groups are established and meet regularly, that all planned workshops, technical studies and other activities are organised in a timely manner, and that they meet expected quality standards. He/she will also specifically be responsible for outreach activities to relevant stakeholders, and the preparation of synthesis reports, policy briefs, press releases and briefing notes for Government, donor, UNDP, etc.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure effective technical support to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- General coordination and liaison of project activities with national counterparts, scientific institutions and relevant stakeholders.

- Coordinate the development and validation of the National IAS Catalogue and Database.

- Facilitate the development, testing and validation of standardized IAS risk assessment protocols.

- Coordinate the development of the multi-sectoral National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Ensure alignment of the project’s technical outputs with the NBSAP, the KMGBF, national biodiversity reporting processes and other relevant national policies and strategic frameworks.

- Facilitate technical assessments, field data collection, consultations and other analytical work required for the development of the National IAS Catalogue, risk assessment protocols, IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide substantive support to project stakeholders in reviewing and validating technical methodologies, assessments, databases, policy documents and other project outputs.

- Coordinate project activities among relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry Agency, Customs Service, Food Security Committee, other relevant ministries and agencies, civil society organizations, academia and local communities, as specified in the Project Document.

- Facilitate the establishment and effective functioning of the Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group for technical coordination, policy dialogue and development and validation of project outputs.

- Ensure the elaboration of the Stakeholder Engagement and Gender Action Plan before the kickstart of project implementation, and further ensure their effective implementation and regular monitoring.

- Ensure that gender-responsive approaches and meaningful participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups are appropriately integrated into IAS assessments, data systems, consultations and policy development in line with the project’s Results Framework.

- Coordinate and follow up on implementation of relevant environmental and social safeguard measures.

- Review all technical reports as required. Fulfil substantive activities under the Project Work Plan which are not covered by consultants or other contracted experts.

- Support the timely technical review, validation, finalization and submission to relevant national authorities of key project outputs, including the National IAS Catalogue, standardized risk assessment protocols, national IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide necessary inputs to showcase project’s experience at national, regional and international forums/events as required.

- Upon request of the Programme Specialist, participate in and make presentations at conferences, working meetings, workshops, round-table discussions and other relevant events on the IAS project and its linkages with biodiversity conservation, NBSAP and KMGBF implementation.

2. Ensure effective operational and programmatic support for the project:

- Ensure operational and programmatic coordination of the project in accordance with the Project Document, approved work plans, Results Framework and applicable UNDP rules and procedures.

- Support the overall management and coordination of project implementation, ensuring timely and proper execution of activities by consultants, experts, contractors and project partners.

- Prepare Terms of Reference (ToR) for national and international consultants, experts, contractors and other service providers in line with the Project Document and relevant UNDP procedures; coordinate and guide their work and ensure compliance with agreed work plans and respective ToRs and the quality and timely delivery of outputs.

- Facilitate organization of the project Inception Workshop and support the establishment and functioning of the Project Steering Committee, Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group.

- Support communication and coordination with government institutions, scientific organizations, civil society organizations, local communities and other stakeholders involved in implementation of activities specified in the Project Work Plan.

- Prepare meeting agendas and background materials, take notes/minutes of project meetings and ensure timely follow-up on decisions and agreed actions.

- Support preparation and implementation of annual and detailed project work plans, including monitoring of implementation progress and follow-up on planned activities and deliverables.

- Monitor project progress against the Results Framework, including achievement of indicators and targets, and coordinate collection, verification and consolidation of supporting evidence.

- Collect and analyze project-related data and information from government counterparts, consultants, scientific institutions, implementing partners and other relevant sources for project monitoring and reporting purposes.

- Assume responsibility for the timely preparation of project progress reports and other required inputs in line with the reporting requirements of NBSAP AAA MPTF and corporate standards of UNDP.

- Support preparation of the project’s final report and project operational closure upon completion of project activities.

- Monitor project risks and issues in accordance with the Project Document and risk framework and ensure that emerging risks are promptly brought to the attention of the Programme Specialist and relevant project governance bodies.

- Support regular updating of project risk log and follow up on agreed risk mitigation measures.

- Monitor project expenditures, commitments and balances against approved project budget lines and work plans and bring potential deviations requiring management attention to the Programme Specialist.

- Coordinate project activities with other relevant biodiversity, climate and environmental initiatives and programmes in Tajikistan to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication and promote synergies, including with NBSAP update and national reporting.

- Provide assistance and substantive inputs to the Programme Specialist in preparation of project briefs, presentations, reports, talking points and other relevant materials.

- Ensure effective dissemination of and access to information on project activities and results, and support project outreach and communication activities in coordination with UNDP communications staff.

- Liaise with the NBSAP AAA MPTF focal point and relevant UNDP regional focal point(s) to ensure effective project implementation, seek and follow up on technical and operational guidance, address project-related issues and queries, and ensure alignment with applicable programme requirements and guidance.

- Support resource mobilization efforts by providing inputs to the new project ideas, concept notes, funding proposals, and other relevant resource mobilization materials.

3. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area.

- Organize trainings, technical workshops, consultations, awareness-raising events and capacity-building activities in a participatory manner, involving relevant government institutions, scientific / academic institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, women and youth groups, and other stakeholders.

- Support capacity building of decision-makers and relevant technical institutions on IAS identification, risk assessment, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based monitoring, data management, use of the national IAS Database to be established under the project, and relevant NBSAP and KMGBF frameworks.

- Support development and dissemination of technical guidance, IAS field guides, training materials, project briefs, factsheets, awareness materials and other knowledge products generated under the project.

- Identify, synthesize and document good practices, lessons learned and implementation experience generated by the project and its partners, including through maintenance of relevant project knowledge and lessons-learned records.

- Participate in and ensure substantive contributions to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and technical exchanges on IAS management, biodiversity conservation and implementation of the NBSAP and KMGBF.

- Promote awareness and advocacy on IAS-related biodiversity risks, prevention and management measures, and opportunities for collaboration in coordination with project partners, stakeholders and UNDP communications staff.

- Support engagement of women, youth and local communities in knowledge generation, awareness raising and dissemination of biodiversity information, in line with the project’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office/Project and the Organization

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will be based in Dushanbe, at the premises of either the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Center or the National Academy of Sciences, subject to management decision with frequent visits to the UNDP Country Office. Within his/her role, the incumbent will coordinate the achievement of the expected project results by providing strategic guidance to project staff and consultants and liaising among the targeted stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of relevant activities. The Project Coordinator will be accountable and report to the UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment.

- Think Innovatively: ​​LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements ​

- Learn Continuously: ​​LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback​

- Adapt with Agility: ​​ LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible ​

- Act with Determination: ​​LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident​

- Engage and Partner: ​​ LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships​

Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.
