Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde el año 2013, la historia del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) está ligada al establecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, contribuyendo a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17 “Revitalizar la alianza mundial para el Desarrollo Sostenible”, con el propósito de apoyar los esfuerzos de la AMEXCID para transitar hacia un modelo eficaz, que refleje las particularidades de un Cooperante Dual, oferente y receptor de cooperación en sus diversas modalidades, y País de Renta Media Alta, de acuerdo con sus propias prioridades y visión, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible.

En su Tercera Etapa (2019-2025), el Programa de Cooperación promueve que la Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (CID) sea un instrumento para alcanzar las prioridades de desarrollo incluidas en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2019-2024, alineado particularmente al compromiso de “Conducir la política exterior en apego a los principios constitucionales y articulada con las prioridades de la política interna”, siendo la CID uno de los siete principios de la política exterior de México.

Específicamente, se apoyarán los esfuerzos que realiza la AMEXCID para consolidarse institucionalmente, encaminados a desarrollar sus capacidades nacionales, fortalecer su política de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta, así como establecer alianzas estratégicas con otros actores relevantes (como el sector privado, la academia y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, otras agencias de cooperación multilaterales y bilaterales presentes en México que realizan esfuerzos de naturaleza complementaria), por medio de esquemas innovadores de cooperación al desarrollo. Además, se apoyará la contribución de la Agencia a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Lo anterior está orientado a potenciar los 6 ejes de acción de la AMEXCID (diplomacia deportiva; diplomacia en ciudadanía, diplomacia científica y tecnológica; diplomacia económica empresarial; diplomacia educativa; y diplomacia humanitaria), su nueva estructura (coordinación de la política de cooperación internacional; análisis y evaluación de proyectos; implementación de proyectos), así como las prioridades de México como país receptor y país oferente de CID.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1.Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2.Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3.Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4.Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1.Liderar la asignación, optimización y fiscalización de los recursos financieros destinados a programas de movilidad y becas bilaterales o multilaterales, asegurando la transparencia y el cumplimiento de las metas presupuestarias de la AMEXCID.

2.Participar activamente en la formulación de nuevas directrices, convocatorias y marcos normativos para fortalecer los convenios de intercambio estudiantil y de investigadores entre México y otros países.

3.Supervisar la automatización de los flujos de trabajo administrativos para la correcta recepción, selección y seguimiento de los becarios extranjeros en México y mexicanos en el exterior.

4.Coordinar esfuerzos con universidades estatales, instituciones de educación superior en distintas regiones del país y dependencias de gobierno para ampliar la oferta de espacios y estancias académicas descentralizadas.

5.Diseñar metodologías e indicadores de desempeño para medir el impacto socioeducativo y regional de los egresados de los programas de intercambio académico de la agencia, retroalimentando la toma de decisiones directivas.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El/la Especialista en Cooperación Académica y Movilidad Internacional formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID o de la dirección general en la que se asigne, responsable de autorizar, coordinar y supervisar los programas, proyectos y acciones que realicen las unidades administrativas y órganos administrativos desconcentrados de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, en temas de cooperación científica, educativa, tecnológica, deportiva, económica y empresarial, en ciudadanía y cultural, de asistencia humanitaria y de ayuda internacional, conforme a las políticas que dicte el Secretario y en concordancia con la Ley de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo y el Programa de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos Mínimos:

- Título de Licenciatura en Administración Pública, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Políticas, Economía, Finanzas Públicas o carrera afines, es requisito.

- Maestría en los temas antes mencionados no es requisito, pero se le dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con título de Licenciatura: 7 años de experiencia en puestos directivos o similares dentro de la administración pública.

- Para candidatos/as con Maestría: 5 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en cargos de alta responsabilidad dentro de la administración pública, en áreas relacionadas con la cooperación internacional, la educación superior, las relaciones exteriores o el desarrollo social.

- Experiencia en negociación, concertación política, diálogo institucional o construcción de acuerdos.

- Conocimiento y experiencia en gestión presupuestal, seguimiento programático, rendición de cuentas, evaluación o supervisión de recursos públicos.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en coordinación o vinculación con instituciones de educación superior o de investigación.

- Experiencia en la planeación, programación, presupuestación y evaluación de proyectos institucionales, relacionados con el otorgamiento de becas, movilidad académica o fomento a la investigación.

- Experiencia liderando equipos de trabajo multidisciplinarios.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Communications Analyst/EVRF, Short-Term
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous references and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet.

Amid a dynamic socio-economic context of Moldova, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP) is embarking on a deeply transformative process. The “Digital Transformation of Social Protection” Project, financed by the Government of Italy through the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), stands as testimony to this momentum forward. Moldovan social protection system faces substantial challenges caused by inefficiencies, limited digital integration, and an unmet demand for institutional framework and service delivery better addressing contemporary socio-economic uncertainties. The MLSP's endeavour is to reengineer this landscape, enhance its digital infrastructure and create a framework that is efficient, inclusive, resilient, and adaptable to changing contexts and conditions. The Ministry has launched three major reforms, namely that of social services (RESTART); that of the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI); and that of the National Council for Determination of Disability and Work Capacity (CNDDCM). These initiatives are not just a response to evolving needs but a visionary stride towards a future where social protection is seamlessly inclusive, empowering, and a realized right for every citizen, as defined by the 2030 Agenda.

The Project aims to address the fragmented digital infrastructure of the social protection system, which currently operates with multiple, disparate, and non-interoperable information systems. This fragmentation causes binding inefficiencies in data management and service delivery and undermines the ability to provide timely and appropriate support to beneficiaries. By developing a new, integrated Information System – eSocial, the Project aims to achieve delivery of social protection & employment services in a more coherent, accessible, and resilient way, enhancing the Ministry's ability to meet existing demands and adapt to future changes.

Complementing the processes above, the Project supports the enhancement and institutionalization of the Ministry’s capacities to lead ongoing efforts of digitalisation of social protection services via a dedicated Digital Center for Social Innovation (DCSI), which will ensure the intervention’s sustainability and advancements. DCSI experts engaged by the Project support the development of the eSocial digital platform and its adoption within MLSP and subordinated institutions: ATAS (regional agencies for social assistance), STAS (regional structures for social assistance), NEA, SLI, CNDDCM, AGSSSI (the Agency for the Management of Highly Specialized Social Services), etc.

Additionally, with UNDP support, the Government has established the Energy Vulnerability Reduction Fund (EVRF), an evidence‑based compensation scheme that has already supported hundreds of thousands of households during past heating seasons.

This support is closely coordinated with UNDP’s Digital Transformation of Social Protection project financed by the Government of Italy, ensuring coherence across reforms, alignment of digital architectures, and interoperability between employment and social protection systems within a unified government-wide digital ecosystem.

The Projects’ strategic approach is rooted in Moldova’s national priorities, as defined by the RESTART Reform of Social Assistance and the UNDP Country Programme Document for the Republic of Moldova (2023-2027). The Project is designed to leverage technology as a key driver of change, streamline processes, enhance user experience, and strengthen institutional resilience. It involves comprehensive mapping and optimization of current business processes, ensuring they are streamlined and designed for the best possible user experience.

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of key functions:

The Communications Analyst/EVRF in close cooperation with the project team, under the direct supervision of the “Digital Transformation of Social Protection” Project Manager, will provide dedicated support to the EVRF communication and visibility plan for the 2026‑2027 heating season, while also contributing to broader communication efforts of the project, contribute to the design, planning, execution, monitoring and reporting of the project activities related to communication and visibility, aimed at increasing public awareness, promoting transparency, and ensuring visibility of EVRF results, while supporting overall project visibility. More specifically:

I. EVRF focused communication:

- Develop and implement the EVRF Communication and Visibility Action Plan for the 2026 2027 heating season.

- Identify key audiences and effective communication channels to ensure inclusive and accessible outreach.

- Draft public facing materials (talking points, briefs, factsheets, presentations) aligned with EVRF milestones and legal updates.

- Draft and disseminate press releases, stories, and newsletters highlighting progress and showcasing the impact of the EVRF.

- Maintain and update public facing content on compensatii.gov.md, including FAQs, registration guidance, and automated notifications (SMS/email/pop ups) in Romanian, Russian, and English.

- Document and promote success stories and testimonials from EVRF beneficiaries and implementers (social workers, hotline staff, librarians).

- Support awareness campaigns, public events, and outreach activities, including the annual launch of the heating season.

- Produce and adapt communication materials and visual content (infographics, short videos, social media posts).

- Monitor outreach performance using analytics and feedback tools; adjust strategies accordingly.

II. Effective Project Communication:

- Contribute to the implementation of the Projects’ Communication Strategies and Visibility Plans in close collaboration with the Project Manager, DTSP Communication Analyst and UNDP Communications Analyst.

- Support the national partners in designing and implementation of joint civic education and information campaigns, as well as in developing and delivering the key messages.

- Draft talking points, briefs, factsheets, handout materials and dynamic presentations, considering the gender and human rights aspects.

- Provide advice and recommendations to mitigate potential public communication crisis and sensible issues. This shall include, but not be limited to, press monitoring (pre and post crisis), drafting of press releases and/or written reactions, and ad-hoc crisis reports.

- Contribute to the implementation of awareness campaigns, trainings, workshops, and public events, using various channels of communication and engaging with media representatives for a broader audience.

- Develop engaging digital content (infographics, illustrations, quote cards, videos, social media posts) to simplify complex topics related to energy vulnerability, social protection, digital services and project interventions and increase public understanding.

- Facilitate regular consultations and dialogue with national partners and stakeholders to ensure their perspectives are well reflected in the civic education and public awareness efforts.

- Develop news pieces, success stories, scripts for video reportages and coordinate with subcontracted photographers and videographers;

- Establish and manage stakeholder communication channels, including newsletters, working groups, and online platforms, to ensure continuous engagement.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

The Communications Analyst/EVRF will work under the supervision of the UNDP Project Manager in close coordination with the DTSP Communication Analyst and the UNDP Communications Analyst, in close cooperation with the UNDP Moldova Country Office and overall project team, for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery.

He/she also will collaborate with other UN projects, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Industry and other national stakeholders (the National Employment Agency; the National Office of Social Insurance; AIPA; etc.). The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP administrative rules, regulations, policies, and strategies.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional and Technical Competencies

Business Development - Knowledge facilitation:

- Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas.

- Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management - Communication:

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Management - Digital Awareness and Literacy:

- Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value.

- Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed.

- Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

Communications - Campaign management:

- Ability to produce and implement communications and advocacy campaigns which lead to impactful change.

Communications - Creative direction and copywriting:

- Ability to creatively communicate concepts in an engaging and simple way.

Digital - Data storytelling and communications:

- Skilled in building a narrative around a set of data and its accompanying visualizations to help convey the meaning of that data in a powerful and compelling fashion

2030 Agenda: People - Gender:

- Communication and Advocacy for Gender Equality.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Journalism, Communication, Public Relations, Sociology, International Relations, or another relevant field, or

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a Master’s degree are not required to have prior professional experience.

- At least two years (with Bachelor’s Degree) in communication, mass-media, public relations, and/or other substantive area is required.

Desired skills:

- Proven experience in similar positions in UNDP or other UN Agencies.

- Proven experience in working in the areas of social protection, energy vulnerability, energy efficiency or employment.

- Previous experience in development assistance or related work for a development organization, governmental institution, NGO or private sector / consulting firm.

- Experience in development and implementation of media/communications strategies and plans, visibility and awareness raising campaigns, drafting communication materials and products.

- Experience in conceptualizing and implementing national and local public outreach/communication campaigns.

Required languages:

- Fluency in Romanian and English is required;

- Knowledge of one or more minority languages relevant for Moldova, including Russian, Romani, Gagauzian, Bulgarian, Ukrainian and sign language, is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Assistente de Cerimonial e Eventos (2 vagas) (Home Based) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Este processo seletivo busca contratar profissionais para atuar de forma compartilhada no apoio técnico e operacional de duas iniciativas estratégicas desenvolvidas no âmbito da parceria de cooperação técnica internacional entre o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) e o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ):

- Justiça 4.0: o Programa, iniciado em 2020, visa desenvolver e aprimorar soluções tecnológicas para tornar os serviços oferecidos pela Justiça brasileira mais eficientes, eficazes e acessíveis à população, além de otimizar a gestão processual para magistrados(as), servidores(as), advogados(as) e demais atores do sistema de Justiça. O Justiça 4.0 é um dos maiores programas de transformação digital do Poder Judiciário e também dialoga com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e com a Agenda 2030 da ONU.

- Justiça [+Segura]: firmado em 2025, o Programa foca no fortalecimento da segurança cibernética no Poder Judiciário. O Justiça [+Segura] desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário. A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade. Nesse cenário, o(a) profissional integrará a equipe compartilhada dos programas, atuando sob a supervisão direta da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos do PNUD e em estreita articulação com as coordenações técnicas do CNJ, com o propósito de garantir a excelência operacional, a sinergia entre as ações e o alcance dos resultados pactuados.

Duties and Responsibilities

O(a) Assistente de Cerimonial e Eventos será responsável por apoiar a implementação dos projetos e programas, garantindo a qualidade administrativa e o suporte operacional aos resultados, em estreita articulação com as equipes do CNJ e do PNUD. A posição será exercida em regime remoto, sendo requisito que o(a) candidato(a) tenha residência no Brasil. Quando houver necessidade de cobertura presencial de eventos, poderão ser realizadas viagens nacionais, com as despesas correspondentes custeadas pelo projeto.

Para o alcance desse objetivo, o(a) profissional desempenhará as seguintes responsabilidades principais e atividades:

1. Apoio logístico e operacional a eventos e cerimoniais:

- Apoiar a execução operacional de atividades relacionadas à organização e logística de eventos e cerimoniais no âmbito das iniciativas institucionais;

- Prestar suporte administrativo em ações realizadas junto aos tribunais parceiros, contribuindo para que o andamento das tarefas esteja alinhado com os cronogramas e metas estabelecidas;

- Colaborar operacionalmente com a Secretaria de Cerimonial e Eventos do CNJ e equipes envolvidas para o bom andamento das atividades.

2. Organização e controle de documentos operacionais e de viagem:

- Auxiliar na compilação, elaboração e organização de planos de execução de eventos, planilhas de controle e formulários de coleta de dados;

- Organizar cadastros de viajantes, apoiar a instrução de solicitações de viagens no sistema e compilar documentos protocolares (tais como roteiros de cerimonial, minutas de nominatas e listas de autoridades);

- Organizar e preparar pastas de documentos de pós-evento, relatórios de atividades e memórias de reuniões.

3. Suporte administrativo a reuniões e alinhamentos técnicos:

- Auxiliar na logística de agendamento, convocação e organização de reuniões para alinhamento operacional entre as equipes participantes dos eventos;

- Prestar apoio de secretaria e suporte logístico em salas virtuais ou presenciais durante as reuniões de alinhamento técnico;

- Apoiar a consolidação e a distribuição de minutas e deliberações de reuniões para assegurar a coordenação dos aspectos operacionais e cerimoniais.

4. Suporte aos processos de compras, contratações e logística de missões:

- Prestar apoio administrativo nos fluxos de instrução processual para contratações de itens e serviços necessários à realização de missões e eventos;

- Auxiliar na coleta de propostas comerciais e na prospecção inicial de fornecedores de mercado (espaços, equipamentos, tradução, cenografia, etc.);

- Atuar operacionalmente em conformidade com as diretrizes de aquisições e regras de contratação estabelecidas pelo PNUD.

5. Apoio administrativo ao fluxo de prestação de contas:

- Prestar esclarecimentos básicos e orientações operacionais a participantes, palestrantes e fornecedores sobre os procedimentos de prestação de contas;

- Auxiliar no recebimento, triagem, organização e conferência preliminar de comprovantes de despesas, passagens, diárias e notas fiscais;

- Organizar a documentação comprobatória e apoiar o encaminhamento dos processos de pagamento e/ou liquidação de despesas em colaboração com a equipe financeira do PNUD.

6. Acompanhamento operacional local e suporte a missões:

- Realizar o acompanhamento presencial (in loco) e logístico de agendas nacionais e internacionais, com ampla disponibilidade para viagens;

- Prestar suporte administrativo e operacional imediato durante a realização de eventos institucionais para garantir a resolução tempestiva de demandas cotidianas;

- Auxiliar na organização operacional e apoiar a interlocução com participantes, parceiros e demais envolvidos nas agendas relacionadas aos Programas Justiça 4.0 e Justiça [+Segura].

7. Monitoramento, guarda de arquivos e gestão da informação:

- Apoiar o monitoramento e a avaliação de eventos coletando formulários de satisfação e organizando estatísticas de participação;

- Manter os arquivos físicos e digitais das pastas dos projetos devidamente atualizados, organizados e com a memória documental de todos os eventos preservada;

- Fornecer informações organizadas e registros técnicos de suporte para as atividades de comunicação e gestão do conhecimento das iniciativas.

O(a) titular desempenha outras funções dentro de seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

O(a) contratado(a) será supervisionado(a) pela Analista Técnica de Gestão e Ações Estratégicas.

Competências

Competências Essenciais

Alcançar Resultados: NÍVEL 1: Planeja e monitora o próprio trabalho, presta atenção aos detalhes, entrega um trabalho de qualidade dentro do prazo

Pensamento Inovador: NÍVEL 1: Aberto a ideias criativas/riscos conhecidos, é pragmático para resolver problemas, faz melhorias

Aprendizagem Contínua: NÍVEL 1: Mente aberta e curiosa, compartilha conhecimento, aprende com os erros, pede feedback

Adaptar com Agilidade: NÍVEL 1: Adapta-se à mudança, lida de forma construtiva com a ambiguidade/incerteza, é flexível

Atuar com determinação: NÍVEL 1: Mostra determinação e motivação, capaz de entregar com calma diante da adversidade, confiante

Engajar-se e ser Parceiro: NÍVEL 1: Demonstra compaixão/compreensão para com os outros, forma relacionamentos positivos

Promover Diversidade e Inclusão: NÍVEL 1: Apreciar/respeitar as diferenças, consciente do preconceito inconsciente, confrontar a discriminação

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios | Pensamento Estratégico

Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e Estratégia de Negócio | Perspicácia Empresarial

Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização.

Desenvolvimento de Negócios | Design Centrado no Humano

Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de Negócios | Gestão de projetos

Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Gestão de Negócios | Trabalhar com evidências e dados

Capacidade de inspecionar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, informar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisões.

jobs.title: Anti-Corruption Analyst, Short-Term (multiple post)
jobs.description:
Background

Preventing and combating corruption is a priority for the Government of the Republic of Moldova and central to its European Union accession agenda. The authorities have adopted the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme 2024–2028 and are strengthening the institutions that deliver it. Moldova is also a State Party to the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), and these reforms support its implementation. The focus is now on putting these frameworks into practice, with sustained technical support.

UNDP implements one component of the EU-funded project ‘Support in combating and preventing corruption and organized crime in the Republic of Moldova’, together with Expertise France and Civipol. The consortium project seeks to reduce corruption and financial crime, including money laundering, by strengthening effective, efficient, independent, and accountable justice, prosecution, and investigation systems. The project will support the application of EU standards and relevant OECD and GRECO recommendations, strengthen institutional ownership, and promote preventive, risk-based, and evidence-driven approaches to integrity management.

The UNDP component is delivered as part of the REDACT project. REDACT (Resilient Democracy through Anti-Corruption) strengthens the capacities of anti-corruption, law enforcement and justice institutions, improves coordination among them, and supports oversight by civil society and the media. More information is available on the REDACT project page.

Under the UNDP-led project component, the intended outcome is to enhance institutional capacities across government to mainstream anti-corruption and integrity frameworks. A central intervention is focused on supporting the establishment and mentoring of a cross-institutional network of integrity, ethics, and corruption-prevention practitioners. Additionally technical assistance to enhance corruption risk identification and mitigation through a combination of strategic analysis, legislative review, sectoral analysis, and digital analytical enablement will be provided.

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will provide substantive and analytical leadership on the activities of the UNDP-led component that relate to the monitoring of the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme, support to the existing cross-institutional network of integrity and ethics tutors, the reinforcement and adaptation of national integrity and anti-corruption instruments, and the strengthening of institutional analytical capacities to identify and address integrity risks.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will have responsibility to deliver substantive technical outputs and effective engagement with partners. The incumbent will act as a technical lead and trusted adviser to national partners, and is expected to spend a large part of the working time with the partner institutions, at their premises, in their working groups and in consultations, delivering analysis, providing hands-on technical assistance and helping institutions align their work. Building relationships of trust and credibility with national actors is central to the role.

I. Lead Technical and Substantive Support on NIAP Monitoring, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Instruments, and Institutional Risk Analysis:

- Lead the technical implementation of the assigned activities (NIAP monitoring, support to the network of integrity and ethics tutors, integrity and anti-corruption instruments, and institutional analytical capacity), providing hands-on analysis and advice to the partner institutions and the Project Team.

- Lead the substantive support to the National Anti-Corruption Centre (NAC) in coordinating, monitoring and evaluating the implementation of the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme (NIAP) 2024–2028, including indicator frameworks, data collection and reporting protocols, and quarterly monitoring cycles with implementing institutions.

- Provide the substantive content for the digital monitoring dashboards (indicators, visualisation logic, reporting formats and analytical outputs) in close cooperation with the ICT Analyst, who leads their technical implementation, and, for the monitoring of integrity and work ethics guidelines, with the tutors and reporting institutions.

- Support the preparation of periodic, data-driven NIAP progress reports and of the quarterly progress-reporting meetings with responsible institutions, and facilitate peer exchange among the members of the NIAP Monitoring Group, reporting institutions and civil society.

- Provide advisory support to the midterm review and final evaluation of the NIAP, including the methodology, terms of reference and quality assurance of evaluation outputs, and coordinate the engagement of civil society organisations in independent shadow reporting.

- Guide the review of the legislative and regulatory framework for integrity and anti-corruption mainstreaming, including its alignment with EU standards and OECD and GRECO recommendations, and contribute to the preparation of regulatory proposals.

- Support the adaptation of existing national integrity and anti-corruption instruments, including integrity plans and early-warning and data-sharing mechanisms, in close cooperation with NAC, the National Integrity Authority (NIA) and other relevant institutions.

- Contribute to the review and update of integrity and ethics learning materials, including a training track for newly elected local officials, and to awareness-raising on integrity obligations and tools, in cooperation with NAC, NIA and the National Institute of Public Administration and Management (INAMP).

- Support the engagement of civil society organisations and the private sector in detecting, analysing and reporting integrity risks, including through the reLAWed platform and the interoperability of the e-Expertise system with Particip.gov.md.

- Lead the substantive work on strengthening NAC’s capacity to analyse integrity plans and to identify trends, recurring risks and sectoral vulnerabilities, including analytical training and mentoring of NAC officials.

- Guide targeted corruption risk assessments in the sectors identified as highest risk and the development of risk remediation plans, ensuring methodological soundness and the use of the evidence generated.

- Facilitate the co-creation of legislative and regulatory proposals between NAC and other institutions on the basis of the risk assessment findings.

- Support the National Integrity Authority in strengthening its analytical and oversight capacities on asset and personal interest declarations, including risk typologies, verification methods and the referral of cases to law enforcement.

- Conduct research, analytical reviews, assessments, mapping exercises, and other evidence-based analyses to inform project interventions, policy dialogue, and decision-making processes.

- Develop and contribute to technical papers, concept notes, guidance materials, analytical reports, recommendations, briefs, and other substantive knowledge products relevant to the project objectives.

- Support the identification of institutional needs, opportunities, risks, and challenges related to governance, integrity, accountability, and anti-corruption mainstreaming and reforms, and propose practical solutions and recommendations.

- Review and provide technical feedback on deliverables prepared by consultants, service providers, implementing partners, and other stakeholders to ensure quality and alignment with project objectives.

- Monitor developments, trends, good practices, and emerging issues relevant to the assigned thematic areas and provide technical advice to support adaptive project implementation.

- Document technical lessons learned and good practices from the assigned activities and feed them into the policy dialogue with partners.

II. Contribute to the network of integrity and ethics tutors:

- Contribute to the further development of the existing network of integrity and ethics tutors, the in-house focal points designated by state institutions, and of the related communities of practice, working with NAC and the participating institutions.

- Provide technical input to the competency model for the tutors and to their structured training, including on building trust in the tutoring mechanism within institutions, confidential peer advice, integrity plans, mitigation measures, corruption risk assessment and compliance.

- Contribute technical sessions and mentoring to the training of the tutors, and guide expert trainers where engaged, so that the tutors apply consistent methodologies and monitor implementation in their institutions.

- Support NAC in convening regular community-of-practice meetings, and contribute technical content to joint working groups, case-based learning, exchange visits and the online learning space on MLearn; logistics for meetings, visits and events are organised with the Project Analyst and Operations.

- Facilitate peer-to-peer exchanges, in which high-performing institutions share their experience with others, and structured dialogue among NAC, the tutors and civil society.

- Capture insights from the tutors on emerging risks, vulnerabilities and good practices, and feed them into NAC’s risk analysis and the adaptation of integrity instruments.

III. Lead the implementation of the assigned activities:

- Act as a subject matter expert for the assigned interventions, leading on the substance and guiding the work of other experts and service providers where engaged, and provide timely technical advice and support to the Project Team and stakeholders and ensure outputs are delivered on time and to high-quality standards.

- Ensure that the analyses, instruments and capacity building supported under the assigned activities integrate a gender equality and inclusion perspective, to the extent the local context allows.

- Draft the technical specifications and terms of reference for the studies, expertise and services required under the assigned activities, and assess the technical quality of offers where requested; procurement itself is managed by the Project Analyst and Operations.

- Keep the Project Manager regularly informed on the substance and status of the assigned activities and of the relationships with partners, flagging emerging risks and needed adjustments early.

IV. Build relationships of trust and provide hands-on support to national partners:

- Work side by side with NAC, NIA, INAMP, the integrity and ethics tutors and other public institutions, spending a large part of the working time at their premises and in their meetings, to understand their mandates, priorities and constraints and to provide timely, practical and candid technical advice.

- Act as the day-to-day technical interlocutor of the counterpart institutions for the assigned activities, building and sustaining relationships of trust with senior officials, technical staff, civil society organisations and academia on the basis of reliability, discretion and technical credibility.

- Align the project’s support with the institutions’ own plans and priorities, and help the institutions align with one another (including on methods, data-sharing and the division of responsibilities), so that results are owned and sustained by national actors.

- Represent UNDP at technical level in the NIAP Monitoring Group, working groups and coordination platforms, and coordinate with the other partners supporting Moldova’s anti-corruption reforms, including the consortium partners of the EU-funded project, to ensure complementarity.

V. Contribute substantive inputs to project monitoring and reporting:

- Provide accurate and timely substantive inputs (evidence, analysis, indicator data and progress narrative) on the assigned activities to the Project Analyst and the Project Manager for the project, donor and government reports, which they compile.

- Identify, analyze, and report emerging issues, problems, and risks to the Project Manager, and support in implementing mitigation measures.

VI. Build institutional capacity and share technical knowledge:

- Design the technical content of, and deliver or lead, capacity building for partner institutions (including analytical mentoring, peer learning and training), involving technical experts and service providers where needed; logistics are organised with the Project Analyst and Operations.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Anti-Corruption Analyst will work under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, without supervisory responsibilities, in close cooperation with Programme, Operations, Communications and other teams in the Country Office (CO) for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery. The incumbent is expected to spend a large part of the working time with partner institutions rather than in the UNDP office. The 130 working days are planned with the Project Manager and scheduled around the partner institutions’ calendars and the project milestones. Two Anti-Corruption Analysts will be engaged. The Project Manager allocates the assigned activities between them at the start of the contract, so that the work proceeds in parallel and each has a clear focus.

He/she also will collaborate with the Project Analyst and the ICT Analyst of the project, other UNDP projects, National Anticorruption Center (CNA), National Integrity Authority (ANI), the network of integrity and ethics tutors and other national stakeholders. The Project Analyst leads project planning and budgeting, operational and procurement management, the results framework and donor reporting, and the organisation of events and knowledge products; the Anti-Corruption Analyst leads the technical substance and the relationships with national partners on which these depend, and provides the substantive inputs they require. The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management - Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Business Management - Communication

- Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Direction & Strategy - System Thinking

- Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Development - Knowledge Facilitation

- Ability to animate individuals and communities of contributors to participate and share, particularly externally

Business Management - Monitoring and Evaluation

- Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively;

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results.

- Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

- Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools.

- Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

2030 Agenda - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions

- Equal Justice

- Reduce Corruption

- Strong Institutions

2030 Agenda: People - Gender

- Gender Equality Strategy

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Law, Public Policy, Public Administration, Governance, Economics, Political or Social Sciences, or a related field relevant to the position is required; OR

- A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional 2 (two) years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 2 years (with Master’s degree) or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience in the development, implementation, analysis, monitoring, or support of reforms, policies, programmes, or institutional processes related to justice, rule of law, anti-corruption, integrity, accountability, or related governance fields.

Required skills:

- Demonstrated experience in supporting the integration of integrity, anti-corruption, transparency, accountability, or good governance principles into institutional policies, processes, programmes, or reforms;

Desired skills:

- Demonstrated experience in monitoring or evaluating national or sectoral anti-corruption, integrity or public sector reform strategies, including indicator frameworks, progress reporting and data-driven reviews;

- Experience in legal and regulatory analysis, including reviewing or drafting legislation and aligning national frameworks with EU standards and OECD and/or GRECO recommendations;

- Direct experience of working with and advising anti-corruption, integrity and prosecutorial bodies and other public institutions, including by facilitating workshops and consultations;

- Experience in corruption risk assessment or integrity planning methodologies;

- Previous professional experience in working with international organisations and donors, including UN agencies, the European Union, USAID or the World Bank, and familiarity with their requirements and procedures.

Required languages:

- Fluency in both English and Romanian is required.

- Knowledge of one or more minority languages relevant for Moldova, including Bulgarian, Gagauzian, Romani, Russian, Ukrainian and sign language, is an asset.
