jobs.title: Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist [Open to Tier 0, 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Viet Nam is undergoing a period of significant economic transformation, driven by its ambition to achieve high-income status by 2045 while transitioning towards a greener, more resilient and low-carbon development model. These ambitions are taking place in a rapidly evolving global environment, where climate change, technological transformation, changing trade and investment patterns, and increasing demands for sustainable production are reshaping the country's development opportunities and challenges.

Achieving these ambitions will require not only effective public policies and investment, but also new approaches to mobilizing and directing finance towards sustainable development. Public resources alone will not be sufficient to meet Viet Nam's development and climate financing needs. Increasingly, the challenge is to create policy, regulatory and market conditions that can mobilize domestic and international private capital and align financial flows with national development priorities.

UNDP Viet Nam works across several areas where these economic, policy and financing dimensions intersect. These include the energy transition and green growth; carbon markets and carbon pricing; biodiversity and nature finance; climate and disaster risk finance and insurance; circular economy; and sustainable private-sector development. Across these areas, UNDP combines policy advice, institutional support, innovative financing approaches and partnerships with Government, development partners, international financial institutions and the private sector.

As these areas of work evolve, there is an increasing opportunity to connect individual initiatives into a more coherent economic and financing offer. This requires understanding the economic and financial drivers underlying different development challenges; identifying synergies and opportunities across portfolios; assessing emerging policy and market developments; and translating these into strategic policy propositions, programmes and partnerships capable of mobilizing finance on a scale.

Against this background, UNDP Viet Nam is seeking an Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist to strengthen the Country Office's capacity at the intersection of economic policy, finance and programme development. The Specialist will work across the Country Office portfolio, helping to connect economic and financing analysis with UNDP's policy advisory work, programme development, strategic positioning and resource mobilization.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the strategic guidance of the Resident Representative, the Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist will provide integrated economic and financing analysis to strengthen UNDP Viet Nam’s policy positioning, programme development and partnerships.

The Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist will work across UNDP’s programme portfolio to identify and articulate the economic and financing dimensions of key development transitions, including green growth, energy transition, carbon markets, biodiversity and nature finance, climate and disaster risk finance and insurance, circular economy, and other emerging areas relevant to Viet Nam’s development trajectory.

A central function of the position will be to connect policy, economics and finance: assessing how regulatory developments, public policy, market incentives and financing mechanisms interact; identifying opportunities for public and private capital; and translating these insights into coherent policy propositions, programme concepts, financing solutions and funding proposals.

The Economic and Sustainable Finance Specialist will support the Country Office in bringing together initiatives that may currently sit across different thematic portfolios into a more coherent UNDP economic and financing offer, identifying synergies, gaps and opportunities for scale. The position will also contribute to positioning UNDP with Government, international financial institutions, development finance institutions, development partners and the private sector around emerging economic and financing priorities.

The incumbent will work in close coordination with regional and global UNDP teams.

Provide integrated economic and financing analysis to strengthen UNDP’s programme portfolio and strategic positioning.

- Provide strategic advice to Country Office management and programme teams on economic and financing issues relevant to Viet Nam’s development priorities and UNDP’s programme portfolio;

- Analyze key economic, policy, regulatory and market developments and assess their implications for UNDP’s areas of engagement and future programming;

- Provide economic and financing analysis across priority areas, including green growth and energy transition, carbon markets, biodiversity and nature finance, climate and disaster risk finance and insurance, circular economy, and sustainable private-sector development;

- Assess financing needs, constraints and opportunities, including the respective roles of public finance, private capital and international development finance;

- Analyze economic viability, incentives, risks, distributional implications and potential for scale of different policy and financing approaches;

- Produce concise analytical and policy products, including policy briefs, strategic notes, senior management briefings, speeches and talking points.

Strengthen portfolio integration and develop UNDP’s economic and financing offer

- Work across programme teams to identify connections, complementarities and opportunities among UNDP initiatives and portfolios from an economic and financing perspective;

- Bring together relevant work across areas such as carbon markets, biodiversity finance, insurance and risk finance, energy transition, green growth and circular economy to develop coherent economic and financing propositions;

- Identify emerging policy, market and financing opportunities where UNDP can provide distinctive value and advice on potential areas for programme development and institutional positioning;

- Identify opportunities to move from individual interventions and pilots towards integrated approaches that can be replicated, institutionalized or scaled;

- Connect country-level opportunities with relevant UNDP regional and global expertise, initiatives and financing platforms.

Lead and support programme development, resource mobilization and financing partnerships

- Translate economic and financing analysis into concrete programme concepts, investment propositions and funding proposals aligned with national priorities and UNDP’s comparative advantage;

- Lead or substantively contribute to the preparation of high-quality concept notes, programme documents and funding proposals, working closely with relevant programme teams;

- Strengthening the economic rationale, financing strategy, theory of change and potential for scale and sustainability of new programmes and proposals;

- Identify appropriate financing approaches and instruments — including public finance, private capital, blended finance, risk-sharing mechanisms, insurance and other innovative financing approaches — according to the development challenge being addressed;

- Identify and cultivate opportunities for collaboration and financing with development partners, IFIs, DFIs, financial institutions, investors, foundations and the private sector;

- Support the development of larger and more integrated programmes by connecting opportunities and financing propositions emerging across UNDP’s portfolio.

Provide policy advisory support, partnership engagement and contribute to UNDP knowledge networks

- Provide economic and financing policy advice to Government counterparts and other partners, in close collaboration with relevant UNDP programme teams;

- Support policy dialogue on economic and financing issues related to Viet Nam’s development transitions and facilitate access to relevant regional and global expertise;

- Contribute, in close collaboration with Senior Management, to strengthening partnerships with Government, UN agencies, IFIs, DFIs, bilateral development partners, financial institutions, the private sector, academia and other relevant stakeholders;

- Participate in relevant policy dialogues, conferences, technical discussions and other forums;

- Participate in UNDP regional and global economic and sustainable finance networks and contribute Viet Nam experience and analysis to relevant knowledge initiatives;

- Facilitate the exchange and application of relevant international experience and innovative approaches to Viet Nam’s development context.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management

- Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

- Human-centered Design: Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process Knowledge and understanding of human centred design principles and practices

Digital

- Data literacy: Understand the potential as well as the limitations of using data driven innovation. Ability to use a mix of data sources (quantitative, qualitative or real- time techniques) to develop understanding, identify patterns to inform decision making or identify opportunities for further exploration

- Co-creation: Ability to design and facilitate a process that enables a diverse group of stakeholders to solve a common problem, develop practice, or create knowledge together. Ability to embrace diversity, work with a diverse group of stakeholders understand their interests, perspectives and views and tap into them as a source for creativity. Ability to facilitate processes and create conditions that are open for diverse inputs, stimulate collaboration and sharing.

Programme & Policy

- Crisis and Fragility Policy and Engagement: Ability to extract, analyse and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making

- SDG Integration: Economic Forecasting

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- An advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Economics, Finance, Public Policy, or related fields is required. OR:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- A PhD in Economics, Finance, Public Policy or related field is an advantage.

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in economics, development finance, sustainable finance, public finance, financial sector development, or related fields.

Required skills and experiences:

- Demonstrated experience in applying economic and financial analysis to development policy, programmes, or investment challenges;

- Demonstrated experience in programme development, including the preparation of concept notes, funding proposals, investment propositions or similar instruments;

- Experience in sustainable or development finance, with exposure to areas such as climate and green finance, carbon markets, biodiversity and nature finance, insurance and risk finance, energy transition, blended finance, or private-sector finance;

- Experience in providing policy or technical advisory support to government institutions and/or engaging with financial institutions, development partners, IFIs, DFIs or the private sector;

- Demonstrated ability to analyze and synthesize complex economic, policy and financing issues and translate them into clear strategic and programmatic recommendations.

Desired skills and experiences:

- Experience working across different development sectors and identifying linkages between policy, economic and financing issues;

- Experience developing partnerships and resource mobilization opportunities with development partners, IFIs, DFIs, financial institutions and/or private-sector actors;

- Experience working in Viet Nam and/or the Asia-Pacific region;

- Prior experience with UN/UNDP, international financial institutions, development finance institutions or other international development organizations;

- Experience working in emerging-market and developing-country contexts.

jobs.title: Asociado(a) de Asuntos Jurídicos y Enlace Institucional
jobs.description:
Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde el año 2013, la historia del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) está ligada al establecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, contribuyendo a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17 “Revitalizar la alianza mundial para el Desarrollo Sostenible”, con el propósito de apoyar los esfuerzos de la AMEXCID para transitar hacia un modelo eficaz, que refleje las particularidades de un Cooperante Dual, oferente y receptor de cooperación en sus diversas modalidades, y País de Renta Media Alta, de acuerdo con sus propias prioridades y visión, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible.

En su Tercera Etapa (2019-2025), el Programa de Cooperación promueve que la Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (CID) sea un instrumento para alcanzar las prioridades de desarrollo incluidas en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2019-2024, alineado particularmente al compromiso de “Conducir la política exterior en apego a los principios constitucionales y articulada con las prioridades de la política interna”, siendo la CID uno de los siete principios de la política exterior de México.

Específicamente, se apoyarán los esfuerzos que realiza la AMEXCID para consolidarse institucionalmente, encaminados a desarrollar sus capacidades nacionales, fortalecer su política de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta, así como establecer alianzas estratégicas con otros actores relevantes (como el sector privado, la academia y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, otras agencias de cooperación multilaterales y bilaterales presentes en México que realizan esfuerzos de naturaleza complementaria), por medio de esquemas innovadores de cooperación al desarrollo. Además, se apoyará la contribución de la Agencia a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Lo anterior está orientado a potenciar los 6 ejes de acción de la AMEXCID (diplomacia deportiva; diplomacia en ciudadanía, diplomacia científica y tecnológica; diplomacia económica empresarial; diplomacia educativa; y diplomacia humanitaria), su nueva estructura (coordinación de la política de cooperación internacional; análisis y evaluación de proyectos; implementación de proyectos), así como las prioridades de México como país receptor y país oferente de CID.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1. Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2. Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3. Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4. Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

1. Elaborar y revisar instrumentos jurídicos, convenios de colaboración internacional y acuerdos de cooperación, especialmente aquellos en materia de medio ambiente y desarrollo sostenible.

2. Dar seguimiento técnico-jurídico al cumplimiento de metas en programas de cooperación técnica con socios estratégicos internacionales.

3. Participar en negociaciones con contrapartes extranjeras multilaterales.

4. Coordinar y priorizar la agenda estratégica de los altos mandos de la Agencia, gestionando compromisos institucionales y optimizando la toma de decisiones.

5. Apoyar al área de protocolo de la Agencia en la organización de foros, reuniones de alto nivel y eventos institucionales.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El/La Asociado/a de asuntos jurídicos y enlace institucional formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID, en el área responsable de autorizar, coordinar y supervisar los programas, proyectos y acciones que realicen las unidades administrativas y órganos administrativos desconcentrados de la Secretaría de

Relaciones Exteriores, en temas de cooperación científica, educativa, tecnológica, deportiva, económica y empresarial, en ciudadanía y cultural, de asistencia humanitaria y de ayuda internacional, conforme a las políticas que dicte el Secretario y en concordancia con la Ley de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo y el Programa de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Académicos:

- Certificado de bachillerato es requisito.

- Estudios universitarios nivel licenciatura en Derecho, Ciencias Políticas, Relaciones Internacionales o carreras afines, se les dará debida consideración, pero no es requisito.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Relevante:

- Certificado de bachillerato es requisito.

- Estudios universitarios nivel licenciatura en Derecho, Ciencias Políticas, Relaciones Internacionales o carreras afines, se les dará debida consideración, pero no es requisito.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidato/as con estudios de bachillerato: al menos 7 años de experiencia en temas legales.

- Para candidatos/as con estudios finalizados de licenciatura: 4 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia legal en áreas de contratos, asuntos regulatorios o vinculación institucional.

- Excelentes habilidades de negociación y liderazgo.

- Experiencia en la elaboración y estructuración de instrumentos jurídicos, utilizando un lenguaje técnico preciso y claro.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Conocimientos generales de proyectos de cooperación en temas como medio ambiente o desarrollo sostenible.

- Experiencia en negociación de convenios o contratos.

- Experiencia organizando eventos de alto nivel.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Stagiaire en Opérationnalisation de l’économie circulaire
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

CONTEXTE DE L'ORGANISATION

Le PNUD travaille dans environ 170 pays et territoires, contribuant à l'éradication de la pauvreté et à la réduction des inégalités et de l'exclusion. Nous aidons les pays à développer des politiques, des compétences en matière de leadership, des capacités de partenariat, des capacités institutionnelles et à renforcer la résilience afin de maintenir les résultats du développement.

Le PNUD travaille au renforcement de nouveaux cadres pour le développement, la réduction des risques de catastrophe et le changement climatique. Nous soutenons les efforts des pays pour atteindre les nouveaux Objectifs de développement durable, qui guideront les priorités mondiales de développement jusqu'en 2030. Le principe clé de l'Agenda 2030, qui consiste à ne laisser personne de côté et à éradiquer les inégalités, est au cœur de toutes nos activités.

Le PNUD s'attache à aider les pays à élaborer et à partager des solutions dans deux domaines principaux :

- le Développement Durable, la résilience au climat et aux catastrophes

- La Gouvernance démocratique et la consolidation de la paix, Etat de Droits, Droits Humains

Dans toutes nos activités, nous encourageons la protection des droits de l'homme et l'autonomisation des femmes, des minorités et des personnes les plus pauvres et les plus vulnérables.

CONTEXTE DU STAGE :

Le Bureau Pays Côte d'Ivoire travaille sur le cycle programmatique 2026-2030 sur les questions de développement durable inclusif, croissance verte, l’innovation et sur la gouvernance. Le Bureau pays s'engage avec le gouvernement dans la mise en œuvre d'un important programme de soutien à la consolidation de la paix pour aider le pays à maintenir une paix durable. D'importantes initiatives sont mises en œuvre en partenariat avec le gouvernement pour renforcer la résilience face au climat et la création d’emplois verts.

Le stage a pour but de : fournir un cadre permettant à des étudiants de divers horizons académiques d'être affectés à des bureaux du PNUD, où leur expérience éducative peut être améliorée par des missions de travail pratiques ; les exposer à un environnement international ; les exposer au travail de l'Organisation dans le but d'approfondir leur connaissance et leur compréhension des objectifs, des principes et des activités du PNUD ; et fournir aux bureaux du PNUD l'assistance d'étudiants qualifiés spécialisés dans les domaines de l’ingénierie et du développement durable.

Le PNUD accompagne le Gouvernement ivoirien, à travers la Cellule Économie Circulaire de la Primature (CECP), dans la mise en œuvre de l’Initiative pour la Transition Circulaire (ITC). Cette initiative comprend notamment l’élaboration du Plan National de Transition vers l’Économie Circulaire (PNTEC) 2026–2035, actuellement en cours de finalisation, la cartographie nationale des acteurs de l’économie circulaire et sa plateforme en ligne, ainsi que la préparation d’un portefeuille de projets structurants, en cohérence avec le Plan National de Développement (PND) 2026–2030 et la Contribution Déterminée au niveau National (CDN 3.0).

Le présent stage s’inscrit dans l’appui du PNUD à l’ITC. Le/la stagiaire apportera un appui technique à la CECP et au PNUD pour l’approfondissement technique des projets du portefeuille ITC (valorisation des ressources secondaires urbaines, valorisation des résidus agricoles, construction circulaire, entre autres), l’exploitation des données de la cartographie nationale et le suivi des indicateurs environnementaux. Il/elle travaillera au quotidien avec l’équipe de la CECP, sous la supervision conjointe de l’Analyste de programme du PNUD en charge de l’ITC et d’un point focal désigné par la CECP.

Duties and Responsibilities

TÂCHES

Le/la stagiaire participera aux tâches et responsabilités suivantes :

- Appuyer l’analyse technique des filières prioritaires (plastiques et autres ressources secondaires urbaines, résidus agricoles, matériaux de construction, équipements électriques et électroniques) : gisements, flux de matières, technologies de collecte, de tri et de valorisation, contraintes techniques et réglementaires.

- Contribuer à l’approfondissement technique des notes conceptuelles et documents de projets du portefeuille ITC : description des solutions techniques, dimensionnement préliminaire des unités de valorisation, hypothèses de coûts indicatifs d’investissement et d’exploitation, en lien avec les acteurs sectoriels.

- Appuyer l’exploitation et la mise à jour des données de la cartographie nationale : contrôles de cohérence, validation auprès des répondants, analyses par filière et par territoire, identification des initiatives présentant un potentiel de mise à l’échelle.

- Contribuer à la définition et au calcul des indicateurs environnementaux des projets (tonnages valorisés ou détournés de la mise en décharge, émissions de gaz à effet de serre évitées, ressources économisées), sur la base de méthodologies reconnues.

- Préparer des fiches techniques et des notes de synthèse (technologies, retours d’expérience, bonnes pratiques régionales et internationales) à l’usage de la CECP et des partenaires.

- Participer aux visites de terrain auprès des acteurs de l’économie circulaire et dans les territoires démonstrateurs, et en rédiger les rapports.

- Appuyer la préparation technique des ateliers et réunions de travail avec les ministères sectoriels, le secteur privé et les partenaires : supports techniques, comptes rendus et suivi des actions.

- Rendre compte régulièrement de l’avancement des activités au superviseur PNUD et au point focal de la CECP, et accomplir toute autre tâche connexe confiée par les superviseurs.

Competencies

Compétences informatiques :

- Maîtrise d’Excel (traitement et analyse de données) et de la suite Microsoft Office ;

- La connaissance d’un logiciel SIG (QGIS ou ArcGIS) est un atout ;

- La connaissance d’outils d’analyse des flux de matières ou d’analyse du cycle de vie, ou d’un langage de programmation (Python, R), est un atout.

Compétences linguistiques

- La maîtrise du français est requise ; une bonne compréhension de l’anglais, notamment pour la documentation technique, est souhaitée.

- La connaissance d’autres langues des Nations Unies est un avantage.

Autres compétences et attitude :

- Rigueur technique et capacité à traduire des données techniques en recommandations opérationnelles ;

- Intérêt démontré pour l’économie circulaire, la gestion des ressources ou la transition énergétique ;

- Bonnes compétences analytiques pour rassembler, vérifier et consolider des données ;

- Intérêt et motivation pour travailler dans une organisation internationale et en appui à une institution nationale ;

- Personne prenant des initiatives, avec un état d'esprit orienté vers les résultats ;

- Communique efficacement lorsqu'elle travaille en équipe et de manière indépendante ;

- Bonne capacité à organiser et à structurer diverses tâches et responsabilités ;

- Fait preuve de sensibilité et d'adaptabilité en matière de culture, de sexe, de religion, de race, de nationalité et d'âge ;

- Répond positivement aux commentaires et aux points de vue divergents ;

- Aborde constamment le travail avec une énergie et une attitude positive et constructive.

Required Skills and Experience

EXIGENCES ET QUALIFICATIONS

Education :

Les candidats doivent répondre à l'une des exigences suivantes en matière d'éducation :

- Être inscrit·e dans un programme de master (Bac+5) ou de niveau supérieur ; ou

- Être diplômé·e depuis moins d’un an d’un master (Bac+5) ou d’études équivalentes.

Domaine d'étude : Gestion de l’environnement, gestion des procédés, génie civil, génie énergétique, génie rural ou agronomique, sciences de l’environnement ou domaine connexe.

CONDITIONS DE STAGE

- Le stage n’est pas rémunéré par le PNUD ; les frais de subsistance et toutes les dépenses liées au stage sont pris en charge par l’entité parrainant le/la stagiaire.

- Toutes autres dépenses liées au stage sont à la charge du stagiaire ou de l'entité qui le parraine ;

- Le PNUD n'accepte aucune responsabilité pour les coûts résultant d'accidents et/ou de maladies ou de décès survenus pendant le stage ;

- Les stagiaires sont responsables de l'obtention des visas nécessaires et de l'organisation du voyage vers et depuis le lieu d'affectation où le stage sera effectué ;

- Les stagiaires ne sont pas éligibles pour postuler ou être nommés à un poste au PNUD pendant la période de stage ;

- Les stagiaires doivent fournir la preuve de leur inscription à un régime d'assurance maladie ;

- Les stagiaires ne sont pas des membres du personnel et ne peuvent pas représenter le PNUD à titre officiel ;

- Les stagiaires sont censés travailler à temps plein, mais une certaine flexibilité est autorisée pour les programmes d'éducation ;

- Les stagiaires doivent obtenir un financement pour leur subsistance et prendre leurs propres dispositions pour le stage, le voyage, le VISA, le logement, etc.

Disclaimer

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

jobs.title: Especialista en Vinculación y Estrategia Institucional de Proyectos de Cooperación

Descripción de Proyecto:

Vigente desde el año 2013, la historia del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) está ligada al establecimiento del Sistema Mexicano de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, contribuyendo a la implementación del Objetivo de Desarrollo Sostenible 17 “Revitalizar la alianza mundial para el Desarrollo Sostenible”, con el propósito de apoyar los esfuerzos de la AMEXCID para transitar hacia un modelo eficaz, que refleje las particularidades de un Cooperante Dual, oferente y receptor de cooperación en sus diversas modalidades, y País de Renta Media Alta, de acuerdo con sus propias prioridades y visión, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 para el Desarrollo Sostenible.

En su Tercera Etapa (2019-2025), el Programa de Cooperación promueve que la Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (CID) sea un instrumento para alcanzar las prioridades de desarrollo incluidas en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2019-2024, alineado particularmente al compromiso de “Conducir la política exterior en apego a los principios constitucionales y articulada con las prioridades de la política interna”, siendo la CID uno de los siete principios de la política exterior de México.

Específicamente, se apoyarán los esfuerzos que realiza la AMEXCID para consolidarse institucionalmente, encaminados a desarrollar sus capacidades nacionales, fortalecer su política de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta, así como establecer alianzas estratégicas con otros actores relevantes (como el sector privado, la academia y las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, otras agencias de cooperación multilaterales y bilaterales presentes en México que realizan esfuerzos de naturaleza complementaria), por medio de esquemas innovadores de cooperación al desarrollo. Además, se apoyará la contribución de la Agencia a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Lo anterior está orientado a potenciar los 6 ejes de acción de la AMEXCID (diplomacia deportiva; diplomacia en ciudadanía, diplomacia científica y tecnológica; diplomacia económica empresarial; diplomacia educativa; y diplomacia humanitaria), su nueva estructura (coordinación de la política de cooperación internacional; análisis y evaluación de proyectos; implementación de proyectos), así como las prioridades de México como país receptor y país oferente de CID.

El objetivo general del Programa de Cooperación AMEXCID-PNUD (PROCAP) es la consolidación institucional de la AMEXCID para fortalecer la Cooperación Sur-Sur en México, a través de cuatro resultados:

1.Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales para la gestión de la CID;

2.Fortalecimiento de la política mexicana de CID, en sus modalidades de recepción y oferta;

3.Promoción de alianzas estratégicas para el desarrollo;

4.Apoyo a la implementación del Plan de Desarrollo Integral.

Alcance de Trabajo:

- Coordinar la estrategia global de comunicación institucional y diplomacia pública de la Agencia para visibilizar sus programas de cooperación y posicionar la imagen de México a nivel internacional.

- Liderar protocolos de contención, análisis de riesgo y elaboración de mensajes o posicionamientos institucionales ante situaciones sensibles o de crisis que impacten la reputación de la Agencia o la política exterior.

- Coordinar las relaciones públicas de la Agencia con Embajadas, organismos internacionales, sector privado, organizaciones de la sociedad civil y dependencias del Gobierno Federal, en el marco de la Agenda 2030 y proyectos de desarrollo.

- Conducir la elaboración de síntesis ejecutivas, líneas de discurso, perfiles para entrevistas, boletines y notas de posicionamiento estratégico para la Dirección Ejecutiva y autoridades de alto nivel.

- Supervisar el análisis cualitativo y cuantitativo de bases de datos sobre cobertura mediática internacional y tendencias del entorno político-económico global, para apoyar la toma de decisiones estratégicas de los altos mandos de la Agencia.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El/la Especialista en Vinculación y Estrategia Institucional de Proyectos de Cooperación formará parte de la estructura operativa de la Dirección Ejecutiva de la AMEXCID o de la dirección general en la que se asigne, responsable de autorizar, coordinar y supervisar los programas, proyectos y acciones que realicen las unidades administrativas y órganos administrativos desconcentrados de la Secretaría de Relaciones Exteriores, en temas de cooperación científica, educativa, tecnológica, deportiva, económica y empresarial, en ciudadanía y cultural, de asistencia humanitaria y de ayuda internacional, conforme a las políticas que dicte el Secretario y en concordancia con la Ley de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo, el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo y el Programa de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo.

Competencias Esenciales:

Logro de Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadoramente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre de manera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisistos Académicos:

- Título de Licenciatura en Administración Pública, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Políticas, Economía o carrera afines, es requisito.

- Maestría en los temas antes mencionados no es requisito, pero se le dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con título de Licenciatura: 7 años de experiencia en cargos de alta responsabilidad dentro de la administración pública.

- Para candidatos/as con Maestría: 5 años de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia liderando equipos de trabajo multidisciplinarios en la Administración Pública.

- Experiencia en relaciones públicas interinstitucionales, manejo de crisis, diplomacia corporativa y diseño de estrategias de comunicación institucional o difusión de proyectos.

- Experiencia en análisis cuantitativo/cualitativo de datos y gestión de proyectos bajo metodologías orientadas al cumplimiento de KPIs y/o metas de negocio.

Habilidades Deseadas:

- Experiencia en la elaboración de líneas de discurso, fichas técnicas, posicionamientos oficiales, minutas, insumos para entrevistas y síntesis informativas.

- Experiencia en el diseño de campañas de comunicación institucional o difusión de herramientas financieras/tecnológicas del sector público.

- Experiencia en el diseño de protocolos de alerta temprana, análisis de escenarios y ejecución de planes de continuidad operativa bajo normativas internacionales

Idioma Requerido:

- Inglés nivel intermedio.

Al ser una contratación nacional al aplicante debe ser ciudadana/o mexicana/o en pleno ejercicio de sus derechos, o extranjera/o, cuya condición migratoria permita la función a desarrollar

jobs.title: Technical Analyst (HomeBased) (Open to All applicants )
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work is carried out through a network of advisors and specialists located at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, to ensure that local knowledge and context specific expertise is linked to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP provides its policy advisory and programme support functions through the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains, in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP’s Strategic Plan.

UNDP's 2026-2029 Strategic Plan highlights our continued commitment to eradicating poverty, accompanying countries in their pathways towards the SDGs and working towards the Paris Agreement. Built around four core objectives—prosperity for all, effective governance, crisis resilience, and a healthy planet—the plan is powered by three accelerators: digital and AI transformation, gender equality, and sustainable finance. As part of the Global Policy Network in the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support, UNDP's Planet Hub promotes and scales up integrated whole-of-governance approaches and nature-based solutions that reduce poverty and inequalities, strengthen livelihoods and inclusive growth, mitigate conflict, forced migration and displacement, and promote more resilient governance systems that advance linked peace and security agendas.

The Planet Hub drives UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together, helping over 150 countries to achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships, funding sources, and deep expertise at global and regional level, the Planet Hub helps countries advance their environmental and economic goals across eight critical thematic areas: Climate and Nature Policy, Ecosystems and Biodiversity, Forests, Land Use and Food Systems, Cooling, Circularity and Pollution Prevention, Finance for Planet, Local Action and Just Transition, Climate Adaptation and Resilient Societies, and Decarbonization and Sustainable Energy.

As the largest single operational and financial UN player in the field of environmental sustainability, UNDP is widely recognized as a global leader in supporting governments to sharpen policy, access finance and develop capacity for the management of biodiversity and ecosystems for sustainable development and poverty eradication. UNDP’s work on nature has as an overall strategic objective to maintain and enhance the goods and services provided by biodiversity and ecosystems in order to secure livelihoods, food, water and health, enhance resilience, conserve threatened species and their habitats, and increase carbon storage and sequestration.

UNDP is expanding its efforts to engage private sector in biodiversity financing, contributing to the overall objective of redirecting global finance flows from nature negative to nature positive, as a prerequisite system change for achieving the post-2020 Global Biodiversity Programme and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among the instruments in biodiversity finance, emerging attention is being dedicated to biodiversity credits. “Biodiversity credits, or ‘biocredits’ (i.e., nature credits, biodiversity tokens and alike), are emerging as a quantifiable unit of biodiversity, supported by a scientific methodology, that can incentivise nature conservation and restoration to benefit marginalised groups living with nature.

The Biodiversity Credit Alliance (BCA) is a multi-stakeholder initiative aiming to provide clarity and guidance on the development of a credible and scalable biodiversity credit market. The BCA brings together methodology developers, private sector stakeholders, NGOs, and academia to advance the concept of biodiversity credits, ensuring they promote nature-positive outcomes while benefiting Indigenous Peoples and local communities. The BCA is structured around a Task Force and a Forum, with working groups dedicated to key technical areas such as biodiversity credit definitions, peer-review mechanisms, demand-side engagement, metrics, digital standards, and marine biodiversity credits. To date, the BCA Task Force brings together 20 leading biodiversity credit methodology developers, including companies, academia and NGOs, which work to generate scientific standards for biodiversity credits in different contexts and ecosystems. In addition, the BCA Forum facilitates the dissemination of knowledge to over 500 member organizations interested in contributing to and learning about the biodiversity credit market. The BCA Secretariat is funded and facilitated by UNDP, UNEP FI, SIDA, GIZ and EC.

This position will play a supportive role in advancing technical discussions, facilitating working groups, and ensuring high-quality outputs that contribute to the integrity and credibility of the emerging biodiversity credit market.

The Technical Analyst will operate as a part of the BCA Secretariat, ensuring that BCA’s technical working groups are well coordinated to deliver the technical outputs in a timely and consultative manner.

Scope of Work

The Technical Analyst will undertake the following responsibilities:

Conduct Market Knowledge & Technical Analysis

- Maintain and apply strong understanding of biodiversity credit markets, key actors, definitions, and emerging practices

- Monitor and synthesize developments in biodiversity finance, carbon markets, and related standards

- Conduct research and analysis on market dynamics, including demand, supply, pricing, and trends

Contribute to the Market Integrity, Frameworks & Demand Enablement

- Support screening of biodiversity credit schemes against BCA’s High-Level Principles (HLPs) using the Assessment Framework

- Distill lessons from assessments and contribute to continuous refinement of the HLPs and Assessment Framework

- Support development of technical guidance and tools, including:

- A digital tool for demand integrity

- A claims catalogue and code of practice for buyers

- Guidance on claims, governance mechanisms, and market architecture

- Contribute to workstreams aimed at enabling and strengthening demand for high‑integrity biodiversity credits

Support Establishments of the Working Groups & Knowledge Products

- Support establishment and coordination of working groups and interest groups

- Facilitate co-leads in defining scopes, priorities, and deliverables

- Identify and engage relevant experts and community members

- Develop and manage workplans with clear timelines and outputs

- Organize and facilitate consultative meetings, manage divergent views, and build consensus

- Analyze inputs and produce issue papers and technical reports

- Coordinate consultations, finalize publications, and support dissemination through briefs, webinars, and events, in line with BCA protocols

Facilitate Country Support & Capacity Building

- Provide technical inputs to country readiness assessments, feasibility studies, and pilot design

- Support delivery of training, workshops, and knowledge exchange

- Synthesize country-level insights to inform BCA’s global guidance and market development work

Support the development of Nature Market Accelerator (NMA)

- Apply and refine integrity assessment tools, including the HLPs Assessment Matrix, to ensure consistent evaluation of all NMA pilot projects.

- Provide independent integrity oversight across all phases of the initiative, ensuring all activities uphold the BCA High Level Principles (HLPs).

- Identify crosscutting integrity risks related to safeguards, governance, benefit sharing, and MRV, and provide recommendations.

- Ensure that insights from the pilots inform ongoing international development of biodiversity credit methodologies and policy dialogue.

Ensure Partnerships, Outreach & Technical Collaboration

- Support technical collaboration with partner institutions and initiatives

- Ensure alignment with BCA processes, protocols, and High-Level Principles

- Contribute to outreach and advocacy to promote adoption of high-integrity biodiversity credits across public and private sectors

- Support organization of targeted stakeholder events and workshops

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangements

- The incumbent will work from home base.

- The incumbent will work in the BCA Secretariat, under the overall guidance of the Senior Nature Economist as the Lead of the Nature Investments Team and will report directly to the BCA Global Coordinator. The role involves engagement with different stakeholders within the BCA Governance Structures including Indigenous Peoples and local communities and external partners.

- The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment.

- The incumbent will be responsible for providing her/his own working station (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, assignment specific software, etc.) and must have access to a reliable internet connection.

- Given the global consultations to be undertaken during this assignment, the incumbent is expected to be reasonably flexible with his/her availability for such consultations, taking into consideration different time zones.

Competencies Core

- Achieve Results: Level 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: Level 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: Level 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: Level 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: Level 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: Level 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: Level 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Development- Collective Intelligence

- Design Ability to bring together diverse groups of people, data, information, ideas, and technology to solve problems and design solutions or services.

- Knowledge and understanding of Collective Intelligence Design principles, methodology and practices.

Business Development- Knowledge Generation

- Ability to research information and turn it into useful knowledge, relevant context, or responsive to a stated need.

- Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches.

- Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management-Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Data-Data Analysis

- Ability to extract, analyze and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making.

Partnership Management-Relationship Management

- Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful IPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Advanced university degree (master's degree or equivalent) in Environmental Science/Management or related field is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Applicants with a master's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of 2 years working experience with biodiversity credits, nature financing, policy development and research.

Desired skills

- Experience of the UN and/or UNDP’s rules, policies, and procedures

- Experience facilitating public and bilateral consultations on topics such as carbon and/or biodiversity credits

- Experience providing technical guidance and/ or capacity building to governments, Indigenous Peoples and local communities, and/or UN Country Offices on topics related to biodiversity credits

- Experience presenting at high-level international events and/or delivering workshops related to nature finance topics such as the biodiversity credit market

- Experience reviewing and/or applying the policy guidelines related to the biodiversity credit market such as the “High Level Principles to Guide the Biodiversity Credit Market”.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in the English is required.

- Working knowledge of another UN language is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Climate Transparency Global Support Programme [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policies and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The newly established UNDP Planet Hub will drive UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized. By 2030, the Hub seeks to help countries achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships and funding sources, the Planet Hub combines thought leadership, technical expertise, and strategic collaboration to help countries advance their environmental and economic goals.

The Planet Hub will build on UNDP’s existing portfolio of over USD 5 billion in over 140 countries, as well as on key offers across UNDP. The Planet Hub’s theory of change rests on five mutually reinforcing service lines that together enable systemic transformation:

- Intergovernmental and UN System Coherence and Support

- National Policies, Strategies, and Planning

- Innovative and Integrated Solutions

- Scaled-up Finance

- Insights, Modeling, and Data

The Planet Hub will be made up of eight interconnected pillars, covering strategic areas of work to deliver its core objective, as well as a set of integrated functions and support that cut across pillars and help ensure cohesive offers and delivery of the Planet Hub. One critical component of the Planet Hub is the portfolio of support to countries on Climate and Nature Policy. The Climate and Nature Policy Pillar provide strategic leadership on integrated climate and nature policy development, implementation, and advocacy, supporting countries to address interconnected environmental challenges while advancing sustainable development objectives. The Pillar brings together expertise on climate policy, biodiversity policy, environmental governance, integrated planning frameworks, Multilateral Environmental Agreements, and science-policy interfaces. Working across all Planet Hub pillars and in close collaboration with governments, UN entities, international organizations, research institutions, and development partners, the Pillar promotes policy coherence, strengthens implementation of global environmental commitments, and supports countries in developing integrated approaches to climate action, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem resilience, and sustainable development.

Climate Transparency and implementation of Paris Agreement’s Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) are paramount to the vision of the Policies pillar, under the Planet Hub. UNDP has extensive experience supporting developing countries to meet international climate reporting requirements and works closely with UNFCCC, UNEP, GEF and other partners in this area.

The Climate Transparency - Global Support Programme Phase III (GSP III) will be jointly implemented by UNDP and United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) (through UNEP Copenhagen Climate Centre

CCC), with project management and coordination responsibilities shared between UNDP and UNEP. Effective delivery therefore requires close day-to-day collaboration between the UNDP and UNEP teams, as well as coordinated engagement with the project's governance bodies, regional networks and technical partners.

It is in this context that UNDP is recruiting a Project Manager -Climate Transparency Global Support Programme (GSP) who will manage the daily delivery of the UNDP-led activities in the GSP III, support the technical quality of activities and outputs, and act as UNDP's focal point in the Joint Project Management Unit, working closely with UNEP-CCC to ensure coherent implementation.

Purpostion Purpose

Under the direct supervision and strategic guidance of the Chief Technical Lead, Climate Transparency, and in close collaboration with the UNEP-CCC, the GSP, the Project Manager will manage the delivery of UNDP-led activities under GSP III; support the technical quality, methodological consistency and gender-responsiveness of its outputs; coordinate work planning, budgeting, procurement, monitoring and reporting, facilitate collaboration between UNDP and UNEP teams; supervise the Climate Transparency Programme Analyst,-Administrative and Financial support personnel and contracted consultants, and coordinate the day-to-day work of the stream's technical personnel on delivery matters; and serve as UNDP's focal point in the JPMU (Joint Project Management Unit) on execution matters, and coordinate with the counterpart focal point in the UNEP-CCC stream to ensure a consistent approach across agencies; provide secretariat support to the Project Steering Committee (PSC) on behalf of UNDP, preparing agendas, technical inputs, minutes and decision-support materials, under the direction of the Chief Technical Lead.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1- Coordinate planning, implementation and administration of UNDP-led activities in the GSP III, in line with Project Steering Committee (PSC) decisions and Joint Programme Management Unit (JPMU)-endorsed workplans:

- Coordinate annual and multi-year workplans, budgets and procurement plans

- Manage day-to-day implementation, delivery tracking and expenditure monitoring in line with UNDP rules and regulations and GEF requirements

- Prepare technical specifications for procurement, and manage contracts, consultants and service providers

- Organize and follow up planning and coordination meetings across all project outputs

- Coordinate with UNDP Country Offices and Regional Bureaux on delivery arrangements for country-level activities under GSP III, including mission planning, in-country support and follow-up

- Ensure timely follow-up to Project Steering Committee and JPMU decisions across all workstreams and personnel

- Maintain effective day-to-day coordination with UNEP-CCC colleagues to promote coherent implementation across the jointly implemented programme.

2- Advice and support technical guidance and ensure methodological consistency

- Support the consistent application of the methodologies, guidance, templates and procedures endorsed by the Chief Technical Lead across project outputs and regional networks

- Coordinate the review of deliverables and prepare them for clearance by the Chief Technical Lead prior to submission to the JPMU or the PSC, ensuring adherence to ETF requirements and IPCC good practice guidance

- Ensure harmonization of methodologies and procedures across regional networks so that results are comparable

- Verify that deliverables covering GHG inventories, NDC tracking, adaptation, and support needed and received follow the technical procedures and templates agreed for the project, and flag deviations to the Chief Technical Lead

- Ensure inclusiveness and gender-responsiveness are reflected in deliverables, in line with the project's Gender Action Plan and Stakeholder Engagement Plan

- Identify technical issues requiring escalation to the Chief Technical Lead or other designated technical experts.

3. Coordinate UNDP's engagement in the programmer’s 's joint governance and coordination arrangements

- Serve as UNDP's focal point in the JPMU and coordinate with the UNEP-CCC counterpart to ensure a unified approach across both agencies

- Provide secretariat support to the Project Steering Committee on behalf of UNDP, preparing agendas, technical inputs, minutes and decision-support materials under the direction of the Chief Technical Lead

- Prepare and consolidate UNDP inputs to PSC meetings, including briefing notes, technical analyses and progress summaries

- Coordinate day-to-day operational liaison with the IPCC TFI TSU/IGES and other executing partners on delivery, deliverables and scheduling, in coordination with the strategic partnerships led by the Chief Technical Lead

- Contribute technical inputs and materials to UNDP's participation in COP and SB sessions and the Global Transparency Forum and participate as a member of UNDP delegations as required.

- Maintain effective communication between the UNDP and UNEP teams and support resolution of implementation and coordination issues.

4. Manage monitoring, evaluation, and reporting

• Coordinate and consolidate UNDP inputs to Programme/Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), half-yearly progress reports, expenditure and co-financing reports, audit related processes and the final project report, in collaboration with UNEP-CCC

• Prepare and maintain UNDP’s annual planning, risk management and contingency plan in collaboration with the Chief Technical Lead

• Maintain the project risk log and alert the Chief Technical Lead to material risks requiring corrective action, and prepare risk information for the JPMU and the PSC

• Support coordination of the mid-term review and the terminal evaluation, and follow up on management responses and recommendations

• Ensure monitoring products provide accurate and verifiable evidence for PSC and JPMU decision-making

• Track implementation of agreed corrective actions and recommendations.

5. Coordinate the programme team and facilitate knowledge, innovation and learning

- Coordinate the work of personnel, consultants and service providers assigned to UNDP's GSP III responsibilities, in accordance with approved reporting and supervisory arrangements

- Support recruitment, onboarding and performance management of UNDP personnel and consultants as applicable

- Foster a collaborative, high-performing and inclusive working culture across globally distributed teams

- Coordinate the exchange of country-level experience, lessons and knowledge products between UNDP's wider GEF Enabling Activities and CBIT portfolio and GSP III, so that national projects and global support reinforce each other and duplication is avoided

- Facilitate the capture and sharing of lessons learned and good practices across regional networks and communities of practice

- Promote innovation and continuous improvement in the project’s ways of working

- Share GSP III tools, knowledge products and lessons with relevant Planet Hub teams, Country Offices and communities of practice, supporting the integration of transparency work led by the Chief Technical Lead

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent supervises the Programme Analysts assigned to the GSP III, as well as consultants and service providers contracted under the stream. Expected number of direct reports: 2. The incumbent additionally coordinates the day-to-day work of the Regional Network Coordinators and other technical personnel in relation to workplan delivery, deadlines and reporting; line supervision and performance management of these personnel rests with the Chief Technical Lead, Climate Transparency.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

2030 Agenda - Planet Climate - Climate Change Adaptation: Climate Information and Early Warning Systems (CI & EWS)

2030 Agenda: Planet - Climate: Climate Strategies and Policy: NDC enhancement

Business Management - Portfolio Management : Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with

its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on

investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Business Management - Project Management : Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Business Management - Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking : Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management - Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of themanagement and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming.

Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Natural Sciences, Environmental Management, International Development, Economics, Public Administration, or a closely related field. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- At least 3 years of proven working experience in climate transparency, MRV, GHG inventories, NDC tracking, reporting under the Paris Agreement or related areas, with a specific focus on developing countries, are required.

- At least 3 years of working experience managing or coordinating multi-country, regional or international projects, including work planning, budgeting, procurement and reporting, is required.

- Demonstrated knowledge of UNFCCC processes and the Paris Agreement, particularly the Enhanced Transparency Framework, is required.

- Membership of the UNFCCC roster of experts and/or UNFCCC certifications related to MRV, BTR, etc., are desirable.
